title: Thumbs up Indigo

Recently, I booked an international ticket with Indigo for my journey from India to Australia for the first time. Indigo offered a route from Chennai to Singapore on flight 6E 1025, followed by a connection to Sydney with its partner Qantas on flight 6E 4674 (operated by Finnair). I was thoroughly impressed with both Indigo and Qantas. Indigo, as the marketing partner, facilitated a seamless check-in process at Chennai airport, where my luggage was checked through to Sydney, and I received both boarding passes at that time. The Indigo flight 6E 1025 was a new A320, just 0.3 years old, with attentive crew members and a thoughtful food pack. Both departure and arrival were punctual. The Qantas flight, operated by Finnair, also departed on time, providing good service. Overall, the experience was excellent and offered great value for money, earning my commendation for Indigo.

title: Save your money and go with another carrier
text:
I made a booking for a flight from New Delhi to Sydney for the 31st of December 2024. And I must say the experience was the worst I have ever had.

1. I paid for xl seats but apartments due to airline configuration changes the seat was double booked. So after a lot of arguments in the flight with another passenger who also happened to pay for it (but their boarding pass did not have the XL seats assigned), they sat in the XL seats. The airline crew were of no help here as the flight was already delayed and they were only interested in taking off as soon as possible. It was a complete circus. Luckily since then I have been provided my refund for the XL seats.

2. My ticket also had a snack bag included in the fee, but I was not provided with anything during the indigo leg of the journey. They just said they will work to make sure it won't happen again. Unfortunately this has happened to other people in the past. Keep in mind this is an internation flight from New Delhi to Singapore. So theoretically speaking, meals should be included anyway (at least a light snack).

3. The second leg of my journey was from Singapore to Sydney via Qantas. The Qantas leg of my journey was in business class, however I was involuntarily downgraded to budget economy class as the flight was full. Again I brought this to the attention of the ground staff in Singapore, but they said the flight was full and my assigned seat could not be changed. I called Qantas and they confirmed this should not have happened but I had to contact Indigo for compensation as I booked my ticket through the Indigo website. Indigo keep saying the fault lies with Qantas and i should contact them. However, Qantas keep insisting a refund is in order but they can't do that because i didn't make the booking through them which is understandable.

I put the full blame of this on Indigo. Qantas said Indigo sould reach out to liase with them for this but i doubt they did that. They'd lose money after all. After several emails, I was offered Rs 500 worth of travel voucher for my downgrade from business to budget economy.🤣 I do not plan to fly with them again, so I told them to keep their grand compensation as i wouldn't know how to spend this much money. What a pathetic excuse for a company which offers international flights. I would personally ban them from even flying local. 

A business class vs economy fare difference is not Rs500. No airline in the world wil upgrade a passanger from budget economy to busoness for Rs 500. Till date I have given them about $20,000 worth of business. However after this i will be taking my business elsewhere.

title: Indigo is NOT FIT for International Travel
text:
Indigo is a BIG NO NO!!! if you're planning to travel via Indigo or their partner airlines for International travel. Indigo has a very hands-off approach when it comes to resolving issues, cancellations etc. Indigo will pressure you to cancel bookings on your own and re-issue tickets as per the new schedules and/or pricing. This is because it will cost you more and make them more money. Anything you propose in complicated scenarios is not an option on the table. It will go Indigo's way or nowhere. Customer service or basic due diligence is nowhere on the airline's agenda/priorities. I am not surprised why Indigo has been recently rated one of the worst airlines to fly with. Unfortunately for me, I had already booked my tickets with Indigo before the survey results came out, so I couldn't really do much with my travel plans. Yes, it got ruined right at the baggage counter... 

Indigo's baggage policy is a scam. DO NOT fall for the amazing 30 to 46 kg baggage allowance (per ticket). They have sneaky baggage terms which allows you to only take 23 kg per suitcase (obviously this is not mentioned upfront or anywhere in the ticket/itinerary issued). The moment you go above the 23 kg per baggage allowance, there is a significant additional charge for every bag which weighs more than the 23 kg threshold. So, that's the first time you'll be ripped off right at the baggage counter. You have to pay the additional charges even if the total baggage weight is below the total weight allowance or you're not boarding... 

Further, Indigo doesn't offer any food even within the International flights. You may choose to pre-order (obviously pay separately) for their taste-less sandwiches which if you trust me be really better off without them. You won't even be offered plain water unless you specifically asked so. Basically, you have to keep asking for everything and wait and wait and wait before something happens or it may not happen at all...

I was deeply disappointed with their on-call customer service operators who seemed super naive and ignorant. The staff is respectful only until you continue to agree with their suggestions. I asked to speak to one of the staff's supervisor as my concerns were not being addressed. The call operator bluntly told me that the call won't be transferred to his supervisor as he has already advised what he had to. 

If the on-call operators are not able to resolve your issues during the call. They'll ask you to expect a phone call within 2 hours from the relevant team. This didn't happen for me. So again, I had to ring them chasing up on my request with no resolutions provided. It's a Nightmare!!!

I wish I could go back in time and book my flights with a different airline. But unfortunately, I can't. But You!, Yes You, the one one reading this feedback, still have time. Please look for an alternative and save yourself from an exaggerated level of hassle and stress. Spend you hard earned money wisely and say a BIG NO to Indigo even if they're flying you for free as it may be another one of their SCAMS to rip you off...

Peace!

 The first cancellation BON-NAG meaning we will spend a happy  9 hours stuck in bombay airport waiting for their next flight.  They refused to organise us access to a lounge in Bombay airport domestic terminal (I'm travelling with my elderly mother) to help improve the impact of their changes.

I've tried to lodge a formal complaint and they ignored that demand too.  Note India does not have the same consumer protections we enjoy in the West.

So by contrast, Singapore Airlines have been incredibly helpful and said if Indigo provide the standard Flight Disruption Notice to me and I submit that to them they may well be able waive the cancellation fees as they have time to resell the tickets.  

Indigo, after 2 weeks of repeated daily emails requesting this document, are just ignoring me and keep sending automated or holding emails.  It would cost them noting to send me this document and they won't even do that.  

I write this as a warning to all international tourists that Indigo will likely cancel flight times in the middle of the day very close to departure date (most airlines firm up their schedules 6 months in advance!). title: Missing luggage (arrived 30 hours later), senior citizen parents.
text:
I am writing to express my deep dissatisfaction with the experience my parents had while traveling with your airline on January 3, 2025. They traveled from Gondia to Hyderabad (Flight 6E-7697), as my mother needed to consult with a spine specialist due to a bulging disc issue that causes her severe back and shoulder pain.

As senior citizens, we specifically chose Indigo because of the trust and satisfaction we have with your services. However, the experience my parents had was not only disappointing but also led to significant financial and emotional distress.

Half way through their flight, I receive a whatsapp message from Indigo stating their checked-in baggage was not connected in their flight and they need to see a Indigo team member when they arrive. I called them on their arrival and asked them to see a Indigo team member to see how many bags have not arrived and what to do next (Note: I booked their flight).
Turns out that 1 out of their 2 bags didn't arrive and that was my Mum's bag which had all her essentials including her medicines, clothes, charger toiletries as well as her MRI reports that the doctor would need to see the other day. 

The travel desk promised that the bag would be delivered to their hotel by 11 PM that night, but it never arrived. After numerous follow-ups, they were eventually told that the bag would arrive at 2 PM, then 7 PM, and finally, it was delivered at 10 PM on January 4th—over 30 hours after their arrival in Hyderabad.

During this period, my parents had to purchase new essentials for my mother and even redo three MRI scans at additional cost—none of which should have been necessary had the luggage arrived on time. title: Delayed departures, overwhelmed and disorganized ground staff, terrible food, cockroaches in the cabin
text:
I took the Prague - Delhi - Nagpur and the Mumbai - Prague flight during December 2024 via the Turkish Indigo codeshare flight transiting from Istanbul.
I was traveling with my wife and my four year  old kid.
I did end up paying upwards of €2000 for this journey, which is comparable to any other international airlines and the only reason I chose Indigo was a domestic connection from Delhi to Nagpur to leverage the baggage limit.

I’ve been doing this route for almost 10 years now, and I would say that this experience has been the biggest nightmare in my life.

Just to start it off I missed my last flights due to Indigo’s incompetence in both my journeys.

Onboarding- 

The biggest issue I see is on the international routes. They have acquired Turkish airlines widebody planes and reconfigured it to add hundred plus more seats.
Well, that looks smart, but there is no provision made to accommodate those hundred for organized on boarding and deboarding from the planes. What you left with is chaos while boarding the aircraft. This meant that none of our flights took off at the time described and were late all the time. 

Seat allocation - 

Indigo has this unique offering that doesn’t allow you to check in if you are on code share flights and it always assigns  seats at different locations in the aircraft, even if you are traveling as a family.
What that meant was during the boarding process the first hour goes with people negotiating with others to exchange seats.

Food -
For a low cost airlines, no one expects to have a lavish spread for the food. But the quality was just poor and missed basic standards. I was served Indian Parathas that had became dry and hardened as it was exposed to air, which I couldn’t even chew and I had to return half of it back.
It took them three hours in my first flight from Istanbul to Delhi to start serving the food, which is nonsense for a flight time of six hours.

Ground staff-
The ground staff at Delhi International Airport was just overwhelmed with the morning traffic. While there was no shortage of staff, it just felt that none of them knew what needed to be done.
When I missed my connecting flight from Delhi to Nagpur due to late arrival of package, I had to jostles for almost 2 hours in a ticket window with fellow 50-70 passengers to get a reschedule done of a late night flight that extended my layover by 14 hours. I was not offered any hotel or meal compensation. I had to book a hotel on my expense and sleep there for the entire day to come back and take the late night flight.
On the flight back, I missed my connection from Istanbul to Prague due to delayed departure from Mumbai. Again, I had to jostle for three hours on Istanbul airport to get a rescheduled done on the next flight which extended my layover by five hours.

Overall experience-

Also, it’s worthwhile to call that I have flown Indigo several times on domestic connections in India and they have been much better compared to any European low-cost airlines. Also the cabin crew while overwhelmed was always nice and helpful.
I just feel that they don’t have the mindset to run international routes and no wonder they have been ranked as the worst airlines across the world. I feel ashamed that an Indian carrier is providing such a low quality service.

The discussed I had of the overall experience could be summarized with a small incident of seeing couple of cockroaches roaming in the cabin.

I would never ever fly Indigo on an international route and would caution everyone else to stay away from Indigo, even if it means that you have to shell out some more money to book a better carrier.

And advice for Indigo please just stop insulting the passengers and stop your international operations.

title: Don’t fly with IndiGo
text:
On November 6, our IndiGo flight (6E 2015) from Varanasi to Delhi was scheduled to depart at 6:40 a.m. I am well aware that certain elements, like fog, can result in flight delays over which airline companies may have little control. On that particular day, however, visibility was already at one mile at 8:30 am (according to the report). Even though the fog had cleared by 8:30 am, the flight did not depart until 11 am. 

We missed our 1:40 pm IndiGo flight from Delhi to Kathmandu. Our flight had to be rescheduled for the following day. Before November 6, Varanasi has been plagued by fog problems for a few days. I wasn't told that this might be an issue so I could make plans ahead of time. 

We were given the impression by the IndiGo employees that we were to blame for missing our flight to Kathmandu. I was not offered to rebooked my flight by the staff. Since there were no other planes departing from New Delhi to Kathmandu, I took that choice. That day, the IndiGo employees did nothing to assist me. Additionally, IndiGo did not compensate us for the hotel expenses we incurred during our overnight stay in Delhi.

Refunds, credits, or rebooking, in my opinion, are not appropriate ways to compensate for the hardships that passengers endure in such circumstances. These are attempts to recover unpaid services. My trip to Kathmandu was cut short by one day. That cannot be replaced by money. I also had to pay for two hotel rooms that day, one in Kathmandu and one in Delhi. 

Passengers from Air India shared the gate designated for 6E 2015 in Varanasi. It was packed at the gate. Air India employees were present to assist and inform their passengers. After the goodies were given out, no IndiGo employees were in sight. Even though the Air India flight was supposed to depart later than 6E 2015, it actually left much earlier.

The paging system was not used to announce the gate change overhead. Some passengers in the front were informed by IndiGo staff, while many seated in the back were unable to hear the announcement. 

That day, the flight's schedule was altered numerous times - from 6:30 am to 6:45 to 9:10 to 10:15 to 11:07 am. However, IndiGo's ground crew failed to get passengers ready in advance for a seamless boarding experience. No extra employees were available to assist with boarding. There was no announcement of zones. First come, first served was the rule. More delays in getting the passengers on board resulted from this procedure.

We were scheduled to depart at 10:15 am, so boarding was finished by 10:15 am. The reason for the additional delay was unknown to the passengers, who sat on the aircraft for nearly an hour. I had to ask the flight attendant. She informed me that a passenger had checked her bags but had not boarded. Clearly as a result of the chaotic boarding procedure.

The delay was causing anxiety for other foreign tourists as well. Two Greek women were scheduled to board another flight in New Delhi at 1 pm. The flight attendants should at least offer their apologies and provide us with instructions on what to do (including the location of the IndiGo office and ground staff in New Delhi). This never took place.

As seen in the attached photos, the aircraft was filthy. Turbulence forced the flight attendants to halt their meal service, which was done very slowly. 

At Delhi's Terminal 2, I had to locate the ground crew. It goes without saying that they were hurried and unapologetic. They only told me to claim my luggage and that they were unable to assist me. There are no instructions to seek help at the IndiGo office located at terminal 3.

Terminal 3's office staff was same. She made me feel like I was to blame and showed no remorse. When she told me that the sole flight to Kathmandu the next day was at 7 am, she was lying. I informed her that I would choose the 10 am flight as I was aware that there were two other flights available at 10 am and 1 pm.

This is the first time this has ever happened to me, and I have flown on several airlines to more than 20 countries. For many travelers, time is of the essence. If you do not want to waste your time and money, I beg you not to fly with IndiGo!

title: Frustrating Experience with Indigo Airlines' Lost Baggage Service
text:
I recently had a terrible experience with Indigo Airlines regarding my lost baggage. I flew from Sri Lanka to Indore, India, with a transit at Hyderabad. At Hyderabad Airport, I noticed my baggage zipper was broken, which I reported immediately. After re-checking the bag for my connecting flight, I landed in Indore, only to find my baggage missing.

I filed a Property Irregularity Report (PIR) and was promised delivery the next day. However, it has been 8 days, and I’ve yet to receive my baggage. Despite multiple calls to their hotline and an email assurance from their team that their Central Baggage Tracing Unit (CBTU) would contact me within 48-72 hours, no one has reached out.

As a tourist, this has been incredibly inconvenient. My bag contains essential items, including food that is now spoiled. Subject: Urgent Complaint Regarding Incorrect Information and Unprofessional Service

Dear Indigo Airlines Customer Service,

I hope this message finds you well. I am writing to formally lodge a complaint regarding the extremely poor service I have received from your team, which has left me both shocked and frustrated. As an international customer residing in Australia, I reached out to Indigo to inquire about baggage allowance before proceeding with my booking. Unfortunately, the information provided was not only inaccurate, but the customer service I received afterward was appalling.

Here are the details of my experience:

Initial Inquiry on 8th November:

I spoke with a female agent (whose name I do not recall) who confirmed that an additional 15kg piece of baggage would cost Rs 900. I also asked if the price would differ if I carried excess baggage in a single suitcase, and she stated the prices would vary.
When I expressed confusion about why an additional 15kg bag would be cheaper than excess baggage charges for 3-5 kg, she assured me that this was the correct information and that she would confirm with her supervisor. After a follow-up, she confirmed that the information was accurate, and I was satisfied with the details provided.
Booking Process on 11th November:

I went ahead with booking my hotels for my trip in December. When I called again to book my flights, I was shocked to find that the baggage information I had been given was incorrect. I was now told by a different agent, Ankit, that I would need to pay approximately Rs 8000 for an additional 10 kg of baggage—an entirely different and much higher amount than what I had been quoted previously.
Further Communication and Inadequate Support:

I called several times to clarify the situation and was passed from one agent to another—Tina, Divya, and others—each of whom either disconnected the call or transferred me without resolution.
On 12th November, I spoke with Vishal Kumar, who claimed to be a supervisor. When I explained the situation, he accused me of lying and insisted that the recordings of the previous calls showed I had been provided with correct information. However, when he answered the phone, he did not seem to have reviewed the details of my complaint at all, making it clear that no such review had been conducted. His rude and dismissive attitude was unprofessional and uncalled for.
Impact on My Travel Plans:

The misinformation has left me deeply frustrated, and I feel misled by Indigo Airlines. I have been misinformed about baggage charges and faced continuous disregard for my concerns. I am now unsure whether I can trust Indigo Airlines for the rest of my travel plans.
I had planned to visit India and had been looking forward to this trip, but after my experience with your airline, I am reconsidering whether this is the right decision.
I request the following actions:

A clear explanation regarding the discrepancies in the baggage charges.
A full review of the recorded calls, including the conversation from 8th November, and appropriate action to ensure such miscommunication does not happen again.
An apology for the rude and unprofessional behavior exhibited by Vishal Kumar and other customer service agents during my follow-up calls.
A refund or adjustment for the additional baggage charges, as I believe I was misinformed about the rates.
I hope this issue is taken seriously, as the service I have received has been nothing short of disappointing. I expect a prompt response and resolution to this matter.

Thank you for your attention to this matter.

title: A Disappointing Experience with Indigo’s International Service Mumbai to Istanbul – A Customer Review
text:
PNR - QZTHNZ

I want to share my recent experience flying with Indigo Airlines on an international trip. My family and I were celebrating a significant milestone – my 40th birthday – with a vacation to Turkey. We traveled from September 20 to October 1st, 2024, and planned everything around the idea that Indigo Airlines would offer us a seamless flight experience, especially since it offered a direct flight between Mumbai and Istanbul. However, our experience was anything but smooth, and I hope this review will serve as a caution for others considering flying internationally with Indigo.

Booking and Initial Experience:

We are a family of four, and we had booked a round-trip with Indigo from Mumbai to Istanbul for our vacation. The flight was scheduled for 6:55 am on September 20, 2024 as a direct flight, thanks to Indigo’s codeshare arrangement with Turkish Airlines. For the return journey, we had a direct flight on October 1st, 2024 from Istanbul to Mumbai. Our family was excited, and we trusted Indigo based on previous good domestic experiences.

However, four days before our departure, Indigo sent us an unexpected notification – they canceled the direct flight from Mumbai to Istanbul. Instead of the promised direct flight, they rebooked us on a Mumbai to Delhi to Istanbul flight with a 30-hour layover! This was incredibly frustrating as we had made all our plans based on the direct flight.

Dealing with Customer Care:

After receiving this frustrating change, we immediately contacted Indigo’s customer care to express our concerns. Their customer service, unfortunately, left much to be desired. While they did offer us the option of a refund, we decided to continue with the revised flight because the return journey was still a direct flight. We thought we could bear the inconvenience of the onward journey as long as the return trip was hassle-free. 

Customer care managed to rebook us on a 1:15 am flight on the night of September 19th (technically the early hours of September 20th). We flew from Mumbai to Delhi, landing at around 3:15 am. This was quite difficult, especially with two children, and we spent an exhausting night trying to manage our family with minimal sleep.

Mumbai to Istanbul Flight Experience:

After reaching Delhi at 3:15 am, we had to wait until 6:55 am for our connecting flight from Delhi to Istanbul. The entire experience was grueling, especially for our children, who were exhausted from a night of disrupted sleep. Indigo’s handling of the situation was poor. They showed a complete lack of care for families traveling with young children. Not only was the service on the flight mediocre, but there were also no considerations for the challenges we faced because of their last-minute cancellation. No compensation, not even an apology, was offered.

The in-flight service was particularly disappointing. Indigo did not offer any substantial refreshments – only a small glass of water (not even bottled water, just a small cup) was provided. For a flight of over seven hours, this level of service is unacceptable. The food quality was poor, and there were no options or accommodations for those with dietary preferences. Considering this was an international flight, I expected at least basic services comparable to other airlines in this category.

The cabin crew, unfortunately, did not make the experience any better. They were largely unhelpful, inattentive, and showed little concern for the passengers’ comfort. It felt like they were more suited for handling shorter, domestic flights rather than a long international journey.

Return Flight from Istanbul to Mumbai:

Given the stressful onward journey, we were really looking forward to the return flight, which was supposed to be direct. The flight was scheduled for 7:35 pm on October 1st, 2024. Unfortunately, the troubles continued.

When we arrived at Istanbul Airport, we found that the flight was delayed by four hours. There were no clear updates given at the airport, and the Indigo kiosk in Istanbul was not helpful either. Passengers were left confused and anxious, with no information on when the flight would actually take off. We waited at the airport with no updates, only to finally board the delayed flight.

We eventually landed back in Mumbai at 9:45 am on October 2nd, completely exhausted and frustrated by the experience. What was supposed to be a direct flight turned into another ordeal.

Overall Review:

After this experience, I cannot in good faith recommend Indigo Airlines for international travel, especially on their codeshare flights. For domestic flights, Indigo has been fairly reliable in the past, but their international service is a far cry from the standards set by other airlines.

1. Service Quality: The in-flight service was minimal, with almost no concern for passenger comfort on a seven-hour flight. The lack of basic refreshments like bottled water, the poor quality of food, and the unresponsive cabin crew made the journey quite uncomfortable.

2. Customer Care: Indigo’s customer care failed to provide adequate support when they canceled our direct flight. While they did offer a refund, the alternative flight they provided ruined the first night of our vacation and caused immense stress for our family.

3. Flight Delays: The return journey was marked by a significant delay with no proper communication or assistance at the airport in Istanbul. A four-hour delay with no explanation added unnecessary stress at the end of an already exhausting trip.

4. Cost: For the amount we paid – 1,40,000 INR for four people – the service was incredibly poor. Other airlines like Emirates or Etihad were available for slightly higher rates (1,54,000 or 1,66,000 INR for a round trip), and in hindsight, these options would have been far better in terms of service, reliability, and comfort.

Final Thoughts:

In conclusion, if you are planning an international trip, I would strongly advise against booking with Indigo Airlines, especially for long-haul or codeshare flights. While they may offer competitive pricing, the lack of service, poor communication, and disregard for customer experience make it a poor choice. 

I hope this review helps others make an informed decision, and I sincerely hope Indigo takes these concerns seriously and improves their service, especially for international travelers.

Thanks,
Mohit

title: Extremely Disappointed with Indigo Airlines at Vizag Airport
text:
I strongly advise against choosing Indigo Airlines if you have other options available. If you must fly with them, ensure you arrive at least two hours before your departure time. My recent experience at Vizag Airport was terrible, and I feel completely cheated.

I booked my tickets just one day before the journey, and the fare was already double the usual price. Despite completing web check-in, due to unforeseen circumstances, we arrived at the airport 40 minutes before the scheduled departure time, rather than the recommended one hour. Upon reaching the counter to collect our boarding passes, we were bluntly informed that the gate was closed and there was nothing they could do.

It became evident that this denial was intentional. I had booked a morning flight at 8:40 AM, and the next available flight was at 12:25 PM, with over 30 seats available. It felt like they purposely denied us boarding just to make more money by forcing us onto the later flight. We were charged an additional ₹2,500 per ticket. To add to the frustration, we couldn’t even purchase these tickets immediately; we had to wait until 11:25 AM—just one hour before the flight's departure—to secure them. This process was confusing and frustrating.

When we were initially denied boarding, the staff told us we were late and should have arrived at least an hour before, even with web check-in. However, after being forced to wait, we were suddenly allowed to proceed through the entire process, including security checks, within that same one-hour window. This inconsistency in their process was baffling.

My 10-year-old daughter was in tears after we were denied boarding, and the behavior of the Indigo staff was shockingly rude and insensitive. While we understand that we were late, they could have at least treated us with some courtesy.

It’s clear to me that this was a deliberate attempt to profit from us by filling up the 12:25 PM flight. I’ve seen different treatment from other airlines in similar situations—for example, SpiceJet staff at Chennai Airport helped passengers who arrived at the last minute by carrying their luggage and getting them onto the flight.

In the end, we’re all human beings. I urge Indigo Airlines to consider the feelings of their passengers and strive to treat people with respect and understanding, even in challenging situations.

title: the worst airline and my experience
text:
I recently traveled with Indigo Airlines from Dubai to Mumbai, and it was the worst flight experience I've had in my 15 years of traveling. Here's a detailed account of the issues I encountered on this journey.
The airplane was dirty, unhygienic, and had a persistent bad odor. The seats, tray tables, and even the lavatories were poorly maintained, reflecting a severe lack of cleanliness standards.
The flight was uncomfortably hot from start to finish. Despite multiple complaints to the cabin crew, the temperature remained high, making it impossible to relax or get any rest.
Before even boarding the flight, the experience at the check-in counter set a negative tone. The Indigo ground staff were exceptionally rude and unhelpful. Their dismissive attitude and lack of professionalism were shocking and completely unacceptable.
The nightmare continued on my second leg from Mumbai to Calicut. Once again, the ground staff were terrible. They seemed disinterested in assisting passengers and were outright rude in their interactions. The lack of basic customer service skills was evident.
The only redeeming aspect was the cabin crew, who were courteous and tried their best to provide good service despite the other issues. However, this was not enough to offset the overall negative experience.
The return flight from Mumbai to Dubai was the worst part of the entire trip. The airplane was filthy, and the bad smell was even more intense than the previous flights. It felt like the aircraft had not been cleaned in days, making for an extremely uncomfortable environment.
Once again, the flight was unbearably hot. Despite bringing this to the crew's attention, there was no improvement, leading to a very uncomfortable and sweaty journey.
The Indigo ground staff in Mumbai were exceptionally rude. They subjected us to unnecessary questioning, adding to the stress and frustration of the travel experience. Their hostile attitude was unwarranted and highly unprofessional.
To add insult to injury, our suitcases were severely damaged upon arrival. The locks, including TSA-approved ones, were broken, and our luggage was mishandled. This level of disregard for passengers' belongings is unacceptable and highlights the airline's lack of care and responsibility

Indigo Airlines failed miserably in providing a basic standard of service across multiple aspects of the journey. From rude and unprofessional ground staff to dirty and uncomfortable flights, the entire experience was a disaster. 

In my 15 years of traveling, I have never encountered such a poorly managed airline. I am extremely disappointed with Indigo Airlines and will avoid flying with them in the future. This airline needs to seriously reevaluate its customer service and maintenance practices if it hopes to retain any semblance of a good reputation.

title: Regular Changes
text:
I booked three flights with Indigo and will do a combined rating. The flights themselves were fine. We booked the extra services to get checked bags, assigned seats and meals. The food was good. They only serve beverages if you book a meal. I assume water is available for everyone. We also got 10 extra kg as there were 3 of us. That came handy on the last flight for sure.

The staff was friendly and polite. Everything worked as with usual airlines except there were a lot of changes to the flights. Most were a few minutes time difference but our flight from Mumbai to Madurai was changed from 11:50 am to 2:20 pm and then ended up going at 1:30 pm. Our direct flight from Jabalpur to Mumbai was changed to a connecting flight through Delhi. This meant we were at the airport at least half the day. We decided to cancel the flight and drive. That’s a 2 star deduction for me.

Airport security is not their fault but is insane. You need to remove anything electronic from your bags. That includes charger and cords. The first time we had a panic attack when one of our bags went missing. Thankfully apparently the security had put it back through the machine without telling us. We thought someone had left with it. We got better at it the second time around.

It is a handy tool when traveling long distances in India but expect possible changes. You also need to be at the airport two hours ahead of time so there’s a lot of wasted time.

title: Avoid Indigo's International Flights (Dublin to Mumbai's. Comedy of Errors)

So, I was all set to jet off from Dublin to Mumbai via Istanbul (part of Indigo's grand plans to expand their reach), and guess what? Here's the comedy of errors that unfolded:

- First off, I stumble upon the delightful news that my flight from Dublin to Istanbul has been nixed (thanks, Google flights, for being more reliable than the airline itself).
Turkish Airlines confirms the cancellation with their usual flair for vagueness, directing me to deal with Indigo for the fallout.
- Next up, I play the role of the dutiful passenger and inform Indigo about their own cancelled flight (because apparently, communication isn't their strong suit).
- Their customer service hits me with the classic denial: "Oh no sir, everything's running smoothly." Cue me having to school them on the reality of the situation.
IndiGo, true to form, decides to savor the moment before getting back to me (getting through to their customer service should be an Olympic sport).
- Faced with their trademark procrastination, I opt to take matters into my own hands and book a flight with Etihad for the following day (as originally planned), since Indigo's idea of a solution didn't quite align with my schedule.
FYI INDIGO - THIS IS WHY I BOOKED MONTHS IN ADVANCE, TO AVOID THIS EXACT SCENARIO, BUT LO AND BEHOLD, YOU DELIVERED YOUR USUAL BRAND OF INEPTITUDE.
-Eventually, I do get a refund, but the extra expenses incurred due to Indigo's inability to handle international flights? Yeah, those were conveniently overlooked.

And why am I recounting this tale now? Well, Indigo managed to pull off a similar feat with a group of students arriving from India to Dublin yesterday, so I figured I'd share my experience as a cautionary tale. I've been warning folks against this airline's inefficiency, but they just keep proving me right.

Here's hoping my story inspires a flood of similar experiences, so people can see why opting for an Indigo international flight is about as wise as playing roulette with your travel plans.

Oh, and to any of Indigo's competitors scouring TrustPilot for content ideas, how about starting an Instagram page dedicated to showcasing Indigo's less-than-stellar service? It's a win-win: customers get a heads-up, and Indigo gets a reality check.
That's me done venting. Time to salvage what's left of my day after wasting enough of it dealing with this sorry excuse for an airline.

title: Do NOT book Indigo if you have an international connection
text:
My review is not on the flight quality. But more on the pain if transferring between domestic and international terminals in Mumbai and Delhi, if your domestic flight is Indigo.
If you need to transfer from domestic to international flight or vice versa, then do yourself a favour by NOT taking Indigo or other other economy airlines. Make sure both your international and domestic are from the same terminal. 
There is a free bus every 20 mins. Typically you have to wait for 1 hour to get into this free inter terminal bus. 
My other issue with Indigo codesharing international flights is that they not have a proper software integration with star alliance flights. So if you have a codeshare flight with Indigo, you will be able to do online check-in book seats, specify food preferences. Bottom line, do not book an international itinerary that has Indigo  part.
For pure Indian domestic travel, I recommend Indigo.

title: IndieGo Airlines: A Disappointing Journey of Inefficiency and Discomfort
text:
I traveled with IndieGo Airlines, opting to carry only my hand luggage—a fortunate choice, considering the frequent complaints about lost baggage. Initially, my flight was delayed by 24 hours. Unlike other airlines that might rebook passengers on alternative flights or coordinate with partners to maintain original itineraries, IndieGo simply notified me of the delay without offering any resolution.

My journey started in South America, aiming for Indonesia, with layovers in Istanbul and Mumbai. This was my first experience with IndieGo, chosen for its route convenience. However, the airline's staff appeared unprepared, particularly evident during our connection in Mumbai. An attempt to expedite security checks for transferring passengers only resulted in further delays. Despite being among the first to clear security, we were instructed to wait for an escort to the gate—a needless measure since the gate number was known and signage was clear. This directive prevented us from accessing food, seating, or restrooms, causing unnecessary discomfort.

Onboard amenities were noticeably lacking. The flight, exceeding six hours, provided no complimentary meals—a departure from even budget airline standards, which typically offer purchasable options. My flight booking, made through a search platform, did not indicate this, and attempts to buy a meal onboard were thwarted by a requirement to pre-order, leaving only unappetizing instant rice as an option.

The aircraft used for the second leg of my journey seemed ill-suited for long-haul travel, more reminiscent of a plane for a short three-hour flight. Basic provisions like water were not offered, and communication from the crew was severely hindered by language barriers. Despite my fluency in five languages, including two Asian languages, the staff's instructions were incomprehensible until a fellow passenger intervened, clarifying we were to exit from the rear door.

The only silver lining was the likelihood of unoccupied adjacent seats, offering additional space—a small consolation in light of the overall experience. Entertainment options were non-existent, with screens serving no purpose beyond operating reading lights and summoning crew members. The absence of any form of entertainment on a flight of this duration was particularly disappointing.

In my extensive travel history, never have I felt such disdain for an airline. IndieGo's service was marked by inefficiency, inadequate communication, and a complete disregard for passenger comfort and convenience.

title: Horrible experience with Indigo airlines Doh-Hyd flight. international flight made as worse than domestic
text:
My horror story with Indigo – Qatar airways codeshare partner 
My troubles started with the moment I decided to take Indigo connection for the final leg of my trip, HYD-DOH-DFW-DOH-HYD...it was a business class ticket in Qatar airways and I had to take Indigo for the DOH-HYD leg, because if I would have wanted the business class for that leg also in Qatar, it would have been a long lay over. I travelled by 6E1318 on 24th (seat 15A). 
But, here is the saga before that. I reached out to Qatar airways well in advance, to seek permission to use the business class lounge at Doha on return. There were issues but that is more with Qatar airways and I will take it up with them. I tried using the same PNR in ‘manage booking’ in Indigo site to find, what will be my seat. Obviously, the so called codeshare is a joke since it said ‘invalid PNR’. Indigo said that they will get back when the 48 hour window opens before travel. Needless to say, Indigo never got back. 
Qatar airways said, they can’t print an indigo boarding pass and that led to numerous difficulties both in lounge, security as well as as simple us buying in Doha duty free, when I didn’t have the onward boarding pass. Finally, I figured out the gate in Doha and it was B2, which was near to the lounge and hence I planned the time of leaving the lounge accordingly. Just before leaving the lounge, I checked the boards again and I was shocked to see that the gate had changed to C85, that meant a much longer walk. I had to cut short my shopping and run. The moment I realised that it was a downward escalator near C12 that leads to the C8x gates, I realized that it is the same old Indigo ‘kanjucy’ trick of ‘bus’ transport. I reached the C8X series of gates. From the vast, calm, well spaced, well managed gates upstairs in Doha, the C8X gate space was a sea of humanity. There was panic everywhere, long lines, crying babies, fights, squabbles and all kinds of announcements. It looked like a village bus stand on a shanty day or better fish market.
 I worked my way to my gate C85 and it was a clear 90 minutes before the flight time but Indigo had already commenced boarding and there was panic everywhere. I joined the serpentine queue (no separate line for Business class since it is all cattle class in Indigo anyway). Finally, I got my boarding pass and it was seat 15A. So much so, for the Qatar assurance that I will get a good seat and Indigo promise that it will be seamless and 48 hours hour before they will allocated the ‘right seat’. Now came another shock, I had a carry on and a laptop bag and no other bag, as part of my business class ticket. The Indigo staff were rude and they snatched the carry on trolley but they were equally rude to all. Then the bus trip began and even the familiar Indigo ramp was NOT there and there was the ladder climb with my laptop bag (now much heavier since I had to repack some valuables hurriedly before the Indigo Nazis took away my carry on trolley). I was seeing that old people, who had take the other US flights & connecting at Doha via Indigo struggling to climb the ladder. 
Anyway, onto seat number 15A. It was a hard seat with the adjustment button for tilt, forcefully removed (maybe it is an exit row seat in some other configuration but in this the exit rows were 2 rows before). The flight left on time and the so called Indigo service began, after about an hour. I had prebooked AVML. When the hostess were near 15x seats,,,the one ones from the forward galley stopped at around 12x and the ones from the rear galley stopped around 17x. They ran out of everything and were going back & forth from pilferaging from each other to serve the respective, last seats. Anyway, finally the trolley made its way from 17X to 16x to 15X and it had taken 45 minutes more. That is 1 hour and 45 mins later, from the wheel up time. The hostess handed off that tiny bag consisting of a cookie, cashew and a mixed fruit drink. She said, she will get me a sandwich and that took about 20 min more. Given the stale sandwich, I returned the same and asked for water and coffee. The hostess refused the same, since the seat belt sign had come on due to turbulence. After some 10 mins, the fasten seatbelt sign went away and I pressed the button to get the hostess. Noone came for about 20 mins and when one finally came, the fasten seat belt sign came on again and she said, she can’t serve coffee. No water either. Now, as soon as she went back, the fasten seatbelt sign was off and I pressed the button again. Again a long wait and she came to find out as if it is a totally new case. Asked for coffee again and she went back and never came back. That is that. So, in a 4 hour flight, Indigo couldn’t find a window to serve coffee or give a cup of water to me. 
Then came the landing in Hyd and needless to say, it is a remote bay since Indigo’s aim is to screw the passengers as much as feasible. All the international gates and aerobridges were open in Hyd (except Oman air standing), the gates were wide open but Indigo had to save the money and hence they went to remote bay. The manual ramps were slided in, after a lengthy delay of 15 minutes. (I was watching from my window seat. The staff on ground were bored and were in no hurry to get the ladder). 15X seats were the last to get down since it was midpoint and we had to take the last of the buses. Now, on to the bus. It was super crowded. Many passengers were returning to India with their children, for the 1st time post covid and this was the experience, Indigo gave by stuffing them. The bus was a brand new electric bus but something is wrong with these buses, It does not crawl more than 10-15 kmph speed. The driver drove it slowly and it was a long drive to get to the international arrival gate. The driver did not switch on the a/c and the passengers were suffocating and when asked, the driver refused. An argument started and the driver stopped the vehicle, to argue. Finally, he switched it on and it was an ugly altercation in Telugu & Hindi. So, we landed at 8 and after long taxing to remote bay, slow ladder pull up, last bus and the argument, we were at the gate at 9.30 AM. That was 90 minutes since touch down. The immigration, customs and baggage (thank God) took 10 minutes each and I was in the taxi after about 45 minutes. End to end, from touch down – door to door, I reached home at 1130AM that is 3.5 hours after landing. 
· Indigo has converted every international flight as cattle class · Codeshare is a joke. No seamlessness to manage the booking and get your boarding pass in advance
 · The crew is ill-trained, ill-equipped and the cattle feed you throw on the face of hyd-BLR flight can’t be same poultry feed you throw on an international trip passenger, esp coming from Business class. You can not handle with the same equipment, same poultry feed dishes, same ill trained crew, of what you dish out for India domestic flights, when flying international routes, even if the distances are small
· Stop using remote bays once and for all. Eradicate your methods of saving costs at the experience of passengers · And train your crew to be sensible and sensitive

title: Delayed.
text: I have been travelling in India a while. Happy to say I only had one internal flight with them. The rest were with Air India who were a hundred times better. IndiGo Airlines are a low-cost carrier. Remember, these sorts of airlines go back and forth between cities and if there is a delay, then there is a knock-on effect for the other flights which is what happened to me. I had a late evening flight which was meant to depart Jaipur at 22:00 for Delhi. This was delayed to 22:30, then 23:25 and finally 23:30. Fine, it was only one and a half hours but late evening and a flight duration of only 50 minutes meant I arrived at my hotel past 01:30 and had to get up early the next morning for a tour. The plane was filthy as they don't clean between flights. It was easy checking in online. Staff were pleasant and friendly. Bags took ages to be delivered in Delhi. Once we finally boarded, they did do this quite quickly although it was chaos and we departed pretty fast. First time in all my years travelling, I had seen a very rushed and not complete safety procedure demonstration! Very concerning. As this was a super short flight, no frills and basic. Complimentary bottle of water provided. You can order food before the flight and they will deliver it to your seat but you cannot purchase anything on board. Seats were average for a short-haul flight and a quick snooze. My baggage allowance weight for checking in my bag was only 20KG and I had to pay as I was overweight. The gentleman did reduce the fee but I felt that he could have let me go as it was only slightly over. I am told flights with IndiGo Airlines are often delayed. In all honesty, Air India are not much more difference in price for internal flights. Use them instead. I only booked this one flight with IndiGo Airlines due to timing but we ended up being delayed anyway. My only positive was pleasant and friendly staff, both when checking in and on board and the complimentary bottle of water, which most airlines would not usually provide for such a short flight.

title: IndiGo flight fraught with problems
text:
The airline has a very dysfunctional payment portal and website in general. I was trying to book return flights BKK-CCU-BKK. It was a pain as website kept hanging up. Eventually I got to the payment page and was told AMEX refused payment. As I called AMEX they said they never got the request, and did not refuse the transaction. On their advice I tried to pay again while they stayed on the line. Same result. So I then booked on AirAsia. However, the IndiGo charge showed up three days later, and I had to get it reversed after disputing the charge.
However, the story continued. I realized that the AirAsia booking was actually BKK-CCU on Spice Jet and CCU-BKK on IndiGo.  I needed to pay for an extra bag on the CCU-BKK sector, and that was the the next problem.  The website hung up when I provided my locator each time I tried. After a 40 minutes phone tag I got a CSR, but then she hung up.  After multiple tries (lengthy wait times) finally one CSR processed my request and asked me to pay through a link that would come on my registered email ID. It did not come! The next time the CSR asked me to process my payment as she stayed on the line, and that too failed and she meanwhile dropped my call.

So I tried to check-in online and again that did not work. At the airport multiple hand held credit card readers did not work, and eventually one did, but would not work with AMEX. The agent asked me to pay in cash, and I put my foot down and said NO. Eventually they did process on a Chase Visa. This was another half hour of my time wasted. On to the next part...

As I was checked in, I received three different emails from AirAsia saying that my flight was delayed by about 90 minutes. I went to the lounge and as I was answering emails I overheard a fellow passenger saying that he was proceeding to the boarding gate for the same flight. I went to the gate and saw that the flight was actually boarding, and on time. Lucky that I didn't believe the emails and missed the flight.

Finally, the flight... the aircraft was clean and boarding was orderly. I did not pre-order any food, so was not expecting anything. But not even water/soft drinks were offered. Late into the flight someone came around with a tray with cups of water, and that was it. For a 2 1/2 hr international flight I thought it was lame. Sitting in row 1, I was not able to manage a shut eye because the entire time the cabin crew were chatting loudly (with an off-duty non-rev crew joining them.

This leg with IndiGo left a bad taste in my mouth, and I have resolved that I woud never again fly the airline unless I had no choice.

title: Indigo Airlines “India’s flying state transport bus”

There are no monitors, chargers in the planes and the seats have the bare minimum cushion. 

In one of the domestic flight, the air hostesses handed over some food packets and beverages for only a few random passengers. I asked for a beverage and the air hostesses politely told me that sir this is only for those passengers who have pre-booked snacks/food. I asked them how I can get it now since I didn’t pre-book. I was told to wait until they serve all the pre-booked passengers. I understand you want to keep your costs down but I have flown quite a few airlines and the basic complimentary thing they offer is tea, coffee, sodas and some juices.
I took an Indigo international flight (I had booked Qatar airways flight from Washington to Hyderabad). Due to their code share partnership, Indigo flights operate from Doha to Hyderabad and vice versa. This international flight was no different than the domestic with basic required amenities(remember no monitors for entertainment or chargers). However, this time I was handed a food packet with a sandwich. I just could not believe the food quality of a so called international flight. I have never eaten a cold “paneer tikka masala” stuck between two cold bread loaf’s. It tasted awful, atleast this could have been wrapped in a roti. Since I was hungry ate little bit of the sandwich as I had another 4 hours of flight time left before I reach Doha. 

Till next time on another Indigo flight, Hoping there is some improvement in food quality and service.
Good luck.

title: IndiGo Airlines Review: Mixed Experience with Flights and Disappointing Customer Service
text:
My recent experience with IndiGo Airlines encompassed three flights on different sectors – BHO-DEL, DEL-DED, and DEL-BHO. While the airline is known for its budget-friendly approach, my overall impression was a mix of positive and disheartening moments.

Let's start with the positives. The flights themselves were generally punctual, adhering to the schedule with minimal delays. The cabin crew on a couple of the flights were attentive and professional, delivering a standard of service one would expect from a reputable airline.

However, my enthusiasm for the airline waned when it came to interactions with the staff. While some members were efficient and helpful, a significant portion left much to be desired. The pinnacle of disappointment was an encounter with Mr. Sumeet at Terminal 2 of New Delhi airport. His lack of politeness and basic courtesy, especially when dealing with a senior citizen, was both surprising and disheartening. Such behavior is not only unprofessional but also reflects poorly on the airline's commitment to customer service.

The inconsistency in the quality of staff interactions raises concerns about the airline's training and employee standards. In an industry where customer satisfaction is paramount, these interpersonal aspects play a crucial role in shaping the overall experience for passengers.

Additionally, the negative encounter with Mr. Sumeet overshadowed the positive aspects of the journey. Even a few positive interactions cannot fully compensate for such a glaring lapse in customer service. It is essential for IndiGo to address and rectify such instances promptly to maintain its reputation in the highly competitive aviation industry.

Beyond the issue with staff, there were no significant complaints about the actual flights. The seating was standard for a budget airline, and the in-flight services were acceptable. However, the overall experience was marred by the unpleasant encounter at the Delhi airport.

In conclusion, while IndiGo Airlines offers competitive prices and on-time flights, the quality of customer service, as demonstrated by interactions with certain staff members, leaves much to be desired. The airline should prioritize consistent training to ensure that all employees uphold the standard of professionalism and courtesy expected in the service industry. My personal experience, particularly with Mr. Sumeet, has left me with a negative impression, and if given a choice, I would hesitate to choose IndiGo for my future flights. Improving customer service should be a priority for the airline to retain and attract passengers in an industry where reputation is everything.

text:
I tried to book a flight on September 27, 2023 for a January 1st, but I haven't succeed.

The funds were completely debited from the card, but the site displayed an error message.
Then I received an email saying there was nothing to worry about and I would receive a full refund within 5-7 business days.

I was repeatedly promised that they would give feedback by email, but, of course, nothing like that happened (I made at least 5 attempts).
I was assured that I needed to wait another 24-48 hours.

Another week of stupid excuses and exhausting communication with customer service has passed.

Surprisingly, they responded to me by email, specifically noting that they processed my transaction manually, and promising that the funds would arrive in my account within 7-10 business days.

As you might guess, today is the 10th working day, no money has been received, and technical support said that they are SUDDENLY having difficulties with the payment gateway, and that I am not the only client who has similar problems.

Empty promises.
An outright lie (if they continue to have difficulties with the payment gateway, why did they previously indicate the time frame for returning the money?).
Incompetence.
Unprofessionalism.
Complete lack of customer focus - some poor fellow from customer service deigned to call me a month later (!) to express an apology that was completely uninteresting to me. And he, too, could not give an articulate answer to a very simple (I would even say "primitive"!) question: when will my money be returned?

If you want to fly somewhere, use the services of another airline.
If you want to lend 500+ dollars to scammers with an unclear prospect of getting it back, welcome to the IndiGo website.

title: The Good and the Bad
text:
It was my first time flying with Indigo Air and the experience was overwhelming. I will not beat around the bush and will give highlights from booking until the end. 

Online Booking:
Good

Customer Service:
Extremely Good and Extremely Bad
     This will depend on who you will be able to speak with. Someone was travelling with me whose passport shows 2 names in first name, no name in the middle and 1 last name. Indian nationals usually have confusing names. Some do not have last names and all will be on the first name section. I called Indigo Air UAE and they said there will be no issues on this and the passenger will not be offloaded. So basically, from UAE to India, it will be ok. However, they are not sure from India to UAE how it will be. I then used chat online to check what can be done and I was advised to speak with an agent. I called Indigo India and the call was transferred to a supervisor who was not friendly and insisted that they cannot do anything to amend the name since they have no proof that it is the same person who booked. This is also regardless of how many proofs that were specified during the booking, which can be tallied with the passport. I would suggest that they become more courteous and be more pro-active when such situation happens since the passports really are an issue. Being a supervisor (if the lady was indeed really their supervisor), then proper training must be given to her.  By the way, I had spoken to one regular customer service rep in Indigo Air on another matter and that gentleman was absolutely professional, Unfortunately, I was not able to obtain his name to give a commendation. He deserves to be promoted. Random calls must be checked by Customer Service Department in order to do proper coaching, even to the supervisors. 

Aircraft Review:
Very Good
     This is a budget airline. Hence we cannot expect too many amazing stuff inside. However, the seats are comfortable and the leg room is very good. 

Cabin Crews:
Very Good
     The cabin crews are all friendly and accommodating.

Pilots:
Very Good
     DXB - BOM
     BOM - DXB 

***My phone was left inside the aircraft
Due to the extreme weather condition in Mumbai during landing, I was praying all throughout. The pilot is skillful and was able to properly land the plane.  However, due to the mental stress and the same time excitement, I forgot that my phone was kept in the next in front of my seat. I only realized that I left it there when I was about to line up at the Immigration Section. I immediately ran to a lady officer (stationed exactly before the restrooms and the Immigration Area) and explained the situation. She requested for me to take a seat and wait for her to give me a feedback. 15 minutes later, she told me to pass through Immigration, take my luggage and there, I will be met by an Indigo Air staff to give hand over my phone. I did as told. When the staff met me, she said that my phone was not found. I told her about the officer who told me and that to call her directly as she is still at her post. She called someone else and insisted that they do not have it. I was given Airport Security's number and told me to try giving that number a call later on. When I reached the hotel, I called the number and it was Security/Control Room of the Airport, who then confirmed they have my phone. I was so confused as the Indigo Staff advised me they do not have it, while the airport officer said it was found and will be given to me at the conveyor belt section. Perhaps, someone else gave my phone to Airport Security or perhaps there was a miscommunication between the Indigo Ground Staff who approached me at the Luggage Section and whoever she was speaking with on the phone. In the end, I am very grateful that they found it and gave it back. 
     Kudos to Mumbai Airport Staff (officer near Immigration Post - Arrival) and to Security/Control Room!!!! Thank you so much. 
     Thank you as well to the Indigo Air staff who tried his/her best to find my phone. God bless you!

So, will I recommend Air Indigo? Yes. There were good and bad things that happened but overall experience was good. Some people are very good while some may require more training in terms of communication. Now, I will only fly either Emirates Airlines or Indigo Air to India.

title: Baggage policy
text:
I recently had the opportunity to use Indigo for my multi-city trip within India and an international leg. While I've heard positive things about the airline's efficiency and services, my personal experience left much to be desired.

I had booked a round trip from Bengaluru to Mumbai, followed by Delhi to Chennai, and finally from Chennai to Abu Dhabi. The flights themselves were relatively smooth, but the issue arose when it came to the baggage policy.

During my journey, I found myself with just 1 kg of excess baggage in my main suitcase. Given that I am a loyal customer and have flown with Indigo multiple times, I had expected a bit of leniency or understanding from the airline's side. Unfortunately, that was not the case. The ground staff I encountered seemed unwilling to consider my loyalty or any special circumstances.

I was taken aback by their refusal to accommodate the minor excess baggage, especially considering the number of times I had chosen their airline for my travels. The suggestion I received was to remove items from my luggage to meet the weight limit. This left me in a rather uncomfortable situation, as I was forced to remove some of my belongings to comply with their rigid policy.

One of the most disappointing aspects was that I was unwell during this journey. Despite my explanations and requests, the ground staff appeared unmoved and unsympathetic. 

To add to my frustration, I had to carry my suits separately, which not only inconvenienced me but also highlighted the airline's unwillingness to accommodate even the most reasonable requests. It was disheartening to see the ground staff seemingly satisfied with my discomfort.

In the end, this experience with Indigo's baggage policy and customer service was far from pleasant. While I understand the importance of adhering to rules, a bit of flexibility and consideration for loyal customers during exceptional circumstances would have gone a long way in making me feel valued as a passenger. I hope that Indigo takes these kinds of situations as an opportunity to improve their policies and customer service approach for a better overall flying experience in the future.

title: Frustrating Experience with Indigo's Lack of Information
text:
If I had the option, I would give Indigo Airlines a 0-star rating for the horrendous experience I recently endured. I booked a flight from Ahmedabad to Toronto through their services, with a connecting flight in Abu Dhabi. However, the lack of communication and transparency regarding the transit visa requirement turned what should have been a smooth journey into an utter nightmare.

To begin with, my booking was done through Goibibo, an associated platform. Surprisingly, neither Indigo nor Goibibo provided any information about the necessary transit visa for my connecting flight through Abu Dhabi. My intention was to ensure a trouble-free journey, so I applied for a transit visa despite having a layover of less than 8 hours, based on the advice I received. However, the lack of coordination between Indigo, Goibibo, and the transit visa guidelines left me feeling completely stranded.

Adding to my frustration, Indigo's website failed to mention anything about the transit visa requirement during the check-in process. No email notification was received either, which could have potentially saved me from this ordeal. Ultimately, I was left with no choice but to cancel my flight due to the contradictory and confusing information provided.

Indigo Airlines needs to seriously address these issues and take steps to prevent other travelers from facing a similar predicament. A significant number of passengers book flights through third-party apps like Goibibo, Yatra, and MyTrip, relying on these platforms for accurate information. It is imperative for Indigo to send out clear and timely notifications via email, especially when crucial travel requirements like transit visas are involved.

This experience has cost me not only valuable time but also a substantial amount of money—over a lakh—in addition to the inconvenience caused. I hope that by sharing my story, others can be better informed and avoid falling victim to the same lack of communication that I encountered. Indigo Airlines must take immediate steps to improve their customer communication and ensure that no other traveler has to endure such a frustrating and costly experience.

title: Bad experience with Turkish code share flight Indigo Airlines from Istanbul IST to New Delhi DEL
text:
While travelling from IST Istanbul to New Delhi DEL, we had a code share flight Indigo Airlines and had a very bad experience. 

Domestic Aircraft Type
- Aircraft type was same type as used in domestic routes in India with congested seats and meal service was super slow. Even though we were seated in row 5, and air hostess took a lot of time to reach because they need to punch in something in their devices after handing over the food to every passenger.

Seat/Meal Booking Issue
- Also for seat and meal booking, Turkish wasn’t able to book any as they said its a code share airline so I had to call Indigo directly but upon calling them they said the same thing so this was a deadlock but later I got in touch with supervisor and he was just able to book the seats.

Limited Food Options
- There were only three Food options available if you haven’t booked the meal in advance (which i tried but didn’t work for me) were only instant hot water based such as Maggie, rice/lentils, and poha so for a six hour flight that was not good at all and they serve only once.

Connecting Indigo Flight missed due to late baggage arrival
- After immigration when we went to collect our bags, there were already lot of bags from a different airline on the belt number and nobody was picking them up due to which all the bags from our flight got stuck.

I had to call the supervisor to let them know that I had a connecting flight so he with his group of other staff members cleared up the belt so that our bags could load but this took an hour or so and we missed our next flight. This was a lesson for us as well to keep more buffer time

Summary: Better to pay extra and get the same carrier flight rather than code share flight. Indigo needs to improve a lot in international as they are just using the same domestic aircraft type and same food service they offer when flying domestically which is not at all comfortable to the passengers taking long haul flights.

title: Diverted to JAIPUR due to severe weather
text:
Diverted to Jaipur due to Severe Weather!

Twelve of us travelling together took the Jabalpur - Delhi IndiGo Airlines flight 6E6073 on 30th March 2023.  The check-in and security procedures at Jabalpur were breezy. 

We were transported by coach from the airport to the Airbus 320 aircraft having 3-3 seating per row.  The flight was almost full.  The leg-space was adequate. 

The flight took off at the scheduled time 1600 hrs.  A snack of sandwiches and fruit juice was served during the flight.  Although the flight was scheduled to land at 1710, it was diverted to Jaipur airport due to severe lightning and thunderstorms at Delhi airport, and landed there at 1820.  The passengers were requested to remain in the aircraft whilst the plane was at Jaipur.

During this forced stay at Jaipur, we were served a packet of snacks (nuts, biscuit and drink) to hopefully shorten the unintended wait.  The aircraft finally took off at 2020 from Jaipur, Delhi bound and eventually landed in Delhi at 2110.  The coach transfer from the aircraft to the terminal took a further 30 minutes.

The cabin crew continued to be helpful, courteous and professional under very difficult conditions especially during the two hours that the flight was grounded in Jaipur.

text:

title: Missed flight
text:
I had a flight from Istanbul to New Delhi,  on 15 February 2023, 20:15, missed because of the long passport border control checking.  
I arrived to the airport at 18:00, more than two hours before flight. When I received my boarding pass, it was 18:30, and I directly went to border passport control.
When I was passing border passport control, I had my boarding pass with me and passport.  The border officer stopped me and sent to their office for the deep checking. This procedure took me about one hour, finally they found the mistake in their computer system.
When the officer found this issue, he informed the gate personnel to wait for me, because I did not have any law violations and allowed to go to the flight.
Another police officer checked my documents again at the border control counter and
finally let me enter the boarding area, I was running to my gate, but, when I came, it was too late, and the gate personnel informed me, that the gate is already closed for the boarding five minutes ago.

I wrote a claim to IndiGo customer relations centre, demanded to investigate my case, provide me a new ticket or a refund for an unused flight. I included the evidences, as the paper from the police, my boarding pass with the stamps, my passport fotos, that there was not my fault. 
The logic is as follows: since you have already checked me in for the flight, you guarantee that the time remaining before departure will be enough to go through all the necessary procedures.  Long police checks are not the problem of the passenger, but the problem of the airline's relationship with the airport.  Especially if, during the verification procedure, the airline personnel were notified by the police services.

The answer I received from IndiGo customer relations centre, was the standard form, without any specifying the specific data of the passenger (seems like they even have not read my letter at all), with the standard answer, that they are refusing to do anything for me.
Therefore, I am totally disappointed and count that Air IndiGo is not customer friendly and I do not recommend to anyone  to use it at all.

title: An enthralling incident with "Indigo" Airlines
text:
Why Enthralling when India's best airlines transport passengers from leg-to-leg (as per them, on time, every time)?

Let me start by disclosing a few of the following:
* Traveled self and family
* Experiences are self-faced and not copied from other sources
* Travel Dates altered to protect privacy.

My Travel Itinerary: 2 Adults and 2 Kids, Per Pax 23 Kgs*2 Baggage + 7 Kgs Cabin Luggage allowed.
> Oct 28 IAD to DOH to HYD (Qatar > Indigo)
> Dec 26 HYD to DOH to IAD (Indigo > Qatar)

The journey from IAD to DOH is pretty and happier with their Code Share partner; all the staff at Origin are helpful, courteous, and professional. Nothing special to be highlighted in this gesture.

The journey from DOH to HYD, concerns starts with Boarding until Landing. So, let's jump into facts. 
* Boarding: All International Airlines across the globe board senior citizens, passengers on wheelchairs, and parents with kids first. For "Indigo" Airlines, this is not the case will "dump" people onto the Bus and transport them from Gate to the Aircraft.
* In-Flight: Seating is congested, just like Auto-Rickshaw. The cabin crew is courteous and helpful. However, none of the passengers screened well and followed their orders/requests to wear masks. As a result, we were hit with Covid-19 with their dull negligence as one of the passengers sneezed inflight and not wearing a mask.
* Landing: 30 Minutes late from their scheduled arrival. As a result, we had to spend another 30 Minutes at the HYD Airport for Immigration Officers' shift rotation.

Overall DOH-HYD Experience is just a dump yard ride for me in Indigo Airlines.

The journey from HYD to DOH, concerns starts with Check-In until the Landing.
Nonetheless, this part of the journey is the most "Interesting" part of this review, don't miss it.

* Check-In: I cannot reiterate my Boarding comment mentioned above, but this Indigo airline is adverse in implementing standards of the International Flight code.
  * Reached the Airport 4 hours before departure, Kids in arms and eight bags to check-in (opted porter service), had to stay in line for 1 hour 25 minutes to approach the check-in counter after repeated requests to follow the check-in code.  
  * Finally, at the check-in counter, the indigo staff was inclined to charge me 15k INR extra as my three bags had 1 kg extra and other bags had less than 23 kg allowed. Perpetuating their Code-Share Policy is per bag and not Total Baggage Allowance.
  * Another 30 minutes decayed to clean up the mess they created with bags and complete the Check-In process.

*Boarding: Reached the Boarding gate running upon completion of Immigration and Security clearance. Boarding will start in 30 minutes. (Boarding Feedback is the same as above).

The flight missed the departure time by 27 minutes and arrived at DOH 36 minutes late. As a result, complete baggage from the Indigo flight passengers onboard couldn't board into DOH-IAD Flight.

We (my family) took a personal oath not to fly "Indigo" in our life in their "International" sector to void amateurish personnel and never on time. We booked a hotel at IAD Airport to wait for the baggage to arrive and travel back home.

title: Experiences travelling with a wheelchair person
text:
Couple of things to be aware of if you have a wheelchair passenger and purchased a multiple route ticket 
(1) I was flying from Durgapur via Delhi to Bhopal. Single PNR, but 2 boarding passes. I paid excess baggage which is insanely high, Rs 550/kg. The airport staff was kind enough to offer a tiny bit discount. They don't allow personal wheelchairs or walkers in flight. They need to be checked in with your luggage but free of charge. Arrive early as things are very disorganized at every Indian airport. When I reached Delhi, the Indigo folks told me that I will have to pay excess baggage for my remaining leg of flight. I told them that I had already paid it, to which they said I had booked 2 leg journey so excess baggage should be paid for each leg. However I was aware of the rules, and asked them to tell me what was the other PNR that they were seeing on their screens. Having been caught in their bluff they backtracked but would have screwed me if I had been a newby.
(2) Called it the airline mismanagement or the Delhi Airport mismanagement, the arrival flight was in Terminal T1, but the departing flight to Bhopal was from T2. T1 and T2 are miles apart and you will need a transport. The Indigo folks at T1 wouldn't let me take my own personal transport since I had a wheelchair passenger who had been entered into their system. No problem with that. The problem was the transport they called for me. One small Maruti Suzuki for 2 people and 5 luggage plus a wheelchair and a walker. I found that once I exited the terminal and knew I could go back to complain and ask for a different vehicle. Sly foxes didn't tell me inside the terminal that their was a tiny car they had booked for me. I was literally sitting in the car with wheelchair and walker on top of me. 
(3) When the plane arrived in Bhopal it was raining. Instead of taking us out from the front where there was a roof on the stairs, they asked us to leave through the backdoor of the plane. My wheelchair passenger got fully wet. Again the shortcut and I don't care mentality most of us Indians towards our fellow Indians.

They however did provide us with a cabin wheelchair, with extra helping hands to board the plane and disembark and talked to us nicely too. They weren't rude at any point of time. The young lads and airhostesses whom they have hired are all north Indians mostly from Punjab, Bihar and UP so communicating with them in Hindi will never be an issue.
