text:
My 84 year old mother came with me yesterday on a business class ticket bought on the Qatar website. While we know indigo dies not have business class seating, we were completely unprepared for the extent of inefficiency and plain lack of care by indigo during the entire experience. Absolutely no communication from indigo ahead of the trip, long wait when calling their customer service. They would not allow a web check in or seat selection or request a wheelchair or a veg meal.  After hours of waiting on the phone, I was finally able to request a wheelchair, and received a confirmation of my request by email. However, upon arrival, she was hassled and told to take out 2 kilos from obe bag that weighted 27 kgs (multiple communications from Qatar had confirmed weight limit of 32 kgs per bag, which indigo refused to honor. In fact, we were told indigo contacted Qatar by phone and were told to 'make no exception to indigo policy'. This is an 84 year old woman, on a business class code share, flying at 2am! 

The pain continued. She was initially denied a wheelchair (we were told she is waitlisted, indigo staff could care less about the confirmation of the request by Qatar) After a long wait, we finally were taken to the aircraft. We asked for veg food, were handed chicken sandwiches, and when I notified staff, they 'were sorry but veg sandwiches have to be ordered ahead of time online'. Remember that we were refused a web check in, or the ability to order online? 

At Doha airport (simply wonderful airport btw) we waited for over an hour before someone finally listened to my repeated requests to send us to the business lounge. My mother was able to test for 45 minutes, while I had hoped for her to be able to sleep for about 4 hours. 

I would say, fly very far away from the indigo-qatar code share. It's a hot mess, and leaves you cold and miserable!! The two airlines don't communicate, assure you of one baggage rule and enforce another draconian one, are insensitive to a senior disabled person's physical discomfort, and completely unable to provide a business class experience at the airports. 

Not a good use of over $4000 as far as my mom's ticket.

title: Baggage Fee Scam....BEWARE
text: So, I tried to heed the many warnings that I saw in this airline's terrible reviews regarding their baggage “Scam” policy. I recently had a flight from Mumbai to Maldives, for which the ticket fare was $159 for a one-way ticket. Still a little pricey, but not bad. The only reason why I took this airline was becuase it was the only airline available that had a direct flight to the Maldives. After booking the ticket, I noticed right away that it said only 20 kilo bag allowance. My initial thought was that it was a low weight for an international flight, but I'm sure I can purchase a bag, just in case. The week of the flight, I spent quite a bit of time looking through the baggage options. One problem is that the website will not allow you to add a bag until 48 hours before the flight, which is incredibly inconvenient when you are traveling. At 48 hours, I started the attempt to add a bag. The website is not user-friendly when it comes to adding bags. When you click on the add bags button, it takes you to another screen which then has two more buttons for add to cart or purchase now. Neither of these buttons works. I tried on Safari, Chrome, and also my mobile. Nada. The day before the flight, I spent well over an hour trying to figure out how to do it. On my mobile, I was able to get a little closer to where it would add excess weight, but only 5 kilos. You click on that button and the screen goes blank. Long story short, I had to spend an enormous amount of time on my holiday trying to add a dang bag. I finally found the loophole. When you go to 6e add-ons (where the add baggage should be but isn't) and just click on anything that is listed. It will take you to the add on page and then there it is. Add a bag. More confusion sets in, because it says add an additional bag for 1800 rupees (~$22 usd). I thought, perfect! One catch, I didn't see anywhere that says what the additional weight is of that bag like you do on ALL the other airline websites out there. The morning of the flight, I saw my bags were still a little too heavy, so I added an extra 5 kilos, which was $40 for just 5 kilos. Yes, $40 for just 5 kilos. I get to the airport and my two bags were 35 kilos. Guy said that my bags were too heavy. I was so confused. I tried what I could to avoid a nightmare and yet it happened anyway. Come to find out, you are allowed 2 bags of 20 kilos TOTAL. Doesn't say total on the website. So, you have to pay $22 extra for the same exact weight, but for an additional bag! What the ever living... That makes no sense. You pay extra for a bag, but actually get less weight, because the additional bag will also add weight, so you have to pack fewer items. What a disaster. I ended up having to pay $162 in baggage fees for my $159 flight. How the government allows this, I have no clue. I saw a review where someone mentioned highway robbery. Good description, but more like extortion. I also notice that it tends to happen more to foreigners traveling. You have been warned, DO NOT use this airline. Hopefully one day, a reputable airline like Vistara (which was great) will buy this company out and change things around for the good, because the current management should truly be ashamed. And if anyone asks about the plane size and baggage weight, it was a normal size plane, probably more to the larger size. There is only one reason for these kinds of prices and it is GREED. BEWARE!

title: Do not recommend for international travel
text:
I had decided to fly IndiGo Airlines from Istanbul to Hyderabad, since it was a direct flight to Delhi from Istanbul with a short layover in Delhi before my connection to Hyderabad. Unfortunately, I didn't pay much attention to finer details about food on-board etc while booking the flight for paucity of time. I simply expected basic food/services since it's international travel & the flying time was ~06h30m. 

I checked-in in advance but didn't receive my boarding pass via email. I took a print at the airport.

The flight was at 20:45 from Istanbul and I just really wanted to unwind and catch up on sleep. I was immediately disappointed on boarding the plane. The seats - the almost 06h30m flight had the same seats as any of its domestic flights. Narrow, thin cushioned and uncomfortable. There is no in-flight entertainment/screens, no charging points, no pillows or blankets, or wet-wipes. 

Food is for sale and only water (in medium size paper cups) is complimentary. I had no idea about the on-board food scene and so this was a massive disappointment for an international flight. Even the food options are the same "instant" food you get on domestic flights. Instant poha, instant noodles etc. If you haven't pre-booked "chef's specials", I would strongly recommend you stuff your face with food at the airport (as I did). 

I had to ask the air hostess thrice before I got my 1st half a glass of water. They police you to wear masks on board but allow for passengers to buy + eat food immediately after a mask patrol. 

Since sleep was important, I covered myself head to toe in my warm, clearly visible green shawl, wore a jacket and also put the hood over my head. I immediately fell into a slumber owing to exhaustion - only to be rudely woken up by the air hostess, almost screaming, to ask if I had garbage to dispose off. She may have raised her voice because I was so fast asleep I may not have heard her. Btw, we still had a good FIVE HOURS OF FLYING TIME when she woke me up for garbage disposal (even my tray was shut). I had an on-set of migraine owing to it and barely got any sleep after. 

My petit size notwithstanding, it was really hard to rest anything except my butt on the seat when I reclined and stretched a little. Seats are super uncomfortable. 

There was no announcement of commencement of descent or expected temperature at the landing city. One harried air hostess was running back and forth making a last ditch attempt to serve water before landing. 

The print on the boarding pass (Del-Hyd leg) was so poor that it didn't get scanned at the post check-in Security at Delhi airport. Needless to mention that IndiGo staff at Delhi had checked and seen the boarding pass I was issued while checking my luggage in. I had to stand in the security queue twice as I was sent back to get a better print from the counter. When I went back to the counter, the staff at the counter was chatting with another ground staff about Jackie Shroff flying on one of their planes later in the day. I had to put my request across thrice and be Stern before they reacted.

There is absolutely no difference between the service you get on a Hyd-Blr stretch and the one you get on international legs with this airline. If anything, this was even worse. Unless the timing of the flight is absolutely non-negotiable, there are a ton of better & more comfortable options. 

All in all, it was a really frustrating flying experience - the in flight crew services were below average. Just nothing about this flight seemed international and it almost felt like they were doing us a favour by flying us to Delhi. 

Even if you are spending a few bucks extra, having a comfortable flight makes a world of a difference when you fly across timezones. So, I would strongly discourage an international flight with IndiGo.

title: Infant / Baby CRS (Car seat) damage
text:
tl;dr- Indigo was utterly careless in handing a sensitive item like infant / baby child restraint system (CRS) even after we safely checked it to them at the gate. 

It looks their untrained baggage handlers at AMD sent the car seat down on the luggage chute/slide!! when it was given to them at the door. The bag the car seat was in got completely torn at the bottom and the car seat inside got scratched too. Imagine being this careless with an infant car seat!!

We packed our Peg Perego/Agio baby car seat in a bag which has proper handles to allow baggage handlers to carry the car seat safely, handed it to Indigo at the gate. The bag was badly torn(not usable anymore) at the bottom and the car seat present inside scratched when we received it at the destination.

The bag which holds the car seat itself was expensive and was not a flimsy one which would have gotten easily torn unless it was handled badly. We use the bag which is a manufacturer designed travel accessory for the car seat exclusively for checking the car seat while boarding flights and have been in 6 flights so far without any issues. How hard would it have been for Indigo to carry a car seat that was properly packed into a bag with proper handles? We are thankful that we did not hand Indigo the car seat without a bag which ended up saving our more expensive car seat from damage than just some scratches.

We made Indigo aware of this issue after we got down and collected the item at VTZ. Without trying to understand the extent of the damage, she blindly offered 500 rupees. We did not accept since just the bag alone costs 10 times more. She also tried to push blame on us that the bag was not strong enough. We left the airport since we disagreed with her 500 rupees offer and did not know what else to do. 

Agent used our lack of knowledge and did not mention that the correct process is for us file a Property Irregularity Report (PIR) with her and use the PIR to later submit a claim to Indigo later. Leaving the airport without PIR means you accept that you received everything in good condition and cannot hold Indigo liable anymore.

Indigo failed twice, was careless with sensitive luggage items like a car seat, and could not offer a fair resolution. Indigo has not trained their employees to treat sensitive items properly. I can't imagine what anyone would do with damaged car seats when going to a new place. 

DGCA sent out a circular in Feb 2022 asking airlines to allow infants to be seated in CRS for their safety instead of being held in lap. Usage of CRS while flying will become more common shortly once passengers are allowed to board the plane with a car seat. Please do not trust Indigo with handling parts like strollers and look for other options when you have to fly with car seats and strollers. Indigo will carelessly throw them around in a rush to keep their schedule on-time.

I had booked Indigo Airlines to fly from Coimbatore to Delhi so that I can then take another flight (Air India) from Delhi to Toronto. Since I had 2 bags with me (23kg and 9kg) that I had to check-in, I used their pre-paid baggage service to:

title: Tech & Service
text:
So what happened today, 

I did my web check-in. Skipped the seats. 
As seats are auto-assigned a few hours before the boarding, the boarding pass is also auto-generated at that time. 

So I got the boarding pass in the app( for Dehradun to Delhi), as per the process. Satisfied. 

FYI  I had a Flight from Dehradun to Indore, connecting via Delhi. 

I cleared the security check, also while boarding they scanned the boarding pass and allowed me through the gate. 

Well as I was about to enter the plane and opened my app to show my boarding pass(BP) to the lady who was cross-checking the BP. The BP disappeared. 

And I didn't even had the BP in my mail. 

Its 7 AM in the morning, and I was asked to get out of the queue and the back door was closed.

As the plane landed in IGI T3 at 8. I recalled the incident and wondered if the same had have happened with DEL-IDR flight. 
I immediately called support where an executive quickly picked up the call and asked what was my concern. 

Now I told him that I am not able to web check in. 
Which I was not. Quoting the same situation as before, I didn't select the seat, and BP was supposed to be auto-generated. Which didn't this time. 

He asked me to be on hold, I agreed and he came back in 2 minutes and mentioned that "your web check in is already been done.  We can't do it again."
I asked the person to provide me BP as I have a flight to catch in the next 1 hour. 

The person mailed me the itineraries and assured me that I will receive the same in the next few minutes. I asked him to send me the BP, he again sent me the itineraries.
I asked him to be on the call as he was mentioning that he has sent the details. And I was confirming the same. In the end, he blaimed me quoting, first I asked for web check-in, which was not the case, now I am asking for BP. 
He mentioned that he will not be able to help me. I asked him to provide BP in mail or transfer the call to the senior. (Till this time I reached the domestic transfer gate)
The support executive put my call on a blank note where no one replied. 
I was asked by the incharge in the domestic transfer gate to check with the Indigo counter by just taking the right(it was approx 200m) 

I took the right was confused about where I had to go, a indigo employee passing by helped me with the same. 

As I reached the counter, in a very bad note I complained about the situation to the person. There were 3 staff member(1 Male & 2 Female).

I was addressed by a person who immediately understood my situation and directly refered me to a counter and asked the lady at the counter to help me with BP generation.

title: Flouting safety rules/advisories for passengers
text:
Don't fly with Indigo if you care for your infant's life.

I travelled BLR-DOH with my infant. After boarding, I was shocked to know that they do not provide any kind of Child Restraint System (belt etc) for infants. When I asked the attendants how am I supposed to secure my infant in case of emergency, I was told that I should hold her with my hands. Does Indigo understand how senseless this is? Going by that logic, why should adults wear seat belts if they can hold themselves in an emergency?

The DGCA of India has issued an advisory that airlines must provide Child Restraint Systems (CRS) for infants as it's extremely unsafe to travel without CRS . Since this flight was operating in international airspace, they are bound to follow these laws (both at European and Qatari airspace). Providing CRS is something standard across various airlines across the world. This is something airlines provide out of their concern for the safety of their passengers regardless of the laws.

I would never recommend anybody with an infant to travel with Indigo. Every life is precious and any airline claiming "safety first" needs to understand that.

@Indigo, if you can give me here one rational reason for not providing CRS for infants that do not compromise the safety, I would take back this criticizing review.

title: I was denied boarding
text:
I was denied boarding at the gate because of a confused crew. I was a transit passenger with a connecting flight leaving Delhi in 4 hours, fully booked. They said, "whoever flies on Indian airlines should have a visa, even if they don't leave the terminal and do not pass through the immigration." Are you kidding me, Indigo? I was supposed to reach terminal 3 and my connecting flight was also from the same terminal. Whatever I said to the crew just fell on deaf ears. 

I only had carry on luggage and I was going to stay at the transfer area for my connecting flight. I have never experienced or heard of an airline which bounces transfer passenger because they don't have a visa for the connecting airline. 

The entry rule is supposed to apply only for the final destination, in this case, which will be my home country (South Korea) and not the connecting country unless you want to pass through the immigration and enter the country. The crew kept me waiting on the sideline and only informed me of this decision a minute before they closed the gate. 

Let's assume that the guy's correct, how come I have never been informed of such ridiculous rule until I reach the gate? I went to the Indigo website and Delhi airport website, to see if such warning or rule exists - of course, no!

I missed my connecting flight and now I have to stay in the airport over 20 hours for a new flight I booked with a different airline. I had to get my new PCR (yeah, S.Korea still requires it) test inside of the airport. All in all, this had costed me more than 2,000 dollars for just a one-way flight and a day completely wasted. The most horrendous experience, ever, because of a confused crew.

I filed a complaint - which I highly doubt they would ever read it or care - to Indigo and also consulted my consulate office. I will take whatever legal actions necessary to receive an official apology.

title: Our family trip to Andaman with Indigo
text:
I have never travelled in a lot of budget airlines and generally try to aviod them due to the hassel of many hidden charges and T&C's... however, for this trip we were left  out of option as the itenary of Indigo was best suited for ourtrip.

At the start it did not go well as the mandatory chekcing policy ment we had to check in between 24 to 2 hrs before flying for which we needed to select a seat however, 14 hrs prior there were no free seats on offer on both our sectors reaching Portblair. This was not a fair play from the airline and the customer service was nto helpful. We had to coughup another 1000.00 INR just to ensure we the 3 of us which included our 4yrs son sit together. I was really repenting my decission to select this airling at this point. 

At the airport the checking Kiasok was not helpful as they could only print one baggange tag and we were asked to go to the long que. After insisting we were heped to a shortcut to the checking counter as we already had our boarding cards.

It is here that we meet a very understanding and helpful Indigo ambassador, she basically changed my opinion about the airline. Ms. Kadambari. She appologised for the issue and did affirm our feeling of being taking for a ride by the system. She was kind to block us seats for our return journey and did a speed checking. 

In the aircraft we did notice some great personalities overall. However there are still inconsistencies in this. Some crew members dont like to smile or welcome which is a sign of missing basic hospitality. This was our experience in particular with Ms. Shushmita a crew member on flight from Chennai to Portblair on 12th May. May be she was over worked or just not in mood to be pleasent on duty.

Overall I think the airline can do much better with more emphasis on fair trade practices, there is nothing worng for a business to make money but it shoud be made in a integrate manner. Secondly they really need to improve their crew service consistency. just because passangers are flying on budget does not mean they deserve any less hospitality. That is keeping the crews job in the first place. Indigo should have more service audits and crew motivation to improve their engagement.

My overall experience was good and most importantly we felt safe as most of the aircrafts were new and well maintained from my passengers eye. I will consider flying Indigo again, but please fix the smaller issues to make it more customer friendly.

1. Always checkin online/web before reaching airport and print the boarding pass, without boarding pass you will not be allowed to enter into the airport (this was a shock to me)
2. Book and pay for luggage to save money, if you have any, before reaching airport
3. Talk to customer care before reaching airport, all the services are charged when you get at airport - that's how they make money
4. Always arrive little early to avoid last minute rush
5. Eat/drink at the airport before you board the plane to save money on plane.

I found IndiGo customer care better than many major airlines, they solved my issues over the phone so no complaints.

I would definitely fly IndiGo again if need to.

text:

Seat number 2D offers a great view of professionalism at play. Along the 2 and a half hour journey, Bharti and Yogyata were waltzing around wrapping up one task after another. Bharti's fingers glide through a big flat screen TV with the finesse of a fine artist. Yogyata has a certain purpose in her walk. Together, they're enough. title: Instead of lean clean flying machine, they should be called cheat, cheap, mean flying machine.
text:
For sure never booking a flight with indigo for international travel again. They should stick to domestic flights in my opinion, as even the airport personnel’s referred to them as some low standard airline when asked, why people prefer emirates or fly dubai indigo  while traveling to and from dubai. 
Had various reasons to come to such a conclusion and specially when i have been a frequent flyer with them over the past decade. 

At first, paid extra for some flexi package, which other than one ready to eat, add hot water kind meal, doesn’t carry any other advantage to be honest.
Had pre-booked a sesame chicken and rice noodle salad, which while opening had an off smell to it and the chicken was as hard as a used Goodyear tyre. 
And to be noted that the total difference between an emirates flight and indigo flight is just 200 AED.
The only good thing about the deal was maybe getting a hot beverage included. In the meal. 100% hygiene and 100% taste as mentioned over the packaging was maybe questionable too. 

Second, even after confirming the baggage allowance from indigo helpline, was informed that i can carry 30 kg in total as a checkin baggage and can hand carry a 7kg bag plus a laptop bag upto 3 kg. I understand that that its my fault that i didn’t confirm, if that includes the duty free purchases as well, hence was asked to pay 240 AED extra  just exactly at the boarding gate when the boarding had already begun. I would have adjusted the same in my checkin baggage, where in I had only put 22kg, if informed in time or while checking in the bags. 

After talking to the officer asking me to pay extra, i was advised to either pay extra or return the purchases and get the refund from the duty free shops, which was not possible as all of this was happening last moment. 
So, as i had no other option available, I agreed to pay 240 AED extra which could totally be avoided if i was informed during baggage checkin. Also, note that in the past 10 years of my travel history, it was the first time my checkin baggage was checked for weight or charged. Even till this i had no problem as I accept it as my negligence too. 
Over and above that, just at the flight’s door, i am asked to remove all the valuables from the hand baggage as they will be keeping the hand baggage along with the checkin baggage as they ran out of space in the overhead cabins to store our bags, at which i almost lost it. 
So due to a miss communication, I had paid extra to keep my baggage with me, just so that i will be asked to transfer the same with my checkin baggage where i already have 8kg vacant space available. 
And all of this is played very smartly, specially last moment so that the Coustomer is left with no other option but to pay for carrying the same 40 kg in total, as initially allotted, just in the name of a hand baggage which is again treated as a checkin baggage by the end. 
And on asking the authorities regulating this whole drama, i was told that these are airline policies and the people charging for the same are just the mediators. 

So in short i had paid the same amount, that I would have paid for a comfortable seat in a world class airline with similar baggage allowance, more humble and informative staff, better meal and a hustle free travel experience all together. 
So kudos to team indigo for losing a Coustomer forever and i am sure many more to be lost everyday due to such incidents. No wonder even the staff is sure that they can never be as big as a their competitive airliners.

And no, i am not doing this to get a refund or an email from team indigo. Being a part of the hospitality industry from the past decade, thought of informing the fellow travellers about the incident and that it is not fair and not to fall for such tricks. 

The worst ever experience flying international with Indigo airlines.

text:

I've travelled throughout covid and Nepal was the first country I went to requiring an exit test. Any other airline would have sent an email letting their customers know, but not IndiGo. I flew the next day Kathmandu to Chennai -(aftrr paying 10000 rupees fare difference), with a short layover in Delhi. I was assured by IndiGo staff at check in that my bag would go straight through to Chennai, and they put Chennai as the final destination on the baggage ticket, so there was no reason for me to go to baggage collection in Delhi. Upon arrival in Chennai at 1am after a delayed departure, I was told my bag hadn't arrived because I was supposed to have cleared customs at Delhi Airport. 

It's now been 3 days, my bag is still in Delhi and IndiGo have no idea what's going on. They don't even know the right number to call at Delhi Airport to get an update.

At the end of the day, fly IndiGo if you want a cheap flight and can count on things going according to plan, but don't expect any support if there are any disruptions as they don't appear to have the customer's best interests at heart.

Pathetic airline, the worst way of flying internationally is via the one and only Indigo. 

Unfortunately my flight via another airline Go first from Colombo to Delhi got cancelled and I had to book another flight on the same day. Indigo was the only option available and it wasn't a direct flight.

When we asked them to check-in the third bag, again weighing just 6kg - the answer is no, we only allow 2 bags for check-in. As if 35kg check-in is such a big problem.

Then I heard the cabin crew talking about a very interesting fact. The aircraft had 39 rows of seats - normally an aircraft would have 30 seats. How did they fake out extra 9 rows? Simple. Do not provide any god-damned leg space whatsoever. Plus they had removed the lavatories from the end of the aircraft that allowed space for more seats. Unbelievable these people are.

Then the crew doesn't accept debit cards for payment. Why? Coz they do not want to miss a single opportunity to piss the customer.

Last but definitely not the least, on arrival our bags were supposed to be on belt 6 but later they changed to belt 1. Ok fine. Then all of a sudden, some bags started to come out from belt 2. Why? 
Belt 1 was still having bags from another flight from HyD. So now our bags were on 2 different belts. 
The bags took forever to come out and in the process, the 3rd flight from Kochi landed in Delhi and guess where the bags were getting offloaded? Belt 1 once again. So now belt 1 had bags of 3 different flights - Hyd and Kochi as we as our flight. What a super mess.

Indigo has ruined the entire T2 at Delhi airport. I thought since T2 is new, it would be atleast at par with T3, is not better, but its a complete distaster, probably worse than T1.

Don't ever book an international flight via Indigo. And if possible, never book a domestic flight too.

title: Bad experience and no value for extra money paid
text:
My wife and I (Senior Citizens) travelled from Chennai to Male by Indigo Flight from Chennai to Male via Bangalore on 8th August, 2021.  We were given a Through Boarding Pass to Male issued at Chennai after verifying all the documents.  At Bangalore, there was no one to direct Transit passengers like us from Indigo. We went to the Departure Immigration counters and then were tolfd to get our tickets stamped at the Departure Counter of Indigo at Bangalore. This is  far away from the Emigration Counter and we had to run with hand baggage and get back to be in time. We had also to represent all our documents for verification. We were never informed about this earlier. 
The Baggage Policy of Indigo Airlines is kept vague just to make sure that they can charge what they want. We had prepaid Rs.10,500 for 2 pieces of Excess Baggage for 10 Kgs, the Free Allowance.  At the check in counter we were told that we could take up to 4 pieces of baggage. For international travel with a Through Boarding Pass, 4 pieces is normally allowed of at least 20 Kgs should be allowed.  This is excess baggage charges to profiteer by keeping the policy vague. 
We had paid Rs.4400/- extra for our seats to be given on the first row. When we boarded at Bangalore, we had each one piece of hand baggage as per international norms. But we found that other passengers with multiple pieces had occupied the storage cabin above our seats. Our baggage was offloaded and made into check in baggage. When we had paid extra for our seats, our hand baggage should have been kept in the cabin above our seats. We were promised by the crew that the hand baggage would be handed over to us the moment we landed at Male. Instead it was sent along with the other Checked in Baggage. We could not access it as it was beyond Immigration Counters We were without papers like Maldives Travellers Health Declaration Form, Covid Test Certificate , Proof of place of Stay when we landed at Male Immigration. We would have been deported as illegal travellers. Luckily the passports were with us.  Somehow, we managed to convince the Maldivian authorities and were permitted to enter. No none from Indigo came to help us get our hand baggage so that we could show our papers to the authorities. We were in danger of detention due to the Indigo staff not bothering to fulfil their words. We have shared our experiences so that other Indian passengers can be careful and avoid the pitfalls and bad experience which we had.

title: Extortion of stranded passengers
text:
Scheduled departure time was 12.30pm on 1st September, 2021. It  rained heavily that morning. in fact, as per records. it was the heaviest rain in last 19 years!. We got stuck in the traffic for more than 2.30 hours and reached the counter at 12.20 and understandably  not expecting to board. At the counter after 10 minutes wait were told flight has taken off. we asked for assistance and were guided to Counter No. 1 and then the extortion process started. 
Girl at the counter offered next flight at 18.10PM and said we need to pay differential of INR 7000 for 2 tickets. We were surprised as the regular fare on an average was INR 3400 to 3600. We moved away from the counter and went online and the fare online was 3600! Went back to the counter and showed her the online fare. Her reply on seeing it was " I said INR 6000"!!
We realized we are subject to unfair practice and she is taking advantage of stranded passengers and once again moved away from the counter and contacted the manager and explained the situation and Traffic chaos we went through. He went to the counter1 and explained to her and asked us to now pay INR 1800 each. We reluctantly paid and booked the flight which was from other terminal. Then came the 2nd extortion attempt. She refused to issue the boarding passes and asked us to go online for web-check in. We explained "we are at the counter and after having gone through the ordeal least we can expect is the boarding passes" Her response " you need to pay INR 100 each" We had an unpleasant interaction for couple of minutes.  By now some other passengers standing around were also bit surprised and told her that it is not fair. Realising she is being unreasonable, In a huff she pressed a button on her system and printed the boarding passes, threw them on the counter, closed the counter and walked away. This is how the leading airline in India take advantage of stranded passengers. Also it came as a additional shock when we went online to check actual departure of our original flight and noticed it left at 13.20 against scheduled time of 12.30 pm. We were definitely late but have a feeling that with little support from the ground staff could have boarded our original flight. Any how, the grievance is with regard to extortion practice followed by the airline  which I have never experienced  travelling worldwide for more than 40 years!!
It is a fit case for the MInistry of Civil Aviation to investigate and take suitable action.

title: Great Experience (Delhi -Malé - Delhi)
text:
Trip Report - IndiGo - DEL>< MLE - 6AUG and 10AUG

Our flight to Malé was on 6th August from Delhi T3. While our IndiGo ticket mentioned T1, please do note that all International flights from Delhi operate from T3.

We entered the airport around 6:45 AM from Gate 6 which was relatively empty. In case you have a domestic flight even then you can enter from this Gate as it is always empty.

We reached Island M where IndiGo was doing check-in for Malé. There was strict paper work checking being done by the Ground Staff team able headed by Amitava. He was flooded with queries but he kept his calm and assisted all passengers. Please do read all travel guidelines carefully while planning the trip and carry necessary documents in print as it saves a lot of time of the airline staff as well as passenger.

After a smooth check-in we headed for Immigration and Security Check, both were less crowded and we were done in 15 minutes.

For breakfast we decided to head to Plaza Premium Lounge. Do check if your credit card offers Lounge access at International Terminal as mine didn't (Citibank Premiermiles) but thankfully I had other cards. The lounge was well sanitised and the buffet spread was very impressive. A quick bite and we were off to the Gate.

Boarding was well on time and we took-off a few minutes prior to ETD, to what they call IndiGo Standard Time.

I made the Bookings in FlexiFare under which I got 50% off on seat selection. It is advised to select seats with extra legroom as the 4 hr flight can be tiring with regular legroom. I booked the 1st row which was very comfortable. Our booking also included free meal so we opted for IndiGo's famous Upma and Poha.

Unfortunately due to extreme weather at Malé, we were diverted to Cochin. Upon landing in Cochin the GS there came into action and brought snacks for all passengers. Due to refuelling and a change in operating + cabin crew, we were on ground for about 2 hrs. Amidst all this, the crew kept circulating water and also gave regular updates which was very satisfying.

Finally we landed in Malé after a delay of 04 hrs due to extreme weather. Malé airport is being renovated hence all arrivals were at remote bay. Coaches were used to transfer passengers from ramp to the arrival building. Upon entering there was regular temperature check followed by Immigration. Please do complete all pre-departure formalities before landing in Malé. A quick stamp on the passport and we were out within 45 min of arrival.

All in all a good experience with IndiGo.

title: Worst Experience with Indigo at Jaipur Airport
text:
Hi,
I am Ashay Gaur. I booked Indigo flight for my journey Jaipur to Delhi on 19th Feb 2021 with PNR TLIPVJ, flight no being 6E 203. For 270 kms from Jaipur to Delhi which can be covered even by road (spending Taxi fare of INR 3600), I deliberately chose to fly by Indigo spending INR 13104 for myself and my family. My reason for travel by air instead of road was:-
a) Safety from Covid as I found cabs in Jaipur and Delhi not taking adequate sanitization precautions 
b) discomfort and fatigue caused by road travel 
c) delay caused by Kisan Aandolan on Jaipur Delhi highway 
d) had to catch another international flight from Delhi to Bahrain for which my reporting time was 7:00 pm on 19th Feb 2021.  
Above reasons prompted me to book air travel even though it was so expensive as compared to road travel. On the morning of 19th Feb 2021, like a prompt passenger, I reached Jaipur Airport at 9:30 am to catch my Indigo flight to Delhi at 12:15 pm. However, I was told by Indigo staff that the flight was delayed, and that the revised departure is 12:50 pm. Then I was told that the revised departure is 01:45 pm. After half an hour on further enquiry, I was told that the revised departure time is 04:35 pm which later became 05:00 pm and then again 05:15 pm (I have all messages stored with me which I Kept receiving from Indigo). During all this time with constant hecklings with Indigo staff at Jaipur Airport, I got perturbed as I had to catch another connecting international flight from Delhi to Bahrain. I kept requesting the Indigo staff at Jaipur Airport that I cannot afford to lose my international flight from Delhi as road travel takes at least 6 to 8 hours to reach to Delhi Airport. Surbhi, Harsh, Shiv, Ramya, Monarch, Khushboo are the names I remember on duty at Jaipur Airport for Indigo on 19th Feb 2021. At 2:00 pm, coolly, I am told by these people that I can take full refund and can go by road. I was like are you people out of your minds? Or have gone insane? Have I not been telling you that I have a connecting international flight from Delhi for which I am supposed to report by 7:00 pm. How on earth will I travel by road and reach there by 7:00 pm if I start at 2:00 pm. I got no absolute answer. For your information, I was doing my parallel enquiry with someone known at Delhi Airport who told that flight 6E 203 was to come from Dehradhun and the same flight was supposed to fly to Delhi and thereafter to Jaipur. However, this flight had not flown only from Dehradhun even at 01:30 pm. This fact was completely hidden from me by Indigo staff who kept telling flight is delayed due to bad weather condition at Delhi Airport. Seriously? Delhi weather was bright and clear that day. I later also realized that Jaipur Airport remains shut for runway maintenance from 2:00 pm to 04:30 pm which is why probably the flight was further delayed till 05:15 pm. If I were kept abreast of all these developments, I would have not reversed my decision of going by road, right? But in that panicking situation with lackadaisical approach to handle my request, I was forced to take a decision at 2:25 pm, to travel by road as Indigo staff was giving me lame excuses and no certain answer. I appeal to the reader of this complaint, what would a sane person do when he has a connecting international flight scheduled from Delhi after 7-8 hours (which I booked with sufficient margin) and he is constantly being told by Indigo staff that Jaipur to Delhi flight is being delayed after lapse of every half an hour. Would he not be in panicking situation? I stood to lose INR 1 lac at 2:25 pm for my further travel from Delhi to Bahrain. Indigo staff just brushed me aside telling you can take full refund. They even delayed in giving me back my luggage (when I was forced by them to take a decision to travel by road) which was taken earlier for check-in. Is that an answer to a harried passenger standing to lose his international travel? Further the airport cab took full advantage of my precarious situation and demanded INR 7000 (double the cost of normal cab fare) for travelling by road from Jaipur to Delhi Airport. In this entire episode, Indigo staff mishandled and I hold them responsible for the following:-
1.	Suppressing the facts from me and forcing me travel by road instead of my pre booked air travel at such high fare of INR 13,104. 
2.	Putting my family at complete distress by travel through road. My wife is still recovering from post-delivery back aches and other personal undisclosable problems. 
3.	Forcing me to book a shady airport cab with no hygiene and sanitary precautions.
4.	Financial loss to me to book a cab from Jaipur to Delhi Airport at INR 7000 when the normal cab fare to Delhi airport costs just INR 3600
5.	In my entire road travel to Delhi Airport I was so stressed that it gave me panic attacks, undue anxiety and fear of monetary loss of INR 1 lac (international travel cost). Further after reaching to Delhi Airport at 8:30 pm, I had to literally beg Air India to allow me to board the flight. It was all due to Indigo staff’s utter mishandling of a passenger’s request which caused me public humiliation and disrespect even at Delhi Airport before Air India staff (my travel partner from Delhi to Bahrain). 
I claim compensation from Indigo which brought me hardship, panic attacks, headache, stress, anxiety, public humiliation and disrespect at Delhi Airport also due to Indigo’s mistake at Jaipur Airport. 
Further, after this incidence at Jaipur Airport, while I was boarding the Cab to reach to Delhi Airport, I received a call from Mr Osama from Guest Experience and Feedback to whom I narrated the entire incidence. I was assured by him that I will receive my entire refund within 48 hours and that in half an hour I will again receive a call from Customer Care of Indigo to adequately address my grievance on this entire incidence narrated above. Well, neither the refund came nor did any call come. I have reached Bahrain now and would be unable to take any calls from India. I have waited enough for a day and time has come for me to act in writing through social media, Twitter, aviation regulator DGCA, consumer dispute redressal forums and various other platforms that I can get hold of. My email id is ashay.sbi@gmail.com and I am reachable only though watsapp number +91-9538082418. 
Ashay Gaur

title: Indigo during COVID-19 Pandemic Crisis
text: I just want to take the time to give some positive customer feedback during this pandemic crisis. We had our holiday booked to India for the end of March/April 2020 - during which the Indian government suspended all foreign visas to try and contain coronavirus. Obviously it was a huge disappointment and hassle for us trying to contact everyone to get flights, accommodation and tours cancelled. But I have to say, my experience with Indigo customer service was phenomenal. After eventually getting through to them (which understandably took a few days because of the thousands of people like me), they were so quick to help to rectify the situation. They provided a refund with no problem after receiving all of our travel information. Indigo was one of our best experiences to date with customer service, and we look forward to taking Indigo flights later in 2019 after COVID-19 has subsided. Rest assured when booking with them, that if anything goes haywire, they’ll be happy to help.

title: Updated Foreign Travelers Beware
text:
I bought round trip tickets for the final leg of our trip from Delhi to Jammu online. I was traveling with my wife, my 2 year old son and my 70 year old mother from Los Angeles California. The first leg of our journey from Delhi to Jammu was delayed 4 hours. On our return flight from Jammu to Dehli, we checked in online the night before. When we arrived at the airport, we were told that even though our reservations said 2/14/20 and our confirmation said 2/14/20 they had us in the system as 3/14/20. We were told not to worry they would figure something out. Then we were told they had no room on the flight and it was the last flight that night, we would have to take the next available flight the following day. We informed them this would make us miss our international flight. After some discussion, with zero responsibility taken on their end, they offered to sell us tickets on the flight we had already booked, checked into and thought we were taking, but then told was booked solid. The price you may ask.....70,000 indian rupees, roughly $1,000 US dollars for a one way ticket. The original round trip was $475 US dollars. Since we were in a bind and recieved no help from the airline we decided to pay and deal with the issue after. So, we offered to pay with our AMEX, but were told, unfortunately, these tickets could only be purchased with cash (shady)... We go to India every year to visit family, this is the first time we have used Indigo and have never felt so taken advantage of. We ended up paying three times what our agreed upon rate was, given zero options, offered zero customer service (the whole conversation was basically focused on how we were stuck), until ultimately we were extorted for money which was only payable in cash.I would not recommend this airline to anyone with a foreign passport as they definitely took advantage of me, I would not recommend this to anyone with an Indian passport similar to my wife either. They could have acknowledged their mistake rather than dig their heels in and refuse to accept responsibility. Further more, they could have told us there was a mix up and charged us the difference in the flight cost between 2/14/20 and 3/14/20 if there was one at the minimum. They took it to the extreme and capitalized on the fact that we were foriegn, honest and in a bind by price gouging us and then expecting payment in cash which is not traceable and ultimately made us feel like we had really been taken advantage of. Please, Fly with this airline at your own risk and be prepared for delays, poor service and to be taken advantage of.

After responding to a request from here to reach out to customer service, I recieved the below response. Notice there is no attempt at offering an apology.

Dear Sir/Ma'am,

 

Thank you for writing to IndiGo.

 

With reference to your mail, we would like to inform you that reservation under PNR XGH36C for flight 6E 535 was booked by the passenger for 14th March 2020, instead of 14th February 2020 from Jammu to Delhi.

 

Further, our airport team tried to assist the passenger and gave them the option of rebooking their travel to 15th Feb'20 with applicable charges however this option was declined by the passenger since they were travelling further to an International destination on 15th Feb'20 so it was very important for them to travel the very same day.

 

As no other flight was available for any other airline also thus our team made a new reservation for 14th Feb'20 under PNR CD37HL and as the fares are dynamic in nature so the passenger was booked at the available fares.

 

Further, our team advised passenger to get his reservation cancelled for 14th March 2020 which is still active.

Also, please see our attached picture of flight confirmation.

title: Absolutely incredible travel experience
text:
Indigo flight 

On the 19th of December I had the incredible pleasure of travelling on what would rank as one of my best domestic travel experience in a long time. 

Heading to Delhi from Bangalore along with my better half, we travelled on Indigo flight     . The entire process from the time we reached the indigo counters in Bangalore till the time we left Delhi’s terminal 2, was outstanding and the credit goes to indigo.  

I shall recount the process step by step. 

The staff at the counters were incredibly helpful and patient despite a huge throng of passengers lining up to travel to various destinations. Since ours was a standby ticket and we were early we were asked to wait and report back at a certain time. We strolled out to get a coffee and were pleasantly surprised to get a call from the counter to report back a few minutes before the stipulated time to collect our boarding cards which were handed over with a smile. 

We proceeded to the  boarding gate which again was as seamless as the counter experience. 

We were greeted on board by a very pleasant set of crew who would thereafter continue to impress by their charm and service throughout the flight. . A flight attendant is primarily onboard for our safety. Hospitality is a secondary role. Most fulfill that either reasonably well or go about it as a mundane task. To carry out your responsibilities with flair and grace throughout a 2 hour 45 minute flight and still have the energy to wish everyone farewell with warm and pleasant smile is the hallmark of outstanding crew. My compliments to the Lead Crew Shobhna and her team, especially Sonia. 

I heard a new announcement by the crew which I feel is much needed in our skies. As we taxied in the crew requested everyone to have the courtesy to allow the passengers seated in the row preceding theirs to deplane first. A majority of the travelling public in India lacks this common sense. This announcement is a great step in educating the frequent traveller in basic travelling etiquette. Despite this announcement, some educated men and women failed to exhibit this courtesy. I guess it will take a long while for people to change. Hats off to you Indigo, for taking this first proactive step. 

Kudos to Capt Jumbunathan for a superb flight and his outstanding PAs. No airline in India carries out specific training tailored towards making passenger announcements despite English not being the first language for most pilots. At best there are mediocre written guidelines that sound either boring or too technical for most of the travelling public. To have the confidence to make your own PA which sounds way better then the drab guidelines and have the perfect oratory skill to follow it through is indeed an achievement. Volume, diction and pace of speech were perfect. Both the welcome announcement and the announcement prior to our arrival into Delhi rank as amongst the best I have heard flying the indian skies. The icing on the cake was a terrific landing into Delhi. Well done Capt     I will looking forward to flying with you again. 

The inflight magazine is a great mix of interesting articles as well information on the airline itself. A special mention about the article on the Vice President Operations, Capt Ashim Mitra who hung up his flying boots on the 9th of December after an illustrious flying career. Hats off to you Sir, for creating such an incredible culture in your airline as well as having an incredible open door policy which makes you very approachable to your team, a feat few airlines can boast of. Wish you many more years of this incredible leadership.

title: Sick, pathetic, they will let you down!
text:
I and my family had booked a ticket on Indigo to travel  on Sunday 29th December 2019 from Varanasi to Kolkata.
On 28th December Saturday 9pm, I was informed by an SMS that the flight had been cancelled due to forecasted bad weather. I was very perplexed and called up Indigo to reschedule my flight. They confirmed that it was indeed due to forecasted bad weather at Varanasi that the flight was cancelled. I desperately needed to travel on 29th or at least by 30th early morning. They informed me that on 29th they were no other flights available so they could reschedule me only on 30th, and that too the only flight they could give me was in the late evening flight from Varanasi at 7pm. I fervently  requested them to provide me an alternative arrangement for 29th even if it was a hopping flight via Delhi, Gaya or any other place which they refused to do citing nonavailability of seats. however nothing was available.
 I was forced subsequently to book tickets for me and my family at a much higher price on a hopping flight on Vistara which was Varanasi - Delhi - Delhi - Kolkata on 29th evening (6:15pm departure from Varanasi and arrival at Kolkata at 10:25 pm).
On reaching the airport on 29th to avail my Vistara flight I was very surprised to see that every other airline was flying out of Varanasi with no evidence of any bad weather what so ever at Varanasi airport. Also three other Indigo flights (6E 6913, 6635 &  499) were also operating. 
On our flight on vistara Varanasi- delhi - Kolkata , we did not find any bad weather or any such disruption.
So it was very clear that weather was not the issue.It is my strong suspicion that Indigo canceled the flight because it was either not cost-effective for them or they had problems with their engines (which has been there in the press recently).
No compensation given. I was totally taken aback by their attitude and was extremely sad to totally let down.

title: Terrible lost luggage handling (Nightmare)
text:
I was traveling through Indigo on 14/01/2020 by 6E7143, from Chennai to Tiruchirappalli. I was going on a temple visit and took a hotel near Tanjore. When we landed, we were informed that due to heavy luggage booking due to transit from international passengers, our luggages were left in Chennai. There are many passengers started shouting. The supervisor (Mr. Ramesh) along with his staffs assuring that the luggages will come in next flight (afternoon) and will be handed over to your house or hotel wherever it may be. After listening to his promise, I signed the form and took his number and went to temples. I also took one more number from the staff. I was keep talking to him and he kept on giving assurances. After temple visits, I reached my hotel near Tanjore at round 5pm and did not receive my luggage from Indigo. I again contacted Ramesh, he mentioned that the luggage is coming by 4pm flight and will reach my hotel by max 7.30pm. Again after couple of phone calls, he assured the luggage is seen by him physically and boarded into a car that is coming to my hotel. Then I called the other number I picked up, to my surprise, I was told  that my luggage is now only coming from Chennai by road and will reach my hotel either by mid-night or in the morning. I got furious and called Ramesh, to my surprise, he mentioned that communication is a wrong one and he again confirmed my luggage is already left trichy airport and will reach by max 8pm. When I tried contacting him by 8pm, his mobile got switched off. Then, i dialled toll free number and registered a complaint on my lost luggage. To my shocking, there is no registration of lost luggage against my PNR is registered. By 11.30pm, i got a call from a driver that he has picked up my luggage from Trichy airport and will reach hotel by mid-night. After several follow-up, the driver finally delivered my luggage by 01.30am of 15/01/2020. I lost my sleep, coule not visit few temples scheduled on 14th even and 15th morning. The following are my concerns.
1. Without my consent, Indigo retained my luggage at Chennai.
2. No proper information. Ramesh who was the supervisor is a liar. Made all sort of promises. I don't think so, Indigo will take any action against him. 
3. They don't have any proper process on lost luggage handling. 
4. When luggage is lost there is no one will give proper response.
5. There will be no "Sorry" or any apology from Indigo. Such an arrogant airlines.  
6. This is my experience, I think the other passengers also would have been troubled this much. One of the passenger informed me during our interaction while filling the form that, this is not the first case for them in Indigo. They have already experienced the same and regret taking Indigo again. 
My recommendation is to avoid Indigo in case you have other alternative airlines. One of the worst and unfriendly airline. Pls avoid.

The Airline kept us abreast with the reason of delay and likely ETD from time to time by emails and sms, and hence we had no anxiety and were well prepared for the delay which was beyond the control of the Airline. On request my 95 years old Dad was provided a wheelchair at both the enplaning and deplaning stations. The Staff was very courteous. We had a pleasant Flight and the Cabin Crew was very courteous and caring. Hot Masala Tea we bought was really hot and nice and my Dad and I really relished it with potato veg stuffed rolled paranthas we had carried with us from Hyderabad. Before we landed at Chandigarh the Captain announced that the temp at Chandigarh was 22 Degrees and we were well clad to deplane in such a cold weather. The Flight reached Chandigarh at 16.00 hrs and a wheelchair with an Attendant was waiting for my Father. It was an excellent Flight and we are glad we travelled by Indigo which took grat of my Dad and me. Thank You Captain and Staff of Indigo Flight 6E 269 for letting us have such a pleasant experience.

title: Poor review that could have been avoided
text:
During our trip to India we flew twice on Indigo Air. I understood when booking that this was a budget airline and didn’t expect a great deal. Our first flight from Jaipur to Varanasi went smoothly running late by about 15 minutes. Our second trip from Varanasi however was a different story. This was the last trip out of India to Bangkok for us. Due to the fog the plane was delayed 6 hours which is out of anyone’s control. After 31/2 hours of delay the airline provided us with a small warm lunch which I ate and then just before boarding we were given the same food again in small containers which was supposedly dinner. The second offering was cold and I didn’t eat it, firstly because it had been sitting for many hours in containers and secondly because it was cold. We had left our accommodation at 730am and it was 10 hours later and so I was feeling hungry. When we finally boarded the aircraft and a trolley was being brought around I asked for a cup of black tea. By this stage I didn’t have any rupees and the hostess said that I had to pay $2 if I wanted a cup - outrageous price even if I had the money. I explained that we had been waiting for over 6 hours but she refused to give me a cup of tea and was quite rude in her response. 
Really Indigo airlines, is it worth a bad review for a measly cup of hot tea? When your customers have waited patiently for a delayed flight, in an airport with limited toilets, food, and chairs to sit down, isn’t it worth providing a hot or cold drink? 
Other than this, the flight was excellent. 
My point - show a little curtesy to your customers when things don’t go to plan - a cup of tea was all it took and understanding from your air hostess.

title: A VERY PLEASANT EXPERIENCE
text:
I have travelled by air about a dozen times in the past three months, but the last Indigo flight which I took from Delhi to Kolkata (6E 615) was probably the best of them. 

Indigo prides itself on its punctuality, but this flight started a bit late. However, the rescheduled time (2050 instead of 2035) was displayed at the entrance of the airport, so I could reach the gate at the appropriate boarding time. The baggage drop was smooth and the security check took less time than expected. 

The flight took off around the rescheduled time. The takeoff was quite smooth. There was a bit of turbulence en route, but this was beyond the control of the airline. 

A copy of the inflight magazine was available in the pocket in front of me, and I flipped through it while waiting for dinner. I had pre-ordered a simple meal of dal-chawal, expecting it to be fresh. I was surprised to find that it was in desiccated form - a plastic box was filled with hot water and I was told to wait exactly 8 minutes. I followed the instructions and found the contents to be delicious. I was also offered a choice of beverages, which I had not expected. The crew were friendly and hospitable - in particular, Nisha took pains to serve the passengers. 

Landing at Kolkata was quite smooth. Two buses were available for the passengers and the luggage was delivered promptly. 

I reached a few minutes later than scheduled, but I will still award 5 stars to Indigo for this journey.

title: Worst 7 hours of flying
text:
It started very well, because from Budapest to Istanbul, the short haul 2 hour flight was perfect. It was smooth, the inflight service was excellent, the food also was exceptional. 
From Istanbul to Delhi it was operated by IndiGo, and it was a nightmare. I booked it because it was an Indian carrier, Alitalia on the same day was almost INR 5000 cheaper, yet I decided to pay more to fly under the Indian Flag. And by the end of it I felt ashamed that not only me the foreigners who were travelling were also humiliated. 
It started with the flight attendants announcing that they will only serve food to those who had pre-booked it else passengers will have to pay for it. As proof they were going to check everyone's boarding pass. And then it all started, the boarding pass did not carry the correct code. I had to prove by showing them my e-ticket, which said meals included. Then they accepted that my meals were included and I was served a sandwich and a juice for dinner. Turkish Airlines which operated the 2 hr segment served 4 course breakfast, that included a loaf of bread with butter and jelly, chicken salad, dessert and drinks. And for the 7 hr long haul with Indigo I had to make do with a sandwich.
When I pay for my meals I expect a meal not a sandwich. Furthermore if you're going to operate a low budget airline, advertise it so, you cannot charge me 500 Euro for a return flight that every other airline is charging and make me sit on a wooden bench for 7 hours, there was no cusions, no inflight entertainment, and they were running 4 shopping trollies on the aisle, people had to wait ages to use the lavatory. 
That was not even the worst part. 
I was sitting next to an Austrian couple, who were not carrying their e-tickets, and even though Turkish served them breakfast on the short haul from Vienna to Istanbul, IndiGo refused to serve them meals. 
It was such a shameful experience for me as an Indian, we believe in "atithi devo bhava" and this airline which is flying the Indian Flag on its crafts is treating our guests as cattles on transport. 
I still have to flyback to Budapest on the 23rd on the same flight, but I'm very sure neither will I ever book indigo again, nor will I ever let anyone. Also i will check 20 times before i book Turkish airlines, because this kind of partner does not reflect well on their customer service either.

title: Delay, Inconvenience, Disappointment and Too Much Hassle
text:
I was travelling to Bhubaneshwar for my friends' wedding on 29th Nov'19 and returning on 2nd Dec'19.

I had booked an Indigo to BBI with a 50 min layover at Kolkata. The flight was scheduled to leave by 4.10 pm. I was always under the impression that Indigo is known for it's punctuality and can be trusted for a layover flight. But I was let down. The next flight from Kolkata was at 7.10. 
The BOM- CCU flight got delayed and finally took off by 5.43pm. Connecting flight also got delayed and rescheduled departure was 8.15pm. I kept asking the Indigo staff whether the next flight would wait , what will be the scenario? All they said was "Don't worry ma'am, it will not take off without you" All fake positive assurances. 

Finally I landed at 7.45pm at Kolkata. All BBI passengers were made to wait outside the aircraft for more than 15 min. Not letting us board the bus to the arrival, despite requesting multiple times so that we could rush in and check about the next flight. 
Ground staff then guided us to Indigo counter at Arrival and there we are handed over new boarding passes of a 10.30pm flight. I was to reach BBI by 8.45pm and now stranded at Kolkata airport. It was bad!! We didn't know about our luggage. It was so chaotic. The staff didn't inform us until we reached the counter that the next flight will fly without taking us.
Reached BBI at 11.37pm with all the possible hassles and inconvenience to others already at BBI waiting for me.

Return flight from BBI to BOM was on time. But, Indigo had to disappoint again this time too. My checked in which I received at Mumbai was completely damaged. The handle was broken and it was too difficult to carry it back. I was left with a new, unexpected expenditure of buying a new bag now. The staff wasn't so supportive and offered meagre 1,000/- as compensation. 
I have escalated the same to Indigo's Customer relations team and still chasing the compensation.

title: "Being on time is a wonderful thing"
text:
Me and my cofounder was travelling from Hyderabad to kochi after a day long meetings and tiring negotiations.  Our flight was delayed by few minutes.  We were little irritated about the delay. Finally boarded the flight by 10.45pm. One of the passengers sitting one row in front of us, noticed the person next to her is unconscious.  It created a real havoc in the time when the crew were busy with their final checklist for take off. He was completely soaked in vomitus. Suddenly the flight attendants took control of the scene.  One lady doc emerged from nowhere and was busy checking his pulse and vitals. Later I could realise she was the same passenger who was sitting next to him. Now we all know our 6E is going to have more delay. But the best thing is, no body is no more bothered about the delay. 
Crew asked any one has a spare shirt to offer the gentleman. Before this question reached the back row, my friend Dr. Rohit, took and offered his brand new shirt purchased from airport duty free. Crew members were repeatedly asking him if he was fine and offering medical help. In this short span of time at least 4 to 5 indigo officials came and made arrangements to clean the soiled seats and carpet.  Eventually our 6 E took off with an additional 45 minutes delay and landed kochi. Rohit was awarded a special gift for his kind gesture and a special mention by the flight attendant. What I could see different, in this entire episode was the human touch  and compassion those elegant crew members shown. Second thing I noticed was the efficiency of the Indigo team,  both crew as well as the ground staff. Being on time is a wonderful thing, but this one is special.

title: Worst Airline I've Ever Traveled With
text:
Never in my life have I had a more poor airline experience. 

We were on our way from Trivandrum to Jaipur, via a connecting flight through Bangalore. On our way to the airport, we noticed our flight, which was to leave at 5:05 pm, was going to be delayed such that we would miss our connecting flight. We knew there was another flight from Trivandrum to Bangalore that would leave at 5:35 pm, and so we asked to see if something could be done to put us on the 5:35 pm flight. We learned that the 5:35 was sold out, but our gate agent was able to find people on the 5:35 flight who were willing to switch flights with us. Tickets for the 5:35 flight were issued to us, and we made our way through security. So far, so good.

Well, we thought we were home free. Five minutes before we were due to board, however, the previous gate agent came to us and told us the people who had agreed to switch flights with us changed their minds. We couldn't believe it - how was this all of a sudden our problem?! The insane thing was the gate agent ended up CANCELING OUR TICKETS WITHOUT TELLING US. And he notified us of this WHILE WE WERE IN LINE TO BOARD. His solution? He gave us tickets that would fly us through the night to 3 different Indian cities. Evidently, this was their way of avoiding getting a hotel room for us. I've never encountered a more asinine solution in my life.

We told them this wouldn't do. The manager told us he would help us get back on our original flight to Bangalore, a new flight to Jaipur leaving in the morning, and a hotel in Bangalore. The next two hours were filled with more of the worst customer service I have ever seen. It was very clear that the Indigo team was quite understaffed. Several other passengers were very upset. The manager had a phone on each ear and STILL had people asking him questions. We had to fight tooth and nail to get the appropriate tickets and security clearances (they printed the wrong tickets several times). Due to the help of the one competent staff member, though, we were able to at least get the correct tickets at the very last minute. We nearly missed our flight! 

When we arrived in Bangalore, we discovered our original flight to Jaipur had also been late, and we missed it by 20 minutes (UGH!!!). We also discovered that no hotel had been booked for us, and all the hotels were apparently booked (which I sincerely doubt), so we had to spend a sleepless night in the airport lounge (and we had to fight with them to let us be in there for more than 3 hours). We did eventually get to Jaipur, but we ended up with a wasted day and a soured experience for the rest of our time in India. I have never been so mistreated by an airline. 

In the end, if you can avoid taking Indigo, you should. This airline is absolute trash.

Here's the summary of what happened to us:
- Changing our itinerary without telling us they would do that, which caused us to miss our connecting flight
- Not putting us up in a hotel in Bangalore, as promised
- Not honoring the extra services we bought (we were supposed to have better seats on the plane)

title: Another delayed, not very comfortable Indigo flight
text:
Friday 29th November we were booked on Indigo Airlines flight 6E977 from Kochi to Goa. 

Originally our flight was due to depart at 21.40 and arrive 23.00 While waiting at the Airport we received a notification, from the Airline that there was a delay and departure would be 22.20 and arriving in Goa at 23.45.

This was subsequently amended yet again, the delay was extended to 22.55 with a new arrival time of 12:20.

The aircraft finally pushed back at 23.00 and was finally airborne at 23.10. We landed in Goa at 00.10, an hour and 10 minutes late.

The captain did apologise for the delay which was as result of congestion at Mumbai Airport. We were informed that the flying time would be 1 hour.

The Cabin Crew did what they had to do, nothing more or less.

The cabin was clean and the legroom was good, seats were not very comfortable, bearable for a flight of this length.

Our outbound flight on Wednesday 27th November was also delayed over an hour.

As a point of interest went back to the Indigo booking page and in red text, there is a note "this flight is usually 30 minutes, or more delayed". 

Another airline might be a better option for punctuality.

title: Delayed and not very comfortable
text:
Wednesday evening 27th November and we were travelling from Dabolim, Goa to Cochi in Kerela on board Indigo flight 6E 901.

We were due to depart at 23.30 and arrive at 00.50, a scheduled flying time of 1 hour and 20 minutes 

Before heading for the Airport we did receive a message, from the Airline, advising the flight was already 30 minutes delayed with a revised departure of 00.05. Later on, we had arrived at the airport, the delay was extended to 00.30

We actually pushed back at 00.40 and were airborne at 00.50. We were informed that the flying time would be exactly 1 hour. There was no apology or explanation about the delay.

We arrived in Kochi at 01.50, which was exactly 1 hour later than scheduled.

Shortly after we were airborne, the Cabin Crew whizzed down the aisle selling snacks and drinks. They reappeared to collect in the rubbish and then to check seat belts before landing, that's it job done.

The legroom was rather good, however, the seating was adequately comfortable for an hour long flight.

Overall the flight was delayed and not very comfortable.

title: Kolkata landing just ahead of cyclone Bulbul
text:
Since I was flying out to Kolkata on a Saturday afternoon, I expected lesser crowds than those I encountered at Terminal 1 of IGI Airport. Check in was a breeze but y other airport facilities were overcrowded.The circulation area and the bright shops and cafes were chock full as were the departure gate areas. Even so, I felt lucky as my flight was the last one allowed to take off for Kolkata since cyclone Bulbul was expected to hit West Bengal that night. It was bright and sunny as we boarded but there was turbulence and darkness as we arrived. The pilot had warned us of this. But we still made a soft landing ahead of our scheduled arrival time. In flight service was high quality as far as budget airlines go. Prim hostesses with their flowery cravats served the passenger efficiently and quickly. On arrival, passengers complained that no aerobridge was provided and so we had to get off in blinding rain and rush to the buses. Still, the Indigo staff did well to make sure that the wheel chair passengers (six of them) were properly taken care of.
Flight operations at Kolkata airport were suddenly shut down for 12 hours thanks to Bulbul. As a result, there was chaos at the airport with long lines at the taxi counters and passengers frantically trying to ascertain the plight of their onward flights. International passengers were especially flummoxed. Mercifully, I had a car waiting for me which took me to the nearby Westin Hotel where I slept out the cyclone.

title: Blue is my favorite colour - Now IndiGo is my favorite budget airline
text:
The colour indigo is fresh and happy – even saying the word out loud makes me smile. The airline IndiGo is no different. Keeping in mind that this is a low-cost carrier, it was virtually impossible to tack any negativity onto this airline. They embrace a fun outlook on just about everything, from their inflight magazine, titled ‘6E’ (pronounced ‘sexy’), to their luggage buggies on the tarmac, called ‘Ground Force’. 

Yes, the seats are narrow (no worse than any other budget airline) and they don’t recline, which is a blessing when you’re trying to watch a video on your tablet/phone – that’s right, the seats do not have monitors built in. You pay for food and beverages (it’s the norm now), but the prices are fair and some of the snacks are served in fun packaging that you might even want to take home. I know I did. I still have my ‘Nut Case’.

Blue is my favorite colour, and now IndiGo is my favorite budget airline.

Four Thumbs Up

title: Not Allowed to Board Flight
text:
My experience with Indigo flight on 11/11/2019 

I was traveling from bangalore to jodhpur with a change of flight at Delhi with my in-laws aged    more than 65 years and a five year old son.
Our flight from bangalore to Delhi departure time was at 7:10am and estimated arrival time at Delhi was 10.00 am and our next flight from Delhi for Jodhpur was at 12:55  pm as per our original tickets booked.
 We boarded our bangalore flight on time at around 6:45 am and were sitting in the flight for around 2 hrs as it didn’t take off due to extreme fog on that day. Flight started at 8:50 am and we reached Delhi at 11:20 am.
As per our original connecting flight timings of 12:55 pm, we were having sufficient time to board our next flight to jodhpur.
But next flight for unknown reasons was preponed from 12:55 to 12:10pm. If Indigo flight staff n management has proactively taken steps, we would have easily catched our next flight for jodhpur even at 12:10pm. But after getting down from bangalore flight, they asked us to stay on side from other passengers. We thought that they are taking us quickly for our next flight. They asked us to sit in another bus . We were eight passengers for Jodhpur flight. But surprising they have taken us to some information desk on terminal 2 where a manger abruptly told us that we can’t board the flight and there is no other flight also for the same day and for tomorrow also no seats are available in jodhpur flight. Then he started doing booking for other passengers for next day. They were not paying attention at all to us. We were clueless as that was not our mistake. First flight delayed and next flight preponed both were from your side and was not our fault. But seriously we eight passengers were treated as if we had committed a mistake n were not able to catch the flight due to our mistake.

Then when we all together asked him n got little angry on him explaining our situation, then he started trying but that too not in an aggressive phase. We checked on internet n it was showing as seats available in other flights like vistara, spice jet and Air India. We requested him to take prompt action so that we don’t miss those seats also.

Then after few calls, they asked us to go to terminal 3 and reach there in 5 mins so that we don’t miss the seats in the next flight.
We all eight passengers with a hope that we will get the next flight same day, ran quickly to terminal 3. They didn’t provide any assistance like wheel chairs for senior citizens or any attendant for helping us to carry the luggage (because the worst part was that our check-in luggages (4 big suitcases)which was supposed to be collected from jodhpur by us was also handed over to us in Delhi). My in-laws who have many health probs like high bp etc were also running with us so that we don’t miss the flight which was actually told to us.
And now comes the best part of the story... after all hassles, when we reached at terminal 3 Indigo desk, they told us that they don’t have any communication regarding it n they are not aware about any seats available. Seriously we all were shocked n disheartened. Infact, they told us that we will give u 50% refund and can’t do anything about the flight to jodhpur. This was also told to us as if it was our fault and they doing charity by giving 50% to us.

At that time, I was having no other option with old parents and a kid to book tickets from my own pocket from Air India. Air India guys helped us a lot in such situation and we got seats in their next flight. I spent 16000/- plus amount for booking four tickets. 

Surprisingly Air India flight was almost empty when we boarded it. If Indigo guys have tried for us properly n promptly, we could have easily got seats in Air India. But may be you guys didn’t wanted to spend on your customers.
Looking at my experience, I will never fly again in Indigo and going to share this experience with my friends n relatives n tell them also to avoid Indigo.

Thanks & Regards,
Shweta Prajapati
