title: IndiGo's Communication Efficiency in India is Poor
text:
From Kuala Lumpur to Bengaluru, and from the Bengaluru to Ahmedabad, India, both the international and domestic (Indian) flights were smooth going and excellent.
However, that was not the case upon the return from Ahmedabad 6E823. In fact, IndiGo India didn't get to inform me about the cancellation of flight 6E823 to Bengaluru - no onward calls or emails. Hence, upon checking in they only informed me at the Check-In counter at Ahmedabad International Airport. The staff kept on asking why I was not informed of this? In the end, a senior IndiGo counter staff made arrangements for me first to travel to Hyderabad, India and then from Hyderabad to catch an immediate connecting flight to Bengaluru and finally, from Bengaluru to Kuala Lumpur (on the connected booked flight in the morning). 
Everything went well from Ahmedabad to Hyderabad and the senior staff officer at Ahmedabad assured me that I would have time to get on the arranged flight from Hyderabad to Bengaluru. However, his promises backfired! As I reached Hyderabad, I had to run and rush to catch the next plane but only to find out the flight delayed for an hour. So if the flight from Hyderabad to Bengaluru delayed, there wasn't any way I had the chance to catch the connecting flight from Bengaluru to Kuala Lumpur and furthermore as an international passenger I was to clear immigration and customs. When I noticed about the disconnection, I quickly highlighted to the (operational) ground staff at the gate that I was waiting. The ground staff apparently were getting to board passengers for another destination in India. The staff seemed unconcerned but noticed the errors in the connection as the delay of the flight from Hyderabad to Bengaluru would create problems for any onward destinations.
As the ground crew was busy, the young man requested me to follow a lady janitorial staff where I would be attended to at another counter that's outside of the gate terminal. As I was following and coming to the security and immigration checks of Hyderabad International Airport, the two (ladies) janitorial staff disappeared after the security and immigration checks. I did not go out because I cannot go out and the janitorial staff were supposed to retrieve IndiGo counter staff to retrieve me and getting approval from the security and immigration officers to exit the area. I waited and waited for the two ladies, they didn't show. I was getting annoyed and infuriated and I returned to the gate (that I was supposed to board the plane). Luckily, the male operational staff was still there, and I resounded my problems to the young man. Upon noticing my problems he attended to me. After he completed his tasks at the gate, he requested me to follow him. This time, he attended to the security protocols to allow me to go out of the gate terminal to solve the problems at the counter. Luckily then, I didn't just go out like that. Otherwise, I could have been arrested for trespassing.
Once at the Check-In IndiGo counters at Hyderabad International Airport, the male operational staff explained to the senior counter staff on the far end of the IndiGo counter. They noticed the problems. The senior staff lady at the IndiGo Counter made some promises to me like, she would change and resourced other flights for me. I agreed to her choices as there were no other choices. The choices were that I had to fly to Delhi from Hyderabad and from Delhi (that's a morning flight at 5:30 am, India Standard time). Apart from these, she also told me that "for my troubles, she was willing to provide the compliment lounge pass for me to eat and relax at Hyderabad and Delhi Internationa Airports." I was delighted at her welfare hospitality.  However, she told me to sit at the far end of the airport and waited for her availability to come over to call for me. I waited for something like 45 minutes to almost an hour. Nothing happened. I also knew about the next flight time which was some time at 5:30 pm from Hyderabad to Delhi. Noting that something was amiss, I decided to return the counter myself and I found out that the lady staff who promised me about everything had disappeared. A senior male staff and a couple of younger junior staff were at the counter. As I was explaining to the senior male staff, he kind of recalled who I was and he said, "Are you, Mr. Chan"? I replied to him saying that I was and he knew about my predicament. I felt relieved as I was getting strained and very disappointed. Then he called out to his younger junior staff to quickly attend to me. I still had to wait...but for only 15 minutes as he was earlier busy with a couple of customers. Similarly, he explained to me about the choices of flights that he confirmed for me and the compliments that he would get senior management to allow me to enjoy the privileges at the lounges at both Hyderabad and Delhi airports. Again I was made to believe the promises.
After my security checks on having to proceed to the gate terminal's concourse, I proceeded straight to the Hyderabad Lounge for food and to relax. Upon reaching the place, the reception staff told me that no complimentary had come to their ends. Initially, they thought they were still awaiting approvals from IndiGo to allow me into the lounge without payment. I waited again (patiently) for almost half an hour and I noticed that I had been had again. I asked the reception staff to double check and in fact, they even called their manager out and they all assisted to check for my complimentary order. IndiGo confirmed with the Lounge at the Hyderabad that there was no concurrence for any 'complimentary' for any customer. Even though, I was disappointed, the lounge personnel were even more disappointed because I was made to wait and every patron saw me malingering in the reception area like an 'impatient idiot.' The lounge staff tried to apologise however, I refused their apologies because it wasn't their fault. Upon knowing the empty complimentary promises, I didn't bother to waste anymore time asking for a pass at Delhi International Airport.

What I am disappointed about my return trip was the fact that:
(A) IndiGo staff were unprofessional in solving customer's problems.
(B) They lacked integrity and made empty promises.
(C) Airlines are all about service, courtesy, and tactfulness, and the ground staff in India is slacking badly in these areas.

IndiGo in Malaysia is FANTASTIC. The way they managed their operations and the concerns staff may encounter with luggage, promptness of flights, etc. In order for IndiGo to compete viably with its competitors like Jet Airways, Vistara Airlines, Air Asia and other budget airlines, your ground crew can perhaps take a page of customer services from these budget airlines.

One piece of advice for all travellers in India, if you have a return ticket, make sure the ticket is viable at least 1 or 2 days beforehand, otherwise, you will encounter problems.

There is a direct Qatar Airways flight daily, but that's costly compared to Indigo. 
At the time of check in at Kolkata, you will be given boarding passes for Hyderabad only however the luggage will be booked through upto Doha. At the moment the International departures at Hyderabad is taking place from Interim Terminal, which has no place to sit before the check in, that will take place only about 3.5 hours to 4 hours before departure.

title: No Frills Airline
text: This is a relatively new airline and it is relatively inexpensive. So most of them have limited experience but they do a good job given the clientele.  For example, for some of the patrons this might be their first flight so the stewardess are spending an inordinate amount of time helping them find their seats.  This also means that there may at least one person who will throw up.  On our flight unfortunately it was the person in the next row and no one told them about the throw up bag.  There is a lot of pushing and no concept of personal space, while this isn’t the airlines issue but rather an issue with the patrons, if the stewardess’ had more experience, they may be able to control it.  Since the airline specifically advertises for young women below 27 years to apply for the positions, it is unlikely that they will have senior staff on their planes. title: Avoid INDIGO Airlines - Worst Airlines I've ever dealt with!
text:
On May 30th, 2018 my husband, mother and myself were supposed to catch our flight from Delhi, India to Goa, India with Indigo Airlines.

However, the day before our flight we received a message stating that our terminal had changed due to renovations in the airport. My husband had called the airlines to confirm and was told that our terminal had in fact changed.

Once we arrived at the Delhi airport, security wouldn’t let us inside the airport and he kept telling us we were in the wrong terminal. We told him that the airlines themselves had confirmed about the terminal change, but he still didn’t want to let us in and asked us to go to the Indigo customer care outside of the airport.

When we went inside the customer service area it was already packed with other passengers and we had to wait a long time before we were greeted by the only one Indigo Airlines agent that was there. After we explained the situation to the gentleman, he called his manager to help us. The manager took at least 15-20 minutes before he came down (after the agent called numerous times). When we re-explained the situation the manager told us he can’t help us and left mid-conversation, baffling both my husband and I with such horrible customer service, especially from someone in management.

The manager left another agent to “deal” with us that was even less helpful. By this time, boarding to the plane had started and we were still stuck with the agent telling us she couldn’t do anything.

We asked instead of giving us full credit to book us another flight and we would pay the difference but she did not want to do that. She said we will have to pay in full for the flights and we would not be reimbursed. By this time, all early flights were gone, and by the time we finally checked ourselves to book another flight with another airlines all flights to Goa for May 30th were booked.

We booked our flight with Fly Air for 6 times the original price and had to book a hotel for another night at Delhi.

We called the hotel in Goa to advise them we wouldn’t make it to the hotel that day, but rather the following afternoon and asked if we would be able to get a credit for that day, but unfortunately we couldn’t.

Because of the horrible service from Indigo airlines and wrong information given to us by them, we had to spend 6 times the price of our original flights, lost 1 day of hotel in Goa and had to book another extra night in Delhi.

I've warned all family and friends to avoid this airlines, and any future customer/client that is looking in to booking with them, AVOID!!!

text:

title: Observations from a North American traveler perspective
text:
Indigo can be compared to Southwest Airlines in North America with an all economy configuration with assigned seating.  Planes tend to be new as Indigo and other Indian airlines are adding a lot of capacity; our flight was operated by an  A320 NEO delivered in November 2018.  As a result the planes are clean but have the newer slim seat design that some people describe as "hard" to sit on.  These seats have limited recline of the seat back as the seat itself slides forward somewhat to give you the same feeling as the older, thicker seats that where only the seat back reclines.  This means that the person reclining in front of you will not take up much of your personal space which is a plus.

Like Southwest, soft drinks are complimentary but unlike Southwest there are food for purchase options.  Indigo does a much better job of getting through the cabin for  service compared to Jet Airways that is more of a full service airline (think American, Delta, or United).  Flight attendants were friendly, helpful, and efficient.

No entertainment service is provided even on personal devices.

Checked baggage is limited to 15kg. (33lbs.) before baggage fees kick in ... about Rs 400 per kilogram.  This is similar to most other Indian airlines with the exception of Air India that offers 25kg. of free checked baggage.

Boarding starts early and ends early with no more than 5 minutes between "now boarding" and the "final boarding" calls.  Customers line up without a lot of pushing and shoving for a very orderly boarding process ... since bags can be checked there is not much concern about sufficient space for carry on bags which removes a lot of tension.  Many airports use a combination of a jet bridge at the front of the plane with stairs made available at the rear which speeds up getting out of the plane ... sitting at the back of the plane is not a bad thing in terms of getting off quickly. Boarding tends to complete about 25 minutes before departure when the doors are closed and armed but the plane sits at the gate waiting for the actual departure time.

Overall you get solid (and for us on time) service at a very low price with only a seat selection fee for some aisle and exit row seats; definitely very different than the Spirit and Frontier low cost business models in North America where add on fees for seats, checked and carry on baggage can quickly eat into any lower fare savings compared to legacy carriers.

title: CANCELLED FLIGHT AND PASSENGERS STRANDED
text:
We were to fly back to Mumbai from Chandigarh on the afternoon of 3 January 2019. In the morning we received a message that the flight was delayed. I was pleasantly surprised that the airline had taken the trouble to inform passengers well in advance. By mid-morning we were informed of a further delay. We decided on having lunch and then heading for the airport. We had lunch, checked out of the hotel and called for an Uber to take us to the airport. We were barely on our way to the airport when we received another message (perhaps the fourth or fifth message of the day) and this time we were informed that our flight had been cancelled. 
We immediately called the airline to check whether this information was correct. Obviously it took us several attempts and long waits to finally get a customer service person on the phone line. Now when we finally got through and confirmed that the flight was indeed cancelled, we requested the airline to re-book us on the earliest available flight. It's at this point that not once, not twice but three times that  the call attendants told us to hold and then cut off the line. This happened on all three attempts they cut off the call. When we finally got hold of a call attendant after many tries, we requested he not hang up but just tell us when we could get a flight back home. He informed us that nothing was available for the next day and was unsure of the following day!
The airline shrugged off all responsibility saying the cancellation was because of "operational reasons". They could do nothing and of course within moments we got cut off the line. So now we had no hotel reservations and no flight home either.
Fortunately Jet Airways were far more courteous and booked us back on their first flight the very next day. Not just that, they cautioned passengers to book seats quickly as the fares were going up.We did book on Jet Airways and got back home on a very comfortable flight the next day. NO THANKS TO INDIGO who just didn't care about their passengers at all.   
Several flights were cancelled on that day due to fog in Delhi and Indigo must have ascertained in advance that the flight from Chandigarh would be cancelled too but instead of apprising passengers they chose to inform them of delays even though the flight was going to be cancelled. Also they made no attempt to assist stranded passenger. Offered no compensation. in fact airline seats got more expensive and Indigo would only refund the amount paid for their ticket. The excess we had to pay for tickets booked so late was of course our problem not Indigo's !! Truly pathetic service and customer care.

After arriving at the airport at 5am scheduled to leave at  7.10 am the flight attendants denied us access onto the flight, on the basis that we had not acquired a transit visa, the flight manger’s precise words were:

 “It’s the responsibility of the customer to pre-arrange the transit visa”

Fair one, but it would have been nice to know this before we paid for the tickets. Moreover, after several hours of drinking cheap coffee from the seven eleven and trying to make a thousand phone calls to the Indian immigration authority, and the Indian embassy in Bangkok we finally managed to get through to both to which they replied: 

“what’s the problem, you would have been fine if they’d  let you onto the flight”

On further research there is a transit visa that you have to acquire for transits but can only be obtained at the embassy itself in Bangkok, and can take up to thirty days to process, with no guarantee of actually acquiring. This seems an excessive amount of time to wait for a 5-hour transit visa! Anyway, what originally cost us £1000 now cost us double, as we had to organise a new flight for the next day! So, all I can say is thanks a bunch Indigo or  INDI-YouNo-GO as your company should be called!

title: On time, No Frill Value for Money Service
text:
I am travelling tonight, 11th Jan 2019, from  Singapore to Kiljata by INDIGO flight 6E 42. I booked my ticket online through MMT and got return ticket with seat reservation at around Rs.21.5k , which was cheaper considering the closest option with other airlines at Rs. 28k plus. Of course Indigo is not a full service airline and don't offer elaborate in-flight services.The scheduled departure was at  02.45 hours from Changi T 2 and I reached airport at 12.30 am. Following is my overall experience about the flight ( Rating given out of 5, 5 being the highest):-
A. Check-in: Checking at Row was smooth and fast (Rating 4).
B. Lounge access: The flight being all economy one , there was no lounge facility offered. I used my Priority Pass to access Airport Lounge.(Rating Neutral)
C. Boarding and departure: Boarding opened at 1.15 am at Gate F31. Push back happened  at  2.40 hours and it took off at 2 50 hours(Rating 4). 
D. Seats and interior: The aircraft was a Airbus 320 series one and looked older one in the service. The signature interior in Blue and Grey looked bright . My booked seat was 2D, a paid aisle seat in the front that allows quick access to toilet and exit. Seat pitch was ok with comfortable upholstery. Seat recline was not too good for a 4 hour plus flight. The cabin was clean and had a fresh feeling.(Rating 3.75).
E. In flight services: Being a no frill flight there is hardly any in flight service.Typical tasteless Indigo meal can be bought. I dislike Indigo meal and avoided food as usual. In any case , who wants to eat at wee hours of early morning .(Rating 3.5)
F. Cabin Crew: The cabin crew in charge inside the cabin were extremely polite , efficient and helpful. (Rate 4)
G. Arrival and baggage: Flying time was approx 4 hours .Flight landed at NSC Bose International on time at 4.10 pm and gates were opened at 4.20 pm. Arriving belt number was announced at the flight, which made things easier for us. Luggage on the belt 12 came after 40 minutes. I collected mine at 5 am.Very poor efficiency (Rating 4)
H.Overall flight experience and suggested area of improvement: Overall flying experience was good and surely value for money. Flight time is little inconvenient being too early arrival and almost a red eye flight that will spoil your day.However the following are my suggested area of improvements a) For a 4 hour International flight they should have considered slightly better seat comfort. b) They must have better menu choice. Passengers are ready to pay but give them descent options for hot menu at least. They should learn from European no frill flights where food also has to be bought but you have much better choice. They can't offer pax to buy same bad menu that they make available in their domestic flights c) It will be a good option to keep first 2 rows as premium economy with better seats (2×2) and better food as well. Pax are ready to pay extra for the comfort. 
On the whole, it was a descent experience and definitely convenient and value for money. (Overall Rating 4).

title: Good No-frills Airline
text:
At Mumbai, Indigo flights operate from the domestic terminal, T1 (A few other airlines like Jet Airways, operate from the International Terminal, T2). It is best to check the terminal beforehand, as transfer from one terminal to the other, is from outside the airport, by road transport, and can take 30 mts or more, depending on traffic.

Refreshment announcement for delay made around 9:30 am at Vango. Imagine 170 odd people lined up to get first their tickets checked and then again wait in second queue for getting hot refreshments. All this while normal customers also being served. Definitely not the best of decisions.

Boarding commences at around 10:10 am onwards. Boarding completed in hardly any time. 

No clearance from ATC for visibility of push back also. I was in the aircraft from around 10:30 and the push back happened only around 12:20. We were actually airborne around 13:15 hours, full over 4 hours of delay.

It is not understood why we were made to board the aircraft if we would be able to fly only after 3 hours. Definitely management needs to make a note of this.

How can fresh refreshments like south indian cuisine be served to over 160 odd people with people being made to stand in two queues ? Why couldn't something simpler like sandwiches, patties, soft drink etc be planned in these fog kind of challenges in advance.

Definitely some planning needs to go into handling these Fog issue days

title: Near Death Experience on Jaipur - Kolkata Indigo flight 6E-237
text: Had a horrible experience aboard Indigo airline while flying from Jaipur to Kolkata last week. I was on-board Indigo 6E-237 and half-an-hour before landing in Kolkata smoke started filling the cabin. This smoke was coming from AC vents and everyone aboard the flight was terrified as this drama unfolded mid-air ruling out any possibility to land any time soon. Everyone was afraid whether the flight would or wouldn't land. It almost felt as if we were sitting in the middle of a pyre of burning plastic and metal. That smoke was so horrible that babies started crying and passengers started murmuring and started throwing nervous glances at each other. Panic was written all over everyone’s face. As the flight landed, I asked a flight attendant to help me get out of the flight but it seems that the crew on board froze. I beg to question the safety regulations followed by Indigo and its crew members. With each moment that passed, everyone grew more and more afraid as smoke completely engulfed the cabin. With little help or information coming from the crew, everyone expected the worse. I swear I will think twice before taking an Indigo flight and will also urge everyone to reconsider Indigo. While it can be written off as a stray incident, the reality is that their aircraft have encountered issues in the recent past.

text:

The onboarding at Gate 5 was managed very professionally and was real fast. The flight departed on time and arrived on time. The inflight crew was great, very prompt, anticipated customer needs and provided good service. The pilot as well as crew announcements were crisp and clear. The flight landed on time and the landing was near perfect, really smooth. However, the seats on Indigo planes are not comfortable, and in this flight the hum of the engine/machinery was too loud and sharp making it very uncomfortable to bear. I found the cabin temperature to be warmer than what I would have preferred. The seat pocket on my seat did not carry the inflight magazine and there were bits of paper left behind by perhaps the previous traveler - so in a bid to remain on time, the crew compromised on the clean-up and seat readiness.

What I also do not appreciate is that for almost "any" window or aisle seat - the airline charges you extra money which is ridiculous. Airlines like Vistara do not exhibit a similar behavior. If Indigo is listening, it should change this attitude. 

Overall, a good experience, but again nothing exemplary - just another airline amidst the so many available. We seem to be missing any WoW factor when it comes to economy class travel in India.

title: Being on Time? Seriously? My view- just like other airlines
text: I am a very frequent flyer and have to travel a lot for business. Though the reputation of being on time always has definitely conditions applied. title: How "On Time" statements can be a scam to make money from the passengers.
text:
I arrived at the airport about 2 hours before from JFK. Line is long and previous flights passengers are called to bypass the line as they would be missing flights. As a result we are getting delayed because fewer counters are available for us. Finally we also had to be called 30 minutes before and got the boarding passes and rushed to the gate 28 (the farthest gate). We reached the gate at 9:05 for the 9:20 flight and gate is closed. The gate person named Karan rudely said that he was looking for us and when I asked where, he said close to gate 23. So  I asked why not close to security, no answer. Then we are sent to counter 8. The gentleman named Moize very cleverly talked in low voice and was trying to be professional but absolutely of no help and he was talking over the phone with friends. But he could not put two of us in the next flight. After traveling 36 hours from JFK with fever my wife got one seat for Rs 1000. Moize was very proud to save me some money which had a very little value at that time.  I got a ticket at later flight in the evening for Rs 18000.00 more. Finally, Alfred came to rescue and he put me in the same flight as my wife. It surely shows Moize's professionalism. While I was waiting for Alfred to change my ticket, unfortunately Moize had to come almost face to face with me and he avoided and took trouble to go behind me which I was closely watching. It confirms that he knew he could have done the same which Alfred did but decided not to do so.

MY QUESTION: IS ON TIME DEPARTURE A SCAM TO PUNISH SOME PEOPLE AND MAKE MONEY FROM THEM IN THIS FASHION?

While indigo made us wait in line while calling passengers of the flights before us, how can they close the gate while we already checked in and on our way to the gate. If Indigo open fewer counters and make people suffer and then show greatness by calling people who are getting late, they make them look good. But by doing so, they are making the next flight passengers late. As Moize said that they call passengers 30 minutes before and then close the gate 25 minutes before. It means it gives passengers 5 minutes to go from check in line to the gates. Obviously denying me boarding also made them delayed because they had to get my luggage out. Also the strange thing is they got 5 pieces of luggage out from the aircraft while we were only carrying 4 pieces. So one of the passengers did not get his/her luggage when reached Kolkata. Does all this trouble worth it for few extra Rupees from me against may be 5 minutes. While passengers are checked in, what is the reason to close the gate. What passenger can do in between checking-in and arriving at the gate. Specially after 36 hours of flying which Indigo knew from boarding passes while I payed extra luggage fee for international passengers. 

So is it a good way to show on time and charge double money from some passengers? So where did I go wrong? Unfortunately our next flight was one hour late. 

ANY ANSWER FROM INDIGO?

DK.

text: I was to fly back to Dubai from New Delhi on 9th December. On that winter morning I reached the airport at 4:30 a.m. checked in my baggage at around 5:00 a.m. cleared immigration and my boarding pass said that I was to reach the departure gate by 6:15 a.m. for a flight departing at 6:45 a.m. Not realising that the Gate 10 was really far I spent time buying medicine and a book and by the time I hopped into the airport golf cart I reached the gate at 6:20 am. To my utter disbelief the staff refused to let me board. I wasn't the only passenger and they refused to accommodate our request. The international norm is that the airline can accept passengers even 15 to 20 mins prior to flight departure. Me and another co-passenger were offloaded and made to go through a harrowing experience just to go by the "indigo" rules of boarding!!! There were no manual announcements made by Indigo whereas other airlines like Air India were making repeated announcements at gate 1 for all passengers. I found the airlines and its staff unaccommodating and insensitive to customers when we were very much within the norm of boarding the flight. My co-passenger was at the gate at 6:15 a.m so they had no excuse to offload him!!! To top it all there was no staff / duty manager ready to listen to our request!! I will surely think twice before selecting Indigo for all my future travels.

title: On time performance, Courteous Crew, New and Well-maintained Aircraft
text:
IndiGo is by far the only domestic airline worth writing about in India today. With 200 aircraft, well-trained cabin crew, and on-time performance, the airline stands out in what is otherwise a dismal aviation scenario. 
IndiGo has adopted the practices of the low cost airlines on the one hand and of the major global carriers on the other. You pay a base fare that varies on the time of booking (the more in advance you book, the better the fare you get) and you also pay statutory levies. Everything else from seat selection to in-flight snacks and beverages have to be paid for. Having flown most of the major airlines, I do believe that the charges for seat selection are high (On a 150 minute flight, I paid almost 10% of the fare to select a seat up front). There is only one class - economy - and charging such a high fee for what is essentially the same seat except for its location - appears a little unfair. The "free" seats are all towards the rear of the aircraft.
The snacks and beverages are priced high. At one level, it is understandable - after all, it is a matter of choice. I have seen passengers "packing" a snack in their cabin baggage to avoid having to pay the high price. 
That said, looking at the other domestic carriers, these may be prices worth paying to make sure the airline remains viable. 
Also, except in a few places, the carrier does not have access to the aero-bridges (another cost cutting measure) and the aircraft is parked somewhere and passengers are ferried to and from the terminal on buses. The airline may do well do do a overall benefit-to-cost analysis in deciding whether to pay for aero-bridges. That would be a real benefit to passengers, particularly children and the elderly.

title: Indigo Flight 6E 559 Mumbai Jammu Srinagar
text:
Beating the queue of Diwali vacation travelers with the help of an airline agent, we dropped out check in bags and got to the departure gate at Mumbai’s domestic airport, in time for 11 am flight to Srinagar via Jammu.There was some delay in taking off- nothing unusual for Mumbai airport where traffic congestion is high. But we-my wife and my friend and his wife- settled soon and began enjoying the flight. I am quite fond of flying with Indigo Airways because their fleet of Airbus A 320 is comfortable and airline ensures good hygiene and its crew are efficient. 

After reaching Jammu airspace the captain announced that for reasons not known to them we were not being cleared for landing. After about half an hour his voice crackled over the PA sysytem to inform that due to low fuel, in case we were not cleared for landing in next 7-10 mts, according to Standard Operating Procedure, our flight would make an emergency landing at Amritsar. Just as our anxiety levels were rising ( I had noticed that it was an Airbus Neo with Pratt & Whitney jets!) the Captain’s voice crackled once again to inform that we were landing in Jammu. The sigh of relief across the plane which had about 99% full. 

After all Jammu passengers got off, we were about 25-30 passengers left on the aircraft. Except one or two, rest of us were eager to land in Srinagar for a holiday. Just then the Captain first broke the bad news- due to early snow, Srinagar runway could not take intouch downs so the flight would go back to Mumbai. This was followed by even worse announcement- we too were flying back. Imagine the disappointment of vacationers! We all requested the Captain & some ground staff who had also boarded the aircraft to book us on next day’s flight and that we would not bother the airline for overnight hotel accommodation. But the officials did not seem in a mood to oblige, although we persuaded them to escalate the issue to the airline HQ through the duty manager at Jammu. 

Finally we were allowed to disembark but there was no word regarding our fate and the officials requested us to be patient. Finally, nearly 2 hours after arrival at Jammu terminal, the officials informed us that the airline was indeed putting us on next day’s flight toSrinagar! But we had to wait further until the passes got printed. Sensing our impatience, the duty manager organized some snacks for us, which we gladly accepted. 

Finally, after another 45 minutes wait, Mr Razdan and his team handed next day morning flight boarding passes to us ! 

The Srinagar Airport teams had worked overnight to clear the runway of snow and our flight was cleared for take off. When we landed at Srinagar, all of us from previous day’s flight clapped spontaneously. 

Our holiday had begun. Thanks in a big way to the concern for passengers shown by Indigo Team led by Mr Razdan.

title: Unprofessional Bad Rude Behaviour
text:
It’s very painful to write the very disappointing experience with your airline indigo.

We were 15 family members travelling by 6E 654 from Chennai to Mumbai today on 11.11.2018. We were very much on time in check in, baggage, security check everything. Boarding started at 4.40 am and as I was suffering from diarrhoea, I had to rush to washroom at that time. My other 14 members were started for boarding and I reached the desk at 4.55 am and I am denied saying gates are closed. Among us four were senior citizens, one on wheelchair who require extra care and attention still every thing fell on deaf ears.

I was very much shocked and surprised to know that and I informed ... how come ? As my group members have yet not entered aircraft still they didn’t listen me. Then they offered me help of a colleague (Ms Kavya, if I heard the name properly) that she will help you. She went on going here and there calling somebody over Mobile not really addressing and informing me what she is doing .... I understood she is arranging something and she wasted time and at 5.15 am she showed me the exit. When I countered and requested her she rudely told me that without her I can not exit. I am told to go to reservation counter and make alternative arrangements. 

When I reached your reservation and customer care counter I met Mr Muthukumar, who told me there is no seat available in next flight at 6.45 am and not even in 9.00 am flight. I requested him lot that my whole family has gone... I don’t have any luggage and I am sick. He told me that he can only confirm at 6 am. Then he said not possible now come at 8 am. When I approached him at 8.00 am I was told no seat available. Meet me after 10 min. Then again I requested and joined my hands not to behave indifferently and consider. Ultimately at 8.20 am, he told me me that he will give me seat and before giving me the boarding pass he asked for 1000/- Rs. When I inquired why money? He said this is procedural charge. I was finally given boarding pass between 8.25 to 8.30 am for the 9.00 o’clock flight 6E 782 PNR no. QI7J8A. No receipt was given for 1000/- Rs and I am advised to rush to gate no 6 or otherwise will miss this flight also. I had no other option than to run and board. I boarded at 8.40 am. Surprising is that more than five seats were still vacant in the flight.

Once I was denied to board when I was 30 min before the time of departure and now I am allowed 20 min before...! The total indifferent and unprofessional approach of your staff was quite unexpected and shocking. In place of helping me they just misguided me, harassed me and lied to me. Buses were going right then, and they could have simply instruct the driver to drop me near my Mumbai flight. But they didn’t.

Sir, I strongly disapprove and am very much disappointed, and the three hours I have spent bagging here and there were like a hell. I don’t know weather I will ever choose your airline on priority basis but will be at least get some consolation if you take up this matter and act positively to improve your staff’s working style and attitude. 

Wish to listen back from you.

Bharat Kothari.

title: Totally Incompetent International Operation
text: This was my 10th or so flight with IndiGo and it came out to be the worst so far! Our original flight (leaving at 10:30 AM from CCU) was discontinued by IndiGo 2 months prior to journey date thereby throwing our entire tour plan in jeopardy. However, we were rebooked automatically to the night flight, which I hated but had no choice. We were offered to change the dates or cancel the ticket for free though. But I chose to take the nightly flight. The flight was delayed by more than 30 minutes in leaving the gate at Kolkata. The seats in the aircraft were usual but one of the hand-rest plastic guard/cover was broken causing a minor cut in my son’s leg. The load factor of the flight was not even 80%. The flight attendants were very customer-friendly throughout the flight. But when I wanted to pay for the bottle of water, they asked for USD 3. I didn’t have US dollar bills with me since we were going to Thailand and therefore had only Indian Rupees and Thai Baht. So, I gave them two of my US credit cards. Surprisingly the POS device refused to recognize/accept both of them! I finally realized IndiGo may not be modern enough to handle foreign credit cards yet. So, I handed them over my Indian credit card and sure enough, the charge went through! I ended up paying 3.5% cross-border fee and 18% GST on that fee. The aircraft engine noise (it was an A320-232 and we were in row 6) was unusually loud during climb after take-off. And I flew in A320 at least 20 times before this. The noise was gone after it reached cruising altitude though. What really killed the flight experience was the distribution of obsolete version of Thai Immigration Cards to all the passengers. It took me a good 30 minutes to fill up the 4 forms (for 4 of us) in the plane only to find at Bangkok airport that a new form came into effect 13 months (not typo) ago! So, I had to spend 20 more minutes to fill up the new form. The luggage carousel number provided at the aircraft was wrong as well - we were told to collect them from belt #20 whereas in reality it came in belt #18. IndiGo was among my top-3 preferred airlines in India, but after this flight, I’ll think many times before booking with them.

title: Agonizing
text: In all of my years of and many, many experiences flying, I have never been faced with such a totally classless airline as Indigo. I booked a flight with them from Kathmandu to New Delhi and had another flight booked a few hours later from New Delhi to Bangkok--meaning I wouldn't be leaving the airport or going through customs/immigration in Delhi. According to their own website, since I did not have checked baggage and therefore would not need to leave the international terminal/go though immigration/customs, I would not need a visa. That's what the warning message said before I purchased my ticket. However, upon checking-in in Kathmandu, I was told that I would be denied entry onto the plane because I did not have an Indian visa. How is that possible? I have since researched this matter more and confirmed that I did not need a visa for my specific situation. Luckily, I was able to get a Jet Airways flight to New Delhi a few hours later and thus did not miss my flight from Delhi to Bangkok. Jet Airways were MORE than accommodating and I would recommend them 100% (good free food too). But, obviously, I did have to pay for the extra, unexpected Jet Airways flight, which put a huge dent in my budget. I spent a while emailing with a member of Indigo's customer relations team about getting a full refund but they wouldn't refund all of it (just part) and the agent kept regurgitating the same line over and over--"company policy"--without ever really combating any of the numerous points I made as to why I was wrongly denied entry onto the plane. It is clear to me that this misleading company doesn't care at all about their customers and so I will NEVER use them again and I implore you not to either!

title: Transit Visa Issue
text:
This evening I had a ticket to travel to New Delhi from Kathmandu, Nepal with IndiGo Airlines for connecting flight to Kabul, Afghanistan but the check-in counter didn't provide me boarding pass and told me that I had to have a transit visa or to book another flight with Jet Airways or Air India. 

Based on the agreement of Indian Government with IndiGo Airlines, passengers can't transit through Delhi airport to third country without a transit visa. But they can transit without any visa if they booked ticket with Jet Airways, Air India or any other airline. 

How funny it is! 

In order not to miss my connecting flight to Kabul, a huge amount was paid for taking a last minute flight to Delhi with another airline. 

PS: Avoid booking flight with IndiGo Airlines if you transit to third country through India without having a valid Indian Visa.

title: my worst flight yet
text:
The flight got delayed by around 30 minutes. By the time we reached Kolkata, we (3 people travelling together) immediately checked in for the transit flight to Hyderabad. We had roughly 2 hours to board the flight. For the 2 hours, we had been near the gate waiting to hear the announcement. When it was almost 2 hours, we got worried and when we started looking for the any sign of boarding the only announcement came and when we rushed to the gate, the rude guy stopped us immediately. We requested him but he was very unfriendly and kept arguing that you are late. The sign clearly showed that the plane was still boarding but he denied us. However, a family of 4 person came running and by that time it was almost 15 minutes we had been arguing with this guy. Upon the familys request he talked on his walkitalki and said it is late. We were requesting for nearly 15 minutes and the family requested them for almost 5 minutes, in total almost 20 minutes. 20 minutes was a fair consideration to all to request the crew as not one or two but 7 people were left behind. I feel it is their responsibility, but they argued that Kolkata is a silent airport. F.....g silent airport when for other airplanes, the announcements were made repeatedly.

I later learnt that this is the way to mint money by Indigo as he just was not in the mood to even make a last call to the air crew and let the stranded passengers board. He just took us to a ticketing agent and then disappeared making us to pay 1000 Rs each for the next flight. Silent airport is understandable but for the first timers, those who cannot read and write will be easy victim to indigo if they do this unethical ways of dealing with the stranded passengers. In other that I travelled far and wide to Hongkong, Bangkok, Heathrow, Dubai, Schipol to cite some have the best priority for passengers and they even come looking for the lost and late passengers even to the point of check in.

We had checked in and the crew at the gates were well aware of the passengers inside the waiting longue. But they did not cared about us and they easily pocketed RS 7000 for these humble passengers. So I request all who think to fly via Indigo to think twice. They have no regard for the passengers and they wont help but pocket and mint money only.

title: Delayed flight, passenger baked in the sun and refusing refund
text:
This is the review of a flight from Terminal 1 of Delhi airport to Pune Airport, dated 12th October 2018. We boarded the aircraft on time and then the whole problem started.
Once inside we were made to swelter in hot temperature (because the plane was grounded throughout the day) for about 2 hours. The plane did not take off because there was an issue with the documentation of the plane. According to the pilot the ATC would not allow the plane to take off because it did not have the documentation. Later we were moved to a different aircraft and the plane finally took off at 4:55 PM IST. It was a total delay of 2:15 minutes. The Indigo staff did not allow us to deplane because of "security reasons" and also they kept saying "the issue will get resolved in the next 10 minutes".

Now when I am asking Indigo for a refund and the penalty of Rs 10,000 they are refusing to comply the guidelines set by the DGCA. This flight proved to me that when it comes to taking money from customers Indigo will never let a penny go but when it comes to refunding customers, Indigo will make your life miserable.

title: Practical, Efficient airline in India
text: Indigo is a very practical no frills airline. It delivers on the fundamentals mostly and is predictable, especially in comparison to other airlines in India. Prices are competitive (key element in India), especially if booked in advance. Indigo is very well connected in India. For foreign travelers, do keep in mind that the free check in luggage limit within India for Indigo is 15 kg. Staff and service are professional, but don't give you the warm feeling. For the taller travellers, emergency row or extra space seats can be purchased online for extra INR 600 or at the airport for INR 800 (approx. 10 USD, may vary in future).  Basic food/snacks and non alcoholic drinks (hot and cold) are available for additional fees. In airports like Hyderabad and Bangalore, travellers have to  check-in at the kiosks or online first before going to the baggage drop counters (which are common for all Indigo flights). If you're delayed, it helps to ask for help from an airport staff member who will move you faster. Common queues at the airport can be long. There is no frequent flier program or observable differentiation for travellers flying frequently.  Based on multiple experiences, overall Indigo sticks to the fundamentals well and that seems to be the brand promise, expectation created/delivered for travellers.

title: Great option at Good Price
text:
I am travelling today 29th Sep 2018, from  Kolkata to Singapore by the newly introduced INDIGO flight 6E 41. I booked my ticket online through MMT and got return ticket with seat reservation at around Rs.18.8k , which was a steal considering the closest option with other airlines at Rs. 23k plus. Of course Indigo is not a full service airline and don't offer elaborate in-flight services.The scheduled departure was at  06.05 hours from Kolkata and I reached airport at 4 am. Following is my overall experience about the flight ( Rating given out of 5, 5 being the highest):-
A. Check-in: Checking at Kolkata Airport  was smooth and fast (Rating 4).
B. Lounge access: The fliht being all economy one , there was no lounge facility offered. I used my AMEX Card to access Airport Lounge.(Rating Neutral)
C. Boarding and departure: Boarding opened at 5.40 am at Gate 9. Kolkata Airport being a silent one no announcements are made as in all other international airports. Push back happened  at  6.10 hours and it took off at 6.15 hours(Rating 4). 
D. Seats and interior: The aircraft was a Airbus 320 series one and was reasonably new. The signature interior in BLUE looked bright . My booked seat was 1D, a paid aisle seat in the front that allows slight extra legroom and recline and quick access to toilet and exit. Seat pitch was ok with comfortable upholstery. Seat recline was 15 degree as per Indigo standard in Row 1, just ok for a 4 hour plus flight. Leg space was good in Row 1. The cabin was clean and had a fresh feeling.(Rating 3.5).
E. In flight services: Being a no frill flight there is hardly any in flight service.Typical tasteless Indigo meal can be bought. I dislike Indigo meal and avoided food as usual. (Rating 3.5)
F. Cabin Crew: The cabin crew in charge inside the cabin were extremely polite , efficient and helpful. I shall particularly recall the incident  when during the flight feeling hungry, I wanted to buy a packet of biscuits, the attending stewrdess could not sell it since I didn't have required change. After a little while, to my pleasant surprise, she offered me a small packet of Parle Glucose biscuits free of cost. Really appreciate her gesture. (Rate 5)
G. Arrival and baggage: Flying time was approx 4 hours and 5 minutes.Flight landed at Changi Terminal 2 on time at 1 pm and gates were opened at 1.10 pm. Luggage on the belt came fast. I collected mine at 1.20 pm. Not bad.(Rating 4.5).
H.Overall flight experience and suggested area of improvement: Overall flying experience was good and surely value for money. Early morning flight and reaching Singapore at noon is a welcome option for tourists in particular.However the following are my suggested area of improvements a)For a 4 hour International flight they should have considered slightly better seat comfort. b) They must have better menu choice. Passengers are ready to pay but give them descent options at least. They can learn from European no frill flights where food also has to be bought but you have much better choice. They can't offer pax to buy same bad menu they make available in their domestic flights c) It will be a good option to keep first 2 rows as premium economy with better seats (2×2) and better food as well. Pax are ready to pay extra for the comfort. On the whole, it was a descent experience and definitely convenient and value for money. (Overall Rating 4).

title: Very basic
text:
I flew from DOH to DEL with Indigo last week (16 SEP, 6E 1702). I know being a low cost carrier you can’t expect certain luxuries or amenities and i’m fine with that; after all it’s my choice to fly for less. 
The crew were pleasant and smiled when spoken to. The seats are comfortable and the aircraft cabin was clean. 
The toilets however were barely looked at by the crew. It was a horrid mess halfway through the flight. The toilet bowl was full, floor was wet, the toilet rolls and hand towels ran out halfway and were never replenished by the team. The girls weren’t busy, as there is no service, maybe an odd cup of water or tea being requested. I saw them seated and chatting on the forward jumpseats, but no effort was being made to look at the toilets. 
They also won’t let you take a handbag into the toilet to freshen up; safety issue they said. I don’t get it... isn’t my bag already screened and checked at the airport like a million times? Who will look after it while I’m in the lav?
Another issue is that they dont carry blankets or pillows even if u want to pay for these. So bring your own creature comforts. In addition, they NEVER switch the cabin lights OFF, even on night flights. They just dim them a bit. So do remember to carry your eye shades. 
Positives: On-time, clean seats and acceptable crew (though on some flights they just look angry all the time. This flight was pretty good by comparison). 

All in all, you get what you paid for.

title: On Time, Every Time, Reasonable Fares
text:
I travel Indigo because they have the most number of flights, on time, and also because they have a very acceptable standard of service for the price you pay. They are not always the cheapest but they are low cost and reliable service. 

I have travelled 6 times with them in the last 3 months and there was only 1 delay of around 1hr. 

More planes means they are able to rotate you into another flight quickly or another plane in automatically in case of delay. And it’s that facility which is useful especially in smaller towns where frequency is low. 

They have spent a lot of time organising themselves, so the wait at the checking or bag drop counters is reasonable even at peak hours. Boarding is efficient. They use a lot of automated scanning. Planes are always clean and toilets also. 

The food menu is not exciting but tasty and is comfort food, sufficient for a 2hr flight. Prices are high but I suppose that’s acceptable as fares are low. 

It’s worth paying extra to book an aisle or window seat or taking the combo package (seat + meal).

title: Time is of Value
text:
IndiGo’s an airline that’s always been time conscious even though they hadn’t coordinated their record flying times with the wait for the baggage. However, the past year has been very different. Not only does the flight always land on time or even a little earlier, the wait at the luggage belt has been considerably shortened. I love it when my time is valued.

Additionally, the airline’s spotlessly clean, making it easier to relax without worrying about how many germs you’re going to have to deal with. 

The food is okay, and they try out new things like the bun and tea they had for awhile, the Thai curry rice, masala tea with the low sugar option and even samosas I think. It’s sad that for quite a while now they’ve done away with the multiple flavour options for their box of cashews. But I suppose that’s because of the ages that it takes some passengers to make a choice. My suggestion to improve things in the food department  would be to train their hostesses to use really hot water for the dehydrated  food. Also, they must fill the container with hot water up to the recommended level. It’s not nice to see a great food option turned mediocre because the hostess was careless about this one thing.

One other time and temper saving hack would be to insist that only people with a single piece of cabin baggage are allowed the option of emergency exit seats. Or there should at least be a pop-up informing a customer of the stow baggage requirement when they select any of these seats. That should be easy enough to do on their web check in page.  

Summing up, I really appreciate IndiGo’s on-time performance and overall efficiency.

I flew twice with Indigo and both times they were so helpful and efficient.

By the time I had gotten to check-in, I only had twenty minutes before  they were closing the gate. title: Time change at last minute
text:
I booked a round trip from Bangalore to Hyderabad. The booking process on the site was very easy. A day after booking my trip,I was informed that my return flight was re-timed from 19.05 to 19.35. This didn't seem much then as it was only 30 minutes. However I must have received over 25 reminders via sms, calls, and emails about the flight being re-timed.

My outgoing trip was smooth and uneventful. And was hopeful that the return would be the same. I checked in smoothly and was waiting for the flight when I received an SMS at 18.50 that my flight had been delayed to 22.00.The reason for booking my flight at 19.05 was that I reach Bangalore at a good time. Now it meant that I would not reach back to my hotel till 1.00am.

When I reached the gate there was a huge crowd of people distraught about the delay. I realised that once a flight is delayed, there is no guarantee that it would ever leave at the new time. So we were boarded by 22.00. But the flight didn't depart till after 22.45. Eventually the flight landed at 12.15am. And by the time I reached my hotel it was 2.am.

title: Indigo’s social media helpline stinks
text:
My wife and me were traveling from udaipur to chennai on 15th sep 18. We were booked on 6e2315 the flight which hops via delhi. We do not need to change planes and continue to sit while they clean the plane at delhi. The flight left on time at 2:10 pm. But if anyone has been to udaipur will know that the airport is a good one hour away from udaipur vilas. So we had to leave at 11:30 am itself. While check in was good the airport did not seem to offer much to eat except a single chain having multiple outlets at very high prices. We decided to wait and eat on flight since we had a prepaid voucher which would get us a drink and some food on board. I was seated along with my wife on the first row and when food was being served had the distinction to be asked first if I would like to eat anything. Both me and my wife showed our boarding pass which had special services which included a meal. But the air hostess mandhakini said that our food would only be served from delhi but that would be well past 5 pm. She said if you want to pay then she would serve. Despite having a valid voucher which was accepted in the next sector we were forced to buy our meal again at higher prices. 
On return when I started politely tweeting to indigo about my delayed lunch the social media handlers made it messier. They kept replying to every tweet with vague replies and finally asked me to give my boarding pass which I did not have. And they said there is nothing more they could do about serving my prepaid flight three hours after 2:10 pm. Is this how indigo treats its passengers who have paid in advance for a meal? 
When you want to travel, try any other airline first since indigo’s motto is it is their way or the highway. Shame on them first for not serving a passenger his prepaid meal when he wants and serving only when he pays again and shame on them for using social media feedback tools only to keep on giving vague replies. In fact I also asked them to speak to
Me on the phone but there also it was the same shabby treatment. All I wanted was an apology and an understanding that their air hostess was wrong but their ego did not allow them to accept their mistake. Indigo will now be my last choice. But isn’t their a regulatory authority to complain to when someone messes around?

Finally we were told that the aircraft which went back to Kolkata is coming back again after refuelling in Kolkata . The whole process should take about 5 hours and we could not expect our flight before 3.30/4 pm . On our insistence they displayed the ETD at 4.30 pm . Amid angry interaction with the passengers they also behaved well .Since this happened in a far off and isolated place , the passengers were also very much tolerant . text:
I was a great fan of Indigo, for their real economy fare, on-time arrival and thoughtful service of the pretty cabin crew. Now I would like to retract my original opinion.
Last time I flew Indigo, I had an unpleasant experience, in flight 6E 323on 30/08/18.
I am 68 years old, with undyed white hair. When I stumbled inside the Mumbai Airport and proceeded towards the Indigo counter to check-in, I found a young boy wearing an ID tag of Indigo run towards me, gently took over the trolly I was pushing and guided me to a counter where I was the second and the last person. He helped me check-in fast, took away the empty trolly and guided me towards the Security check. I almost cried.
I, as most people old people do, was 2 hours early. I went and sat in front of the departure gate, and was the number two in the queue when the departure was announced.
As it may happen in economy airlines, my window seat, which I had purchased for Rs 300.00, was within a group of labourers returning from the Gulf. The young boy sitting next to me stank, and the first thing that he did was to take off his new gleaming sneakers and sit with his feet up.
The refreshment service was started after a little while after take-off. The pretty looking cabin crew who was serving my section was a little harassed as all the labourers in that zone had tickets with pre-ordered food and were making a lot of ruckus as they did not want sandwiches. I was sitting quietly waiting to be served and tried to catch her eyes. Suddenly, I find that the hostess moves further down the aisle totally ignoring me. Then I rang the bell and she comes to me with a scowl, and when I asked her the reason for denying me any service, she gave a lame excuse.
Anyway, to cut a long story short, I called for the supervisor, who got the air hostess to come and apologise to me.
That flight was about 20 minutes late, so there goes the boast of on-time airlines.
I do not think that if I am not forced to, I shall avoid Indigo like the plague.

title: No Concern for Women's Safety and Comfort
text:
This is the worst airline to fly if you are a lady traveling alone. I had read they beat up their passengers, but I still booked a flight with Indigo. As I was taking a 2.15 am flight from Trivandrum to Delhi and was traveling alone, I reached the airport, which has to be the worst in the world in terms of traveler amenities and facilities, at 8 pm and went to check-in around 8.15 pm. I was told to come back at 12.00 am; in Trivandrum, there are no cabs available after 8.30 or 9.00 pm on Ola or Uber. I was told to wait in this pre-check-in area without any restaurants or a coffee shop for the next 4 hours. When I asked to be checked in, they said they would do me a special favor and check me in, but I would have to wait until 12.30 am to go through the security check, which was the same thing as not checking in. Then came the really traumatic part. On weighing my baggage, they said I had exceeded the weight capacity of the hand baggage as they weighed my laptop bag too. When I pointed out that the laptop bag is never weighed and nor was I carrying a handbag as I was using my laptop bag for emergency essentials, they refused to consider my request. I had to empty my suitcase in front of other passengers and transfer the crisps/banana chips into a plastic cover that were in it to carry an empty suitcase as my hand baggage along with my laptop bag.
My takeaways from this experience:
1. Indigo is not a woman-friendly airline. They don't have any provision where women can physically check-in early at the airport for late-night flights when traveling alone. This is also based on my previous experience when I flew via Indigo on August 13, 2018 and they stuck me between 2 men and I was uncomfortable for the 3.25-hour flight from Delhi to Trivandrum
2. Despite seeing all the contents of my baggage and that my empty suitcase, with the stipulated hand-baggage dimensions, weighed approx. 5 kg, Indigo staff Viji and her manager, Augustine, ensured that I was embarrassed, humiliated, and subjected to unnecessary anguish and worry for baggage that was well within the stipulated cabin size.
3. The fact that laptop bags are not weighed, at least I have never seen them weighed, or that women's hand bags are not weighed either did not matter to the Indigo staff who I interacted with.
I never want to travel on Indigo again. I miss Kingfisher Airlines and Jet Airways, because both these airlines let human considerations weigh in when following the rules, which Indigo obviously doesn't because it would prefer to either physically or mentally abuse their passengers.

title: Unreasonable refusal to board flight no 6E 496
text:
As the subject suggests I missed flight no. 6E 496 from Mumbai to Indore on 29th August 2018 scheduled to depart Mumbai at 10:35am. Thanks to the overzealous professionals at the boarding counter who stands by their duty at all cost, human or inhuman!!! Indeed if Ms. Kripa was not trained to be “that perfect time keeper” I would have been able to attend a very important meeting scheduled at Indore.
Since minutes and seconds have been the bench mark to Ms. Kripa performance I would like to give my account too with “time precision accuracy” :-
I reached the airport at 10:03am. For evidence I am attaching an image of the screen at the terminal 1 which is supposed to display gate number of the corresponding flight. To my utter disappointment the screen was not working which led to wastage of precious minutes. Every time I get a message on registered mobile number regarding the gate number, but this time I have not received any message whatsoever from your end. If at all you have to contradict me send a proof for the same. Because of your short comings; First – Failure to send an SMS regarding gate number, Second – No display at the terminal regarding flight and corresponding gate number,led to wastage of precious time in reaching the boarding counter!! 
By 10:08am I was undergoing the mandatory security check, where by my phone also had to be given away in the tray and, unfortunately I got a call at the same time from indigo airlines staff as a last call to proceed for boarding. Of course I missed it as it was not with me.
By 10:10am I rushed to boarding counter and had shared the call I had received, but missed, by indigo staff with Ms. Kripa, but was refused to board the flight. Do you really think that refusing a passenger who is late only by a minute as per your staff version, with euphemisms and phrases will ever justify monetary loss and in this scenario a very important meeting I had to attend at Indore. as well.
Deferring my request to board this flight just because of a minute (10:08am I got my last call for boarding and at 10:10am I was already the boarding counter.)Seems very unreasonable and unjustifiable and by all rights I demand that a refund be processed for the same. Being late by 1 minute does not seem irrational or improbable but refusing a passenger to board a flight who is late only by a minute is irrational and subversible conduct by any airlines. Corporate SME discounts  and schemes  are offered by airlines for their clients who are frequently travelling for business purpose. Similarly airlines need to see requirements of a business traveller vis-à-vis a tourist/people who travel for leisure. Delay in reaching the destination can cost insurmountable losses to a businessman.

text:
On Time flights, clean planes, good customer service. Everything that a low cost carrier should do well.

The reason I do not give this a 5 * is simple - one of the things that Indigo requires is having the credit card on which you made the booking when you travel. With me, I had two bookings with the same credit card, one TRV-BLR and the other a UDR-JAI. 2 different legs. As luck would have it, I lost my credit card, got a replacement with a different number, and contacted 6E to tell them of this before my travel. I only mentioned my JAI-UDR leg to customer service.

I flew the TRV-BLR leg without issue. For the UDR-JAI leg, I wasnt allowed to check in online, and at the airport, was asked to present the credit card. I did take a print out of the credit card statement, so I did have proof, but I would think that since I had contacted customer service, they WOULDNT make it an issue.It seems that I would have saved myself trouble if I hadnt contacted them earlier.

title: As usual, average...
text:
Flying in IndiGo has become an average affair. It used to be a pleasure with them being a no-frill, no-nonsense, quick turnaround flight - you could almost be sure they would be on time.
They are still on time. This flight was.
Noting was wrong, but things were not as they should be.
To begin with, we were made to wait in a queue before our luggage was scanned pre-check-in. This the first time I have faced a situation where an airline employee has told me that scanning for my flight had not started yet. Please wait for five minutes. Stand here. After standing "here" for 20+ minutes and listening to the same person say: five minutes to every other passenger of the same and other flights, I asked him how many minutes made five. He said that they were waiting for late passengers of earlier flights. I don't know what prevented them from continuing to scan baggage and break the queue for late-comers.
Check in was pleasant enough, in fact, the person at the desk was very helpful, but there was no bus to take passengers to the plane from the terminal and no one to guide you which way to go. Admittedly, there was only one IndiGo plane on the tarmac, but there might have been people who needed assistance - being elderly or new (first time fliers). Similarly, there was no word of welcome to passengers as we boarded, unless you catch the flight crew's eyes accidentally. They are usually busy doing something else.
It was raining when we landed. The ramp to the rear exit was open to the skies. The ramp to the front exit had a covering. The buses stopped to cater to the front exit passengers. Those who had to exit by the rear, had to get wet as they took the three flights of the ramp, and ran the entire length of the plane to reach the bus.
The only reason to use this airline is 1) if the timing of the flight suits you and 2) if you are mindful of the amount you will save - because IndiGo is not really that inexpensive any more.
The airline allots a seat when you buy a ticket. Yet, they will insist that you select a seat if you web check-in. You will not be shown the seat that has been automatically allotted. Instead it will be marked as "already taken". You will find that only premium seats (with more leg room/ exit row) are available for a price. If you want to web check-in, only non-premium seats available would be middle seats towards the end of the fuselage.
I suggest you don't web check-in if you can reach 2 hours in advance (you need to do that if you have check-in baggage anyway). You will probably find you have an automatically allocated window seat towards the front of the plane.

Resting on the past glory just would not help, I believe. Increasingly, one has started to feel that the service level at Indigo has gone bad in the recent times. 
Just few days back I was flying to Delhi to Lucknow. It is understandable if the flight gets delayed - happens ! and I am not complaining about that. But how you deal with your patrons speaks a lot about the mentality of not just the ground staff but also the organization - as the values are seeped in across the levels of any organization.
We were made to board the shuttle after a delay of around 30-40 mins, perhaps more. But the issue was that after the boarding of the shuttle that was jam packed - much beyond the normal limits, they made the shuttle wait for long - I guess more than 30 mins before we actually boarded the aircraft. It was like animals stuffed inside a shuttle - no care about the occupants- there were families with little kids struggling to cope, there were old people who could not stand for long, I myself was uncomfortable, being a young chap - i was hardly able to manage inside the shuttle. PLUS, the shuttle that was filled later got the first boarding to the aircraft - where is the logic ? Do you even care about the passengers ?
I take indigo as sometimes it becomes absolutely necessary given the flight circuit and non availability of other flights. Else, I would never choose Indigo - this kind of callous attitude of Indigo's staff is a norm now - high time ! wake up !

The poha had raw onion and tomato in it as well as curry leaves, but not enough to give it any specific flavour. Taste- and texture-wise, this was a disappointment. 

My daughter had ordered a junglee chicken sandwich, which I ended up finishing off for her. While fresh, it had an oddly sweetish flavour and lacked any interesting contrast in texture - even the addition of a few chopped nuts would have made this better.

I have almost always had a good experience with IndiGo: this time, when it came to cleanliness and food quality, I wasn't satisfied at all. The punctuality and service was fine, however.

title: The best cabin service with worst pilot on the job
text:
I took the 17:55 flight from Mumbai Airport and as usual the flight was delayed. Initially we were assured that the flight was in time however it was well passed boarding time and we didn’t see any movement. Upon Enquiry we were informed the flight was slightly delayed. Finally boarding started after the scheduled departure time!!

In case of 5 min delay the passengers are not allowed to board the flight then why would the airlines company be not penalised for such delays. Think rules of the game should be same. Anyways the passengers settled quickly and luckily we didn’t have to wait much in the que to take off.

Immediately after takeoff, the blowers started pumping in air with great speed and force. The noise was so loud that it was hard to bear. All passengers started complaining and few were panicked. However it settled soon.

The rest of the flight was uneventful with the cabin attendants taking good care of the passengers with their plastic smiles. But we must appreciate they were very attentive and acting immediately unlike many of their competitors.

But the landing was really bumpy. In fact the worst I have experienced in my life of 38 years. With no rain or strong wind and a perfect visibility, as confirmed by the captain, we were all relaxed but boy what a landing. We should not call it touchdown but a thump down as we banged on the runway. But well we all were in one piece to write the review.

title: With Success should come Great Responsiblity
text:
This review is going to be primarily on the levels of service, customers' comfort, acting responsible without going into the other parameters. Why so? Well in today's world where we pompously talk about our being market leader, go overboard on talking about what we offer for the price, and above all trying to out-compete others how far are we going to protect our principles and sacrifice them.

So, let me begin my review with the good things first
1. Check-in desk staff: Overworked yet smiling and ready to serve which is a fantastic attitude and I take a bow. 
2. Cabin crew: Absolutely pretty, overworked yet eager to reach every single passenger with their requirements, and more importantly honest.

Now the bad bits which as a customer who has paid requires from the airline
1. Responsibility to own up to their errors and stay honest under delayed flight conditions. 
2. Increase passengers' comfort during the delay especially if we are put into the flight hurriedly to avoid accountability in case the flight gets delayed beyond a permissible time limits.
3. Give passengers who have young ones, toddlers, and ladies the benefit of de-boarding and or better comforts in case you are not able to do so due to regulations.

I was traveling from Kolkota to Bengaluru and the original departure of the flight was 2125 hrs. Then I received a sms stating that the flight has got delayed due to the delay in incoming aircraft and the reason for delay was given as traffic congestion. While the truth was that the aircraft that we boarded came from Varanasi and that flight was delayed due to non-availability of pilot who got to Varanasi on a emergency basis. Then, our flight which was to depart at the new departure time of 2205 hrs got further delayed as the pilot's licence was to be renewed before the departure of our flight. This was announced by the pilot himself after 2300 hrs before which he had told us that he was awaiting some papers from the airport authorities. In the meantime, our ordeal continued as we were made to board the flight as per schedule of departure by 2205 hrs and also to avoid any penalties that may be incurred due to the delay as per norms. Also, passengers would claim from their travel insurances or whatever other reasons, the airline just tucked us off into the aircraft and were left to ourselves. The flight finally took off around 0015-0030 hrs and we reached Bengaluru thereafter.

The most important thing in this entire episode was that till date I did not even receive a simple apology by sms forget a call for the ordeal that we underwent. So, what I understand is that the airline is doing a favor upon us by rendering the service and is not obligated or obliged to think that the customer is who makes the important aspect of their business. Well, it is pity..........

title: Airline blues
text:
Travelling by air is no longer a pleasure, and when you make the grave mistake of planning to travel on Indigo airlines, you're really in for something special (read ripoff). Probably the worst choice of airline not to be ever repeated. 

In April, a month earlier, I made an online booking (travel portal) for my wife. My own ticket was already booked for the same flight by our corporate travel  agent. Fast forward to May 29, the day before our travel. 

Our travel agent (normal practice) had already checked me in and sent my boarding pass via  email. I logged into indigo to complete her check-in so as to be able to choose a seat next to mine. But the system refused to let me log in, and after multiple tries, I called the airline. To my utter dismay, I was told that this ticket was also in MY name! What had I done! 

My worst fears were about to be realized. After a lengthy explanation about the mistake, and despite the fact that I already had another ticket in my name (and was already checked in too!) I was rudely turned down. “We don't allow changes to name, it's our airline policy” I was told. Surely your policies are there for good reason and not to hurt your customers? My pleas fell on deaf ears. “Sorry, can't help”. Buy a new ticket. What about this one?? “Sorry this will be wasted”. “But ma'am, if you check, you'll find I'm already checked in for this flight in my name on another ticket!”. How can ONE person travel on TWO tickets??? What's your policy on THAT??

The story above brings me to the heart of the issue. Indigo takes its customers for granted while also frequently taking them for a “ride”. To make it worse for passengers, there's no  recourse. I ended up paying 8000/- for a new ticket while Indigo coolly pocketed the 8000/- + 6000/- of the original ticket. Not to mention the bonus they must have made by selling that original ticket again for 8000/- or more!! 

Customer be damned. It's about grabbing as much as you can. And so what if this ONE customer won't ever travel Indigo again, there's enough business coming from our ever expanding population and innocent first time travelers.

Of course the 6000/- I had originally paid had no value. The cancellation charge of Indigo usually totals more than the ticket value paid !! Which is a whole different issue to be discussed another day and time...
