title: Oxygen for Kochi passengers
text:
As we got off from the flight at Kochi airport on 25/8/17, and came down towards the bus I was shocked to see an Air India bus at our service, an old bus with so much of high ground clearance which was so difficult for elders to board. Then as we all got into the bus it was very hot with hot air blowing out of the A/C vent. I immediately stepped out of the bus to inquire with the ground staff if something was wrong with the bus or the A/C. The staff outside the bus did not speak to me well neither did he know English or Malayalam or Hindi. I am good at all these languages and God knows what he got of me, he went straight to the driver and spoke to him, but still i was not given an answer at all. Finally i had to speak with the driver and ask him what the problem was and he told me in Malayalam that the A/C was not working for the past few days and that is the reason it was so hot. By this time the staff had pushed many more than the required passengers into the bus and the bus left. It was so suffocating and difficult to breathe for many of us and the elders in the bus were finding it difficult to stand. Thank God the terminal was not very far off and we reached in about 4 minutes and all passengers were pushing each other to go out of the bus in search of air to breathe. It was a horrifying experience as if there was no oxygen.
Next after getting into the terminal i went up to the conveyor belt and it took so long for the baggage to come over it. Meanwhile i spoke to a ground staff a gentleman who did not even bother to take note of what i was saying and just gave me  deaf ear. I grew very anxious and spoke to him in Malayalam and told him that i would seriously remark in the media if your manager does not see me now. With great reluctance he called for his manager and that gentleman arrived. Thank God he was polite and heard me completely and showed me some papers in which it was mentioned that similar complaints had come in from morning and also on previous days. He told me that he had written to the airline asking for a separate bus but so far no result had come on. He took down my name and contact number and assured me that he would take up the matter with his management.
In all it is a matter of highest concern for an airline like Indigo to be so careless and dont care attitude shown to passengers especially in such hopeless condition of buses. It just goes to show how arrogant the airline has become after getting its name across and now the true colours are being shown. Not many would write like me or tell others but i am a citizen of India and will like to tell all my fellow Indians that please carry oxygen packs with you if at all you fly Indigo into Kochi. Its also a matter of concern that Indigo is borrowing old stubborn Air India buses and unable to provide buses of its own. Most importantly attitude to resolve these issue is surely not there because they are so busy with faulty engines being replaced. I pray God that the management will open its eyes soon and prevent any untoward incident in the bus like breathlessness or fainting especially for the elders and children. 
As i have titled the review please carry oxygen masks when you fly Indigo to Kochi.
Long Live India.

title: Struggling in Indigo
text:
1. Boarding started at gate 10 well in advance. Everybody was in the line but the line stopped moving suddenly. I later discovered that there is only one bus to ferry passengers to the aircraft and the entire line of people including senior citizens like me were standing for over 8 minutes before the bus returned. Simultaneously, other IndiGo busses were ferrying passengers for flights to Delhi, Coimbatore etc. I can understand being Mumbai, there are many flights simultaneously operating. But what I can't fathom is why they can't have at least 2-3 busses continuously operating for each flight (like even in a small airport like Varanasi) so that passengers are not inconvenienced?
2. In Gate 10 (and other gates) as people are standing, there are no chairs or conveniences provided. At least, if people could sit & wait, it may not be so torturous.
3. My wife & I (and our group) had to board from the rear entrance. The bus was parked about 150' away from the rear entrance. The front entrance stairway had a rain cover but the rear one did not. It was raining rather heavily and we had to sprint to the steps and climb, all getting wet.
4. While the front entrance had a V shaped stair-case, the rear had a direct one, resulting in high steps, making it very difficult for seniors to climb.
5. In Chennai, the aircraft arrived at 11 PM and was parked really far off (may be 2 KM from the entrance, with a bad road and winding passage). Busses were jam-packed and the standees had a very tough time holding on the the handles every time the driver swerved (hanging handles were placed very high and were too few in number to cater to all standees).
6. Because of the far off parking, the luggage too took some 20 minutes to arrive.
7. IndiGo boasted of another "before-time arrival" but the proof of the pudding is in how the passengers felt jostled and when they really got to their homes. I reached only by 12.30 AM.

A.Pros

1. Young fleet, good clean aircraft
2. Active, efficient cabin crew
3. On time 
4. Clarity in check in,boarding and alighting/ baggage handling
5. Comfortable cabin

B. Cons
1. Leg room is too less and uncomfortable.

3. The web check in - most seats are charged and web check in passengers get only the last rows/ middle seats. This discourages mobile/ web check in.

Despite some pain points which I guess are prevalent in most budget airlines, Indigo is far better compared to competition in this segment. My Hyd- Blr trip was also well   executed and perfect for a business traveler. The best journey was Blr- Delhi on a A320Neo- amazing and silent cabin. really unfortunate that this fleet stands grounded due to engine issues. Will certainly recommend Indigo to one and all.

title: Indigo - best to reach you on time
text:
=> 1. Timing. 
To me, the most important & basic thing to fly is to save time. Be it for having a tight schedule, or to reach urgently to a place. Indigo, have served it very well, at least for last 5 years. I never had a Indigo flight which had a late take-off. Indigo generally do not Cancel or Change their flight schedules and do not get late, there might be problems related to signal to land or taxing to take-off, (thankfully I never faced it, only but once), but the airline itself never get late. 

=> 2. Food. 
Quite a bit costly. And not really worth of money. Quality is good, but quantity is very less compare to the cost. 
Indigo do not provide any free food/ meal, as Air India & Jet Airways do. 

=> 3. In-Flight sitting. 
Quite clumsy sitting arrangement. If a little fatty or healthy person sits, it becomes very much a problem. Also leg space is very little. 
But it is the same story for all the domestic flights from all the airlines. 

=> 4. In-Flight staff. 
Mostly all the airlines have supportive staffs. Well Air India staffs are little non-cooperative, they take too much time to get even a glass of water. 

=> 5. Airport assistance: 
Indigo attendants do help you, where to go and how to check-in & all required stuffs. If you are quite late for your flight they will escort you to urgent check-in. 

=> 6. Cost. 
Mostly Indigo fares vary in the lower range among all the airlines. But as I said few of them provide free food. 

=> 7. In-flight entertainment: 
Nothing. No TV/ Movies/ Songs/ Wifi.  

=> 8. Cleanliness. 
Excellent. 

Indigo overall: 
Timing, Staffs - excellent & helpful. 
Food - too costly, very less quantity. 
Siting in-flight: very little space to sit and very little leg space.

title: Nickle & Dime airline
text: An airline that will go to any extent to dip into your wallet. While fares appear lower than Jet and others at times, they more than make up for it on the charge for everything once you buy your ticket! Charge for seat choice in almost the entire aircraft, with the exception of the last few rows on the plane. So whether you choose an aisle/window in an exit row, or from row 1 to 20 something, you got to pay - just because you're making a choice! You also pay for water, food, tea, coffee. And whats worse, I had a bad cold before taking the flight, which led to pain in my ears. They don't even keep that most basis of item for passenger comfort - cotton buds or cotton in any form. This most basic item carried on all airlines (including Air India!) since the 1950's !!! title: If you are on budget, fly IndiGo
text:
I have lost count of the number of times I have had to fly with IndiGo in the recent years. Hence trying to summarise my overall impression.

First the pluses ->

1. 80%+ of the cases, they are on time. Whenever they are on time or even a minute before the ETA, they tend to brag a lot stating that IST (Indian Standard Time) is actually IndiGo Standard Time. Brings a smile but also a smirk since whenever they are late (for whatsoever reason), the crew remains silent about it!

2. The number of cities covered and the timing options are probably far better than most of the other players operating in the domestic sector. 

3. If you purchase roasted cashew nuts / almonds etc, the container can be used for multiple purposes at home :o)

Now the minuses ->

1. Food -> Be mentally prepared to have stuff which is usually consumed cold or chilled [aerated drinks] in the room temperature and those we usually have hot [sandwich / roll etc] in a chilled manner. Of late, I have found that the upma served is the only palatable stuff.

2. Seating -> Uncomfortable to say the least. Disclaimer - I am of average height and built but I still find the leg space inadequate and the additional charges they ask for "supposedly better" seats are a rip off

3. On Flight Entertainment -> Zero Options and hence unless the flight you choose is lesser than 90 - 100 minutes, you are in for a tough time if you are not of the meditative kind or have a wonderful capability to doze off in crowded local trains.

4. On Flight Service & Staff Behaviour -> Usually polite but quite often pretty rude and they are so obsessed to be able to chant "Indigo Standard Time" that many a times basic necessities of passengers are overlooked. I was unfortunate to have boarded their flight once with a sore throat and repeated requests for a few glass of warm water was not entertained -- either the staff was busy for take off and latter busy to sell the food and other merchandises. 

So to sum up, yes, fly by this airlines [I do fly] if you want to save some money and be more or less on schedule. Do not by mistake expect any special request to be entertained as most of the folks employed do not understand what that means.

At 1500 hrs, they served a snack box. They were able to give me an additional one after all the passengers got one.
The Indigo plane bearing passengers from Kolkata finally arrived at 1630. My flight took off at 1700 hrs. The air crew took extra efforts to answer the many questions passengers had. They were all smiles. The took service to another level.
IndiGo is one of the few institutions in India that leaves you satisfied. I cannot say the same for others.

text:

The turn around & baggage handling was done very fast in spite of the heavy rains pouring on the tarmac, where the staff were doing their job.They were ready to take off within twenty minutes of delay but the heavy stack of aircraft lined up for landing & take off all operating only from one runway, delayed it further.Entering the aircraft there was assurance & confidence radiated by the flight attendants proudly displaying their "Girl Power",the emblem badge visible on their forearms! The eats & beverages were good.

On landing,i was amazed to see my baggage on the convyer belt within just two minutes of my reaching the site! No wonder Indigo with its prompt & efficient services commands nearly 40% of the market share, with the next one Air India only 14%! They are the first ones to bid for the Air India privatisation & i do hope that they get to keep India`s flag proudly flying abroad !

title: These guys are professional and take security very serious
text:
I took a early morning flight and business was as usual. After all, how much can you tell about a 2-3 hour coach flight?

My attention was caught when I saw the discipline of the procedure that the crew followed when the cockpit crew wanted to use the bathroom. 

In one word: impressive. 

They did it exactly the way it has to be done by first blocking the way to the front with a trolly that was guarded by a stewardess, then locking the toilet after which the purser entered the cockpit and the captain could make use of the bathroom. After him the co-pilate had her turn and the security measures were unwinded. 

I am a frequent flyer mostly in Europe and I have not seen this follow up on security even with my all time favourite Lufthansa. If Indigo are so disciplined with this I feel safe to assume that they are disciplined with the rest of my safety as well. It feels good and I am now an official Indigo fan.

text:
I have always preferred traveling via Indigo airlines for their impeccable on-time service and highly professional staff. This flight too matched my expectations on these attributes. The staff on the ground as well as in the air demonstrated utmost professional conduct and behavior. The flight took off and landed on-time.

The security checks during check-in were hassle free and smooth. 

The boarding experience could have been better at the Bhubaneswar airport. The staff did not use the public address system to announce the boarding sequence. Most passengers could not hear the boarding staff announcements clearly and hence ended up crowding the boarding gate. That caused avoidable inconvenience.

The inflight experience was not so great, the aircraft's seats (Economy class) were too firm and offered no lumbar or comfortable neck support. This is the case with almost all the aircrafts that Indigo operates. 

Further, some passenger was playing some kid's audio continuously (on speaker and not on headphones) probably to keep his/her kid amused through the flight. That caused avoidable irritation. It is sad that despite complaining to the air hostess, there was no respite observed.

Other than that, as usual, the flying experience was good, hassle free, predictable and on time.

The flight we took from Dubai to Delhi and back, did not have individual / common TV screens, so be sure to carry your iPads while traveling with Indigo. The plane(s) were old but visibly well maintained. We paid a little extra for the first row seats, which was a requirement to sit comfortably. I'm confident that the other non-leg room seats would have been uncomfortable for our 4-hour flight. The flight attendants were friendly, although we hardly interacted with them as refreshments were not included in the price of the flight. There is an option to order refreshments from the in-flight menu for an additional charge. The seats were just satisfactory, and not very comfortable. We had trouble sleeping during our night flight as we were tossing and turning on our concrete seats.
What I liked best was the neat interiors (despite the age of the plane), and what I liked least was the seats.

title: Poor Little Budget Cousin
text:
I remember my childhood. Flying Indian Airlines was such a pleasure. An all economy class with good food served on board. Then came the monopoly and they started charging hefty fees for each sector. "Enter the Deccan" with the promise to fly every single Indian. Exit the Deccan and enter Indigo. With a whiff of swanky new aircrafts, good connections, hip air hostesses and a promise to be on-time every-time. 10 odd years down the line with a stiff competition from other full fare and budget airlines, Indigo has stood out on few fronts:
1. Most of the time they try and are on-time. 
2. They offer the latest air buses which are fun to fly on and safe too
3. Their network has spread far and wide and they are the largest airline of India today

But they do have their handicaps:
1. Budget my foot, apart from doling out a few 1000 buck tickets, they are at par with
    other full fare airlines most of times. This can only happen when there is a cartel.
2. The leg space on the aircrafts is pathetic. If they could, they would make people sit  
     in each others laps !
3. Though sold for money on-board, the food offered is also pathetic except tea, 
     cookies and nuts and maybe sandwiches.
4. They try and charge you every single penny where they can. Put in an extra kilo
     in your bag, pay 250 bucks. Make your bag arrive first, pay a few dollars. Want
     a comfortable seat, shell out a few bucks. The list never ends. I often wonder,    if        they could even charge  their passengers to review their services !!
5.  The staff is callous and impolite. That is their biggest drawback. In the rush to
     be on time and finish as many as trips possible in a day, they forget basic courtesy
     an airline staff needs to offer.

Now compare the frills with the chills. If Air India is poor and falling apart, Jet never forgets to serve with smile albeit at a price.  Spice Jet and Go Air have their own problems and a pan India connectivity eludes both airlines.

Maybe India awaits another half fare/low fare airline which would offer better services?
Guys and gals , airline business is all about service and not selling. And maybe Indigo has forgotten that.

title: Horrible experience- indigo running a racket
text:
I have travelled with this airline a number of times and had a good experience, though i had heard people complaining about how unscrupulous they can be. Somehow i had the misfortune to be on the wrong side and had a bitter experience. I along with my family (wife and two children) was scheduled to travel by Indigo Flight 6E 921 from Delhi Terminal 1D to Kolkata on 29th December 2016. PNR no. KD5CTD. The departure time was 13:40 hours and the boarding time was 12:55 hours from gate no. 8B. We reached the airport at 12:15 hours and reached the boarding gates at 13:05 hours and the sign at the boarding gates read Indigo flight Kolkata 6E 921 with people standing in the queue. So we also stood in the queue. The queue started moving and progressed towards the gate counter by 13:20 hours. We patiently stood in the queue under the impression that the flight was marginally delayed. At 13:35 hours when we actually reached the boarding gate counter, we were told by Ms. Nancy that our flight had left and that the queue was for the subsequent Delhi- Patna flight. We protested that how could this happen and how were we to know that our Kolkata flight had left when the sign at the counter was still showing Kolkata flight. On realizing this, the personnel at counter quickly changed the screen sign to that of Patna flight. When we again protested then, Mr. Guruprakash who was at the counter shouted at us that it was our fault and that this is a silent airport and that they are not allowed to make announcements.  But I guess in a silent airport you are allowed to play bhajans and songs at load volume but not allowed to make announcements to help passengers!!!
Ms. Savita Rai who was the manager also refused to help us, saying that she needed to investigate. By the way, I am not exactly sure what is she going to investigate, since she neither asked for my name or details of my boarding pass!
At the counter they just took away our passes stamped them and then told us we could book fresh tickets for a much higher cost. They then realized that we were 4 passengers and they did not have any seats available. When I requested her to help me out, the attitude of your staff left me fuming. Believe me, with two small children travelling I was left fumbling and helpless. I kept running from one airline to another with no seats vacant.  I subsequently took the help of a travel agent who advised me split my family and I was forced to book separate tickets on Spice jet and Jet airways at very high price (Rs. 64000/- apporx for 4 passengers).
Since me and my wife are both doctors, we both had important appointments fixed up for the day, which had to be cancelled and our patients inconvenienced.

We also realised that we were not the only people to miss the flight. There were few more persons who missed the same flight even after collecting boarding passes from the counter. And it then made me wonder as to why a passenger should be harassed like this.
I also got to know that Indigo does this quite often.

title: competitive LCC, some minor things get irritate
text:
First off, let's put the most important deal-breaking things into perspective. Prices are competitive against other LCCs (SpiceJet, GoAir) and mainline carriers (Jet and Air India). Scheduled timings are OK. One thing that stands out IndiGo out from other LCCs is that it has a much larger network of routes.

However, that being said, there are a things which does irk about IndiGo. The airline code (6E) sounds cute maybe the first or second or third time you heard it read aloud. After that, it just irritates. And unfortunately the airline code is read out time and again: when you check-in, when you try find your boarding gate, when passengers are called to board, when you are onboard and the captain reads out a welcoming message, when you land and the captain reads out a thanks for choosing 6E message, etc. etc. etc. Quite clearly, the airline code wears out its welcome very quickly.   There's also a bit of a cognitive dissonance to hearing that read out so often about the airline, and then you look around: how? 

Another issue is more localised to DEL T1 domestic departures. The terminal is a bit cramped. There is a relatively limited choice of take-away place for breakfast. (Had a plane to catch --- the physical check-in ate away all the time I had left for doing a sit-down meal...) Foreign purchasers cannot check-in online as the airline insisted checking your credit card at check-in counter. (Call centre was at least quick to confirm that, thanks.) And the terminal-to-tarmac buses are a little slow and cramped and hot. An LCC can be expected to be a little less smooth sailing than other carriers, but it does irritate a little when you are on the bus waiting to head off to the aircraft, and it just sits there, and meanwhile it's a bit like a steamer inside, you're beginning to sweat a little, and it's only 6:15am -- oh and you're still trying to munch on your take-away breakfast samosa.  In comparison, another domestic flight using T3 (for arrival) was more comfortable and easy to connect to local public transport. (Whether the taxi drivers take your business is something else.)  

Fell asleep for the entire flight (to Kochi, 3.5 hours). Can't comment on the service. Obviously the legroom and comfort were sufficient to fall asleep upon.

title: Frequent Flyer Smiles - is a joke
text:
For the last few days Indigo Airlines has been publishing full page ads in the newspapers, claiming they have the least amount of complaints of all airlines. I laughed bitterly at the malicious joke the ads contain becaus Indigo has very devious ways of minimizing the complaints they receive or taking any constructive action on them.

A couple of weeks back, my wife and I flew on a domestic Indigo flight. During the flight, my expensive suitcase (which, incidentally, had been marked 'fragile') was so badly handled that one of its roller wheels was broken off. Since I used the airport trolley to carry the bag to the car, I noticed the breakage only when I reached my destination address. I was naturally eager to complain about this poor handling and claim reimbursement or replacement. Therefore, I attempted to respond to the Indigo feedback request email that I received soon after the flight on my mobile phone itself. The form is so poorly designed that it is virtually impossible to read on a smartphone. This is step 1 in Indigo's battle to reduce customer complaints. 

All the same, I persisted. However, while I was shifting the phone to landscape mode (to make the small fonts slightly more legible) I was suddenly thanked for submitting my feedback which I had scarcely started filling in. What is worse, every successive attempt to use the same link met with the same response ie that the feedback had already been submitted. This is step 2 in Indigo's formula for reducing customer complaints. 

While these stratagems to prevent complaints  from reaching the airlines may be good for gathering favourable statistics, they are clearly not the right way to actually cut complaints.

When I saw the ad boasting about Indigo's matchless complaint record, I was stung into digging out a general email id from their website (there is no specific one for customer complaints) and sending an email conveying my problem. I received a typical bureaucratic response saying they can't do anything to help. I had been exposed to step 3 of Indigo's way of not recognizing customer complaints. 

I am waiting to see whether escalation within the airline brings any results before taking up the matter in other forums. I guess I wouldn't be so upset if they didn't practice an Orwellian doublespeak in their ads claiming to be the best on an attribute where their actual performance is so dismal.

title: Missed flight due to huge crowd at security check
text:
Hi,
 I have booked tickets to travel to Visakhapatnam from Hyderabad by 6:35 AM flight on 15th Feb 2017. I have booked 5 tickets  

We have reached RGIA hyderabad well before time and took the boarding pass at 5:30 AM, we did not have any check in baggage and we headed towards security check near the immigration counters, there is big queue at the security check. The security check personnel, even though we requested to make it quick due the flight time, they did the process completion at 6:15 AM.  All through this while my mother is standing in the queue being a senior citizen and having her both knees operated for knee replacement.  There were so many people who requested the CISF authorities to help as everyone need to catch their flights.  But there was no positive response. 

We headed to Gate number 25E by 6:20AM where in a indigo representative helped my mother to reach the same in a wheel chair. The lady officer informed that the gates are closed. Being a silent airport there weren't any announcements made, but to my surprise the office said she made announcements. Also she said the flight took off at 6:25 AM. We asked, her how could it go 10 minutes before time, for which she said they got clearance from Air Traffic Control and so the flight took off(which looks a false statement made, as your call center officer today 16/feb/2017 confirmed that flight took on on time).  She also said to go and complain with CISF and she cant do anything. Indigo will not take the responsibility of the delay caused by CISF. Listening to the same, i asked her to help me to speak to concerned indigo authority for which she said, she was the responsible and final authority.  

Along with us there were several other people who were also stuck at the security check and got delayed due to the same security check , they were also supposed to travel in the same flight. 

I am supposed to travel in the morning flight and return back in the evening flight. But due to the delay caused in the security check which was not our fault, where in we were pretty much on time because of which we were issued the boarding passes also by the executives. We lost 20,100/- which i have paid towards booking the flight tickets. 

We were in continuous touch with officials yesterday at the airport and even tried to see if they can accommodate us in the next flight at 8:45 AM which wasn't successful. Mr XXX one customer service officer also said and acknowledged that this is almost a daily routine that is happening from the recent past at this airport at this particular timing due to the security check and several people are missing the flights because of which indigo is getting a bad name. 

 If such was the case and your officers were aware of this. The operators should have atleast informed the passengers about the same in advance. I spoke to Mr Shareef to see if he can arrange for next immediate flight and i was ready to pay the difference which he informed as 3200/- per person. Finally at the exit Mr XXX who issued us boarding passes helped us to move out of the exit gate after making an entry also was surprised that we missed the flight as he was saying, "Sir you took boarding passes much before and how could you miss?"

I am also surprised that along with 15 of us there are passengers who were supposed to travel on indigo flights to Bengaluru, Mumbai also could not make it and missed their flights. 
Thanks

title: Indigo again
text:
I went to a conference in Mumbai from Kolkata on 12th January 2017 and came back on 14th January 2017 via Indigo flights.
I have reviewed Indigo flights here before as well, but this time want to put in two things which I thought I should mention for the sake of other would-be travelers.

Firstly,Indigo served a Chicken hot dog inflight,which though tasted bland and pretty ordinary caused a mild stomach upset for me. I am giving the benefit of doubt here to Indigo,as I cannot pinpoint to it exactly. I was on the 6E 596 flight.

Secondly, after boarding the return flight (6E 395)from Mumbai, I noticed a peculiar thing which my accompanying pictures will show. There was a kite on the roof of our flight,when it was standing on the apron,and Indigo personnel were joyfully trying to bring the kite as well as its long string down. 
Isn't it unsafe for a kite to be inside the airport area,getting entangled on the roof of a plane,which is about to be airborne ??!

Nothing to do with Indigo I guess,but then I hope DGCA reads these reviews. I will send two emails - to DGCA as well as Mumbai Airport authority to ask them to look into this serious matter.

Apart from these two things,overall the flights were good and incident free. On board food was pre-booked with my tickets

title: Level of the airline has gone down drastically
text:
Over the years me & my family has used IndiGo airlines and it has been our first choice in India even including the big names in the domestic market.
So it was a huge shock when we booked couple of flights from them around a wedding and not one flight took off in time. This is all around winters in 2016.
From Patna to Delhi, the flight was delayed by more then 2 hours. The ground staff was trying to just keep us at bay and I don't think the right reason was shared. To give him credit, he never lost his patience. Finally, when I got down in Delhi airport, the line I saw of people waiting on IndiGo counter at the airport. Couple of flight may have got cancelled & there was just one person handling all the customers.
My wife & her cousins were taking the flight from Patna to Lucknow on the same day just after my supposed departure but after their flight being delayed by two hours, they could only make to Delhi as they couldn't land in Lucknow due to fog. I believe if the flight was on time, it should not have been an issue. Then there luggage took more then a hour to come out.
To top it up, when we flew from Lucknow to Delhi a few days after, the flight was just half an hour delayed which is fine but while checking-in our luggage, we had extra weight & had to pay for it. And the staff at the counter told me it is better to pay by cash as the payment by machine will take more then 15 minutes. I could not just imagine that all the customers are waiting & then one customer will just stand on the counter for 15 minutes blocking everyone behind him. And this was the time when country was going demonetization & cash was not freely available. One of the major airlines of India does not have enough card machines.
Overall, IndiGo prides upon reliability & customer service (flight crew customer service was still high) but they were far below that this time in my experience. The fog will be there everytime and is not a surprise in winters in North India. If they could not manage the flights and keep them on time, it just seems to be an airline company which has lost its mojo. I am not sure if I am going them again especially during winters.

title: Clean, simple & easy
text:
I am a regular flier with IndiGo. I love their simplicity, speed (Must say the ad agency who worked on the copy for the airline has done a fabulous job!) and clean, lean & brand new A320s.

I must have flown them about 7-8 times this year alone. Every time I have had great experience dealing with the cabin crew. I really appreciate how they are humble, patient and genuinely helpful. This is a great departure from certain "world class" and "national" carriers who offer a lot of non-human comfort, but when it comes to human element (cabin crew) they fail. 

I see plenty of low income workers traveling to India from the Gulf region, and it is wonderful to see how these staff members treat them so cordially.

Really special thanks to them. They make IndiGo great experience. And their trainers.

I also need to add they never "over charge" you. I have noticed IndiGo prices are lowest even during peak times despite their popularity.

I wish they place a few screens on each side to let passengers know where they are in their journey. In this information age when everyone is used to tracking their whereabouts, not knowing that is a distressful part.

I would also wish if the Captain can be a bit more interactive. 

These two small things can make this Airline perhaps the best Indian airline (I do not care for those surveys etc that says IndiGo is not. I have about 15 flights to look back to when I say this)

title: crawl out of their obligations
text:
I flew to Jaipur from delhi on 02-01-17 through indigo and the handle of my suitcase was ripped of by the baggage handlers. I thought ok i will send them an email about it when i get to my hotel which I did a couple of days later together with photos. After a few days i got an email back from them saying that unfortunately i should have complained about it at the airport in Jaipur on landing. This is a ridiculous, the flight was an early one and I had to get up at the crack of dawn to have breakfast and get tax it airport and i was really tired when i landed. They knew that my bag was in perfect condition when it was loaded because if it wasnt they make a note of it on their records just to protect against scams. I know this for a fact because a few days later I flew with Indigo from Jaipur to Hyderabad and the check in clerk pointed out that the handle was broken and made a note of it and, (I think), asked me to sign something to that effect. Where on earth do they think that this handle was ripped off? By the driver of my 4 star hotel that picked me up from Jaipur airport and took me back 3 days later. Or perhaps they think I ripped it off myself in a fit of pique.
Compare this to another of India's low cost airlines GoAir. On 17-01-17 I was booked on their 8 am flight from Bangalore to Delhi in order to connect with my Jet Airways flight back home to Manchester at 1-30 pm. I had ample time between flights - 3 hours between landing and take off but there was fog in Bangalore and the flight was 2 hours late to take off. title: No Go To IndiGo
text:
Hi, I have always flown Indigo and even repeatedly suggested so to my friends since Indigo's punctuality is well known. However, my recent flight experience has left me tremendously disappointed. I was flying from Kolkata to Delhi (6E 9206) on Jan 1st and had been waiting in the queue for almost an air since it was crowded and on reaching the check in counter, was told that the check in for the flight had closed already. The flight was scheduled to depart at 5:25 and believe me when I say that there had been no staff coming and asking for passengers going to Delhi. I understand that the airport is a silent airport but flying Indigo regularly from Kolkata to Delhi, I am well aware that the staff asks for the passengers. It was a particularly crowded day and the airport short on staff which resulted in not just me but at least 4-5 other passengers to miss the same flight. Now I really am not complaining about the missed flight here. Perhaps I should have been there earlier. What followed that is what really bothered me. I had a connecting international flight from Delhi and it was imperative that I got up on a plane. I was directed to the counter 16C where a lady (assistant customer relation or something) refused to even look at me inspire of my repeated pleas to find me the next flight. I wish I remembered her name since she chose to lecture me about missing the flight for 15 minutes rather than find me a solution. And after I fully explained my connecting flight situation, she looked at the lady next to her and said that she was leaving and that I go to the next counter. Now the lady on the next counter kept talking on the phone and wishing people happy new year, while I silently waited for an alternate flight. A gentleman from the staff. Dominic Chettry I think was also around and I asked for alternatives. He looked blankly at my face and said that there are no flights today, and to come back tomorrow. I kept insisting and after almost 50 minutes of waiting, he showed me to the booking counter, where I got a ticket to the next flight scheduled at 7 in no time. Others who missed the flight too had no option but to book the next one since they were all flying abroad from Delhi. BTW the flight difference fee was 7k. Now, If there were tickets available, why did Mr.Dominic ask me to go back exactly? Imagine the stress it caused to someone who had to fly to another continent in a few hours. Now I hear that the 7 pm flight was delayed till 10:30 and that I should go to Coffee and More for complimentary refreshment. I was quite happy that there had been arrangements from the airlines. Now once at Coffee and More, they asked me to go to gate 22. I went there and a lady was there who asked me to follow her, I waited for her and then followed her only to see her to go ahead and chat with her colleagues. I really don't understand why is it so hard to take a little care of your flyers? I mean flight delays happen and flights get missed, that is fine. But it is the attitude of the staff that really makes it smoother. I was made to run around from 1 point to another to pick up refreshments for a flight that was delayed due to no fault of mine. Eventually I paid for my own refreshments at the food court as Indigo clearly had no intention of even letting me know about when or where to get it from. Now if you think, that this sort of behaviour is acceptable, then so be it. But in my flying experience, this was unpleasant and I would voluntarily not choose Indigo again. 
PS. I was flying from Goa to Kolkata on Dec 28th (6E 633) and that flight too was 2.5 hours late.

text:
Although Indigo has been known for being on time, this was the time when it just disappointed me. 
My flight was at 8pm from Nagpur which would have reached Bangalore by 9:45pm but instead it left from Nagpur at 10:15pm and landed in Bangalore at 12:15am.
The only good part was that I was well informed that my flight is delayed and so I was not stranded at airport unlike some other unfortunate passengers.

While this was acceptable to me that the flight got delayed since it was coming from Delhi where due to heavy fog conditions many flights and trains were being cancelled, it was bad on the airline's part where after landing in Bangalore all passengers had to wait for more than 20 mins for coaches to come which would take us to the arrivals. ( attached are pictures).Moreover there were senior citizens and ladies travelling with infants but no help was offered to them especially when the flight was delayed more than 2 hours. 

And those who are aware about bangalore would know that the city is far from airport and even at night it takes at least an hour to reach anywhere. I reached my hotel at 2am where I would have reached there by 11:30pm in a normal scenario.

And this is just one case. Few of my friends were coming from Mumbai to bangalore the next day. Their flight was at 4pm and at around 2pm when they were waiting in the queue to check in, they get an sms saying the flight is delayed and would take off at 8pm. (In reality it took off after9pm)

As per Indigo's policy you can cancel your ticket if it the flight is delayed for more than 2 hours and that's what my friends tried. But the ground staff was not only unhelpful but also rude to them. But luckily there was another flight by Jet in an hour and they managed to get on it by making extra payments. 

Everything might seem unfortunate, but when you are in service industry, you must understand how to keep customers happy when things don't work out. Probably some water and snacks in the delayed flight would have helped the passengers and informing the delay on time would have been great.

title: Indigo AIrlines - "PLEASE DON"T BE IN AIRLINES BUSINESS"
text:
Short Story

Indigo took full advantage of Bangalore's bad fog morning on Jan 20th.They've not only successfully disrupted ours(family of 4 with 2  young kids) trip, but didn't leave any mark left in causing enough tension, trauma, starving, stranded, us at airport.They failed to meet their promise, we were at loss and finally were forced to give up and cancel our onward journey from Bangalore to Jaipur via Madras.

Long story

I had planned and booked my airline tickets from musafir.com to fly on Jan 20th from Bangalore to Jaipur via Chennai on Indigo for onward and return flight was on Air Asia on Jan 27th.Basically to visit-support my recently widow’d mother-in-law.

On Jan 20th we all left our home at 3:45AM to Bangalore airport to board Indigo flight 6e233.We found that original departure of  our 6:20AM flight was delayed due to fog, finally we were able ti board the flight at 8:15AM.We were seated in the flight until about 9:30AM, but the flight didn’t take off, even though the sky got cleared earlier.Passenger's anxiety grew as many had connecting flight to either Port Blair or Jaipur from Chennai, as it was cutting it close.

Around 9:30AM suddenly in-flight announced, asking all Jaipur and Port Blair passengers to disembark the flight.When I enquired, Indigo staff promised and assured that they are arranging a direct flight to Jaipur.I was bit skeptical, but had no choice, I guess than to disembark.We were asked to collect our checked-in luggage from arrival conveyer belt.We waited more than an hour for our checked-in luggage to show up on belt.

Finally at about 10:45’sh to 11AM’sh  we got our checked-inluggage.Then we approached the Indigo’s group operations customer service counter hoping as promised to get us in direct flight.There were others already there who were in similar boat asking Indigo for direct flight as promised.Some where student flying to Imphal, some had package trip to Port Blair and about 25’sh for Jaipur.

The operation staff their at that time were Ramya, Santhosh. These guys have seen such rude and uncourteous.
Rather than  meeting what was promised, they wasted our time.At 1:30-to-2PM’sh they gave us ultimatum with only one option to either go with midnight flight
which was departing 12AM to Jaipur from Bangalore or leave it.

The Chennai(MAA)-Jaipur(JAI) flight # 548 was also delayed and left at 1PM from Chennai.The flight from Bangalore to Chennai left around 10:30’sh.
We all could have easily made it to our next leg flight from Chennai.Rather Indigo made us suffer.How pathetic and low this airlines can go.

My kids were 6 and 10 year old, tired as they’ve been awoke since 3AM and have not eaten anything.
They failed to offer decent breakfast, but rather settled by giving cheap unhealthy(chips, biscuit) snack box.
They never offered accommodation for passengers whose flight was scheduled more than 8 hours later.
They are hideous.Never acknowledged their mistakes, but gives lame excuses and blames other.
They will never put on other airlines flight.Inefficient airlines.
Indigo plays games with customers, IMO.They cover up.

Although Indigo has cancelled my tickets and promised to full refund, thanks, but no thanks because of so much loss I incur.
I took a day off from work to travel, my kids took a school day early off on Jan 20th.
Who will pay for all the trauma my family had to go through.
Who will pay for my return air tickets which also has to be cancelled, I”ll be losing 10,000 rupees at least against cancellation.
I will have to now follow up and waste my time in calling agent, Indigo, etc.

“MY KIND ADVICE TO ALL FAMILY AND OLD PEOPLE, THINK TWICE BEFORE TAKING THIS WORLD”S MOST UN-CUSTOMER FRIENDLY CENTRIC  AIRLINES”.

Pathetic service with pathetic customer behavior.

While travelling from Bangalore to Chandigarh, my bag got misplaced because of carelessness of indigo staff.

While waiting for long in the baggage claiming area in Chandigarh Airport, I went to ask one of the staff member about my bag. He went for inquiring about the bag and came up saying that we don't know where is your bag, we have to check it out. I was really surprised to see his reaction.

And the day when I had to go back i.e; 7th December 2016, I started from my hometown to Chandigarh. After reaching Chandigarh I got a message that my flight is cancelled. I was totally mad on them because I don't know where to go then. I got a mail where i can book another flight or take the refunded amount. title: The worst airline
text:
I used IndiGo in March 2017. Everything was great. Naturally, I went for IndiGo in my recent trip to India. What a mistake? I couldn't believe how far things can worsen? First, let me describe the positive parts, that are still good, then I will get into the negatives.

The flying staff, cleanliness of the planes, service in the plane, staff servicing the counters are all great. Although, on my flight from Bhubaneswar to Delhi, the tray table had a big dead bug on it, which the service personnel quickly swiped off and didn't even allow me to take a picture. But overall this part of the experience was good. 

The "terrible rating" for customer service is not for in-flight service, check-in or flying staff on the plane, but for call center service staff and web site service operations.

Now come the negatives and the nightmares. Too many to list. Let me describe them item by item and number them.

1. The booking website has numerous errors or has been intentionally designed to rip off customers. While booking my ticket, I purchase 6E upgrade (Rs. 2500), which entitles you to free choice of premium seating and free meals on your flight. But when I selected seats, the website charged me Rs. 600 per flight. Similarly, I was asked to choose between veg / non-veg meals, and charged Rs. 500 per meal.

2.  I called IndiGo's Call Center. There response was try later as the website is unstable. I tried later. This time I was able to assign seat and meal for the Outbound flight without any extra charges, but not for the return. I had to call Customer service and get the seats and meals assigned manually. But when I got on the return flight, there was no record about my 6E upgrade, so the service Staff wanted to charge for the meal. I had to show them my ticket to get the free meal, that I was entitled to.

3.   Prepaid Excess Baggage rip-off scam: On IndiGo's website the excess baggage charges for 30 Kg is either Rs. 3375 or Rs. 6750 (see attached screen shot). It's not clear what is the correct amount. Last March, they had charged me Rs. 7500 for 30 Kg round trip. So naturally, I assumed the round trip 30 Kg excess bag charge may have dropped due to competition. But when I booked the ticket on their website, I was charged Rs. 8000 for the 30 Kg excess baggage. A difference of Rs. 1250. I sort of ignored the difference and rationalized it as inflation and booked the ticket. But when I printed the ticket, I realized the Rs. 8000 was for only the Delhi to Bhubaneswar flight. If I wanted 30 Kg excess bag for the return flight, I had to pay another Rs. 8000. Between March and December it's an increase of more than 200%. The lower prices shown on website and the higher prices charged while booking, is the classic "bait and switch" scam that's illegal in most countries.

4.  For 3 days before my return flight, I tried to buy prepaid excess baggage, but IndiGo's website kept giving errors with a message to call a customer service number. I called the customer service number. Their response was, " we can't do anything; this can only be done on the website; try the website later." The classic "let the customer run around in circle" strategy. 

5.  On the day of the flight, I tried the website and got the same error message. So I called the customer service again and asked for a resolution. The rep said the only other way to get this done is to go to IndiGo's airport office. I asked to talk to the supervisor. I was put on a 15 minutes wait and then the rep came back and repeated the same stuff all over again and said the supervisor is not available and hung up on me. This appeared to be IndiGo customer service's best strategy. When you can't solve the customer's problem, just hang up the phone. They hung up on me at least 10 times.
    
6.  So as a last resort, I dashed off to the airport and tried their reservation office. The girl at the counter said they can't do it as they don't have the system capability. So I asked, can I be eligible for the lower prepaid excess baggage rate, since IndiGo's website was not working. The response was "NO"; per their rule if you don't prepay 6 hours before scheduled departure time, you have to pay the full rate. It doesn't matter that their website was not working for 3 days before the flight.

7. Finally, I had no choice but to minimize the contents of my bags from 30 kg excess baggage to 10 Kg and leave behind lot of stuff; and pay the full rate on the excess baggage.

Summary: 
1. I believe I was overcharged for excess baggage.
2. Customer service is atrocious. No help at all. Don't even try to resolve your problem. Very illogical, irrational and parrot like in their response. They hang up the phone, when you ask to escalate the call. Makes you run in circles.
3. Website is error prone and deceptive. Tends to overcharge you multiple times for the same service.
4. Avoid this airlines at all cost. Try Vistara or GoAir. I haven't tried them yet. Hearing from others that, these two are way better than IndiGo.

title: Airline has grown beyond manageability and lost its Hospitality
text:
Indigo was my preferred Airline after Jet, Kingfisher. They had a record of ontime arrivals. Hospitality and treatment to customers was good. Pricing was economical.
Now they have grown very large and beyond manageablility. The treatment to customers is very bad, the manner of leading ladies and cabin attendants is gruff and at times insulting for senior citizens like me. 
Never Never pre-order meals while doing online booking either on their site, Make My trip or Yatra. They give no priority in delivery and you have no choice - I was given a 'Nut case' as I did not want Dal Chawal at 5.30 PM ! What an insulting way to treat customers who paid Premium for window and Middle seats. 
The cabin announcements by the captains are mumbled lingo and I wonder what would happen if there is an Emergency how the Captain or FO - First Officer will communicate with passengers? 
They quote DGCA and ban on powerbanks in checkin luggage and Samsung phone on both checkin and cabin baggage - but NO ONE CHECKS ! So much for flight safety.
I sent two SMS feedbacks which had very prompt auto replies - that's IT !  
I have decided not to go with Indigo any more. Not friendly to senior citizens to say the least.

title: HORRIBLE experience
text:
Indigo airlines is one of the few Indian based low budget airlines that fly internationally. As a Dubai based resident, I frequently travel to and fro to India via Indigo. Recently, I ended up getting a pretty good return deal for 600Dhs which led to my unplanned travel to India for few days. But was it worth it? Here's my take: 

Horrible feels a small word to describe this flight experience overall. 

DELAYS - We faced delays on both our flights while take off from Dubai it was delayed for a good hour or more. Even though the pilot covered up for the lost time, we weren't allowed to land on reaching Mumbai as the airport officials told us to circle the airport for 45 mins! 
While coming back from Mumbai was the same story and that just peaked my frustration to another level after been delayed for 1 hr 30 mins. We were told the flight is not getting clearance from traffic control at the airport.  And obviously we landed later than our landing time. 

EARLY BOARDING - For a flight supposed to take off at 11:30am, a final call at 10:20am is too early which is why the delay seemed even longer! 

HAND LUGGAGE NOT ALLOWED - This is the first I had ever seen, on the flight from Dubai we were not allowed to take our hand luggage because apparently the overhead compartments were full. 25 other hand baggage like ours were sent with the check in baggage. First of all, overheads can't get technically that full as each passenger is allowed a 7kg bag with specified measurements and the overheads are made accommodating that. So when I sat, I was shocked to see 70% of compartments still empty. Can the airlines please explain the motive of such an unnecessary action? 

NO ENTERTAINMENT- While a frequent flyer in all sorts of flights, from luxurious to lower budget ones, I obviously get it this is why indiGo is a low budget airline. But when you are hauled up for 2 extra hours for a 2 and a half flight, without individual tv screens or even audio for that matter but rather the noise of kids screaming & fellow passengers voicing their frustration, one cannot sleep peacefully or do anything for that matter. Only form of entertainment I had was the  6E magazine, Sunderella story & the brain games on my sandwich box!!!! 

NOT ACCEPTING INDIAN CURRENCY - Why on earth is an Indian based flight not accepting Indian currency? Apparently, they only accept dollars or dirhams. So well if you don't have either these currencies, die of hunger people because they don't provide free meals either! 

NO MEALS - Ok again I know low budget, but seriously if you don't want to accept Indian currency and delay your flight to such an extent, a complimentary meal or snack wouldn't hurt right? 

My solution to the delay is that if so many flights were queued up before 6E 61, they should have informed the passengers way in advance about possible delay. So at least we could have not boarded and sat in the plane for 5 hours! 
While flying every minute is precious, 2 hours of delay is not worth the low flight rates of indigo. I'd rather pay more for a higher quality flight which atleast has some entertainment to keep passengers busy, oh and sorry meal included as well. NEVER EVER FLYING INDIGO! I want compensation for my flight!!!

title: Good flight
text:
Five of us flew from Delhi to Kochi.  When we checked in at the self serve terminal at Delhi airport we managed to get five seats in a row.  Bag drop was very busy and we were queuing past the sign that said '8 minutes from here'.  I thought to myself "and all the rest" but check-in staff were efficient and we didn't have to wait long to drop off our bags.

Leg room is about average, which is what you would expect with a 'no frills' airline.  Food not included but you can purchase on the plane.  The sandwich and veg biryani we bought were a good price and very tasty.  You can also buy small tins of biscuits for ₹50, which are nice and the tins come in use too.  Service from the cabin crew was good and friendly.

Despite the 3.5 hours flight, we arrived relaxed and refreshed for the car journey ahead.  I'm travelling with Indigo to Jaipur next week so hope the experience is as good as this one.

Anyway the check in was so chaotic, mess and for passengers like me who come from as far as away as Mysore but in time it was such an unpleasant experience. I kept calling for an Indigo staff to manage the mess no one turned up. Then one smart aleck staff who passed by when I said can you see not the mess around, can you now do something and showed him checked in passengers elderly and children having to negotiate luggage and luggage trollies and so on and when I told him it is a mess, he responded saying "may be"!. 
I thought instead of being helpful and clearing the mess he was being over smart and teaching me english. In my opinion he should be sacked, does not belong to any service industry leave alone an airline. At the boarding gate I told the staff at the gate my experience and said I want to talk to a senior Indigo staff. No one turned up. What it all told me while Indigo may be very impressive in terms of punctuality, cleanliness and costs, keep in mind that in an emergency situation they may not be the airline to trust. title: No care for elderly people
text: My parents Mr and Mrs. Kejriwal both around 75 years travelled by indigo on 1st October, 2016 from Kolkata to Hyderabad. Around 3 days earlier than the travel date I had requested airline to provide assistance in checking and boarding in the aircraft since they are elderly people although no wheel chair were required. We visited the indigo counter at 6.30 PM and requested the lady to provide the assistance to elderly people. She called her office and asked us to wait outside. We waited till 7 pm but no one turned up in spite of our repeated request made in the counter. Finally both my parents had to go themselves ( since check in counter closes at 7.25 pm)  and did check in and boarded the flight without any assistance provided by the airline. At around 7.15 once they entered in the airport I visited again at the counter and asked the lady what went wrong. Then one service person whose name is Mr Subodh came and told the lady in the counter that he was waiting at GATE 2A where as we were asked by the counter lady to wait at gate 3B. I think the airline has to relook and revisit the way they are providing service to elderly people and INDIGO MANAGEMENT has to think seriously whether they are at all interested in providing service to elderly people or its just name sake. We do not mind paying any charge if any levied by the airline for such service but how we can depend on this type of service when we send our elderly parents on the belief that they will be taken care by the airline inside the airport without any hassle. I am very much dis-appointed the service quality of indigo and that man subodh should be immediately thrown out from the system.

title: Indigo - Best Indian Airline
text:
I have flown Indigo extensively over the years and have always had good service with Indigo. 

They have well maintained airbus A320-200 aircraft which are maintained in tip-top shape. Their ground staff are very polite and so are the crew members on board. The pilots are more chatty than other airlines i have flown and that to me is very important! I also prefer flying the A320 rather than Boeing 737 which is used by Spicejet and JA. 

They also have access to aero-bridges in most top airports so that is one less hassle of getting into an overcrowded bus and roaming around all over the airport in search of the aircraft, which is an ordeal we typically endure with Spicejet and Jet Airways, although, this could just be down to the fact that they have a lot more ATR-72 and Bombardier Dash-8 aircraft which cannot really use the bridge. 

Booking a ticket on the Indigo website is an absolute breeze and so is the web check-in, where you can just print your boarding pass and proceed for security check with hand baggage, or use the baggage drop off at the counter. 

I am a bit surprised that Indigo is not offering business class on their airline, guess its all down to being fit into the LCC mold though. Still, it would be better to get the right configuration on their newer aircraft with a section used for Business class. Seeing as all their morning flights go full always, i guess they are not too concerned about the Business class folks as they are probably making more money of the additional seats anyhow.

The only one grouse i had was with regard to the food which is quite over-priced and could do with a revision in my opinion.

All in all, i would not hesitate in recommending Indigo as the best LCC in India, and indeed one of the best airlines in India.

I was allotted seat 5C, and one would normally expect that at least, on front rows the staple breakfast items would not get exhausted so fast.After repeatedly requesting to try with other stewards, finally I could manage to get Veg sandwich.A little while later, when I wanted to use the front toilet, I was rudely asked to walk all the way down (from 5C) to use the rear toilet,as the front toilet was blocked for a long time for use by the crew, exclusively. So much for the concern for guests vs crew.As if this was not enough, later when I purchased an item from sky merchandise, I was asked to pay Rs 10 extra, that I paid readily, presuming it to be the handling cost. But later, I when I asked for a suggestion  card, to record my harrowing experience so far ( not about extra charge!), I was surprised when the hostess sheepishly returned the extra Rs 10 collected , although a receipt was already given by her, including the extra amount. It took a while for her to locate the feedback card, and she kept on asking whether my experience was good, thereby raising a doubt whether the card will be delivered actually to the person concerned!I could have put up with all had the flight reached on time, that is touted as the USP of this Airlines. title: My first flight of fantasy
text:
I was born and brought-up in the tribal-belt of Orissa. As a child, like any other kid I too had child-hood fantasies of cars, trains and aeroplanes. In my tender age, many nights in the sleep I dreamt of elevating from bed and flying in the sky as if a Superman. But it was not until the year 1983 on my 7th Standard in school, I had the first glimpse of a flight at Kolkata. Till recently journey by a flight was considered to be a way of luxury and out of reach for any common Indian.

In September ’10 I had been to New Delhi. On my return journey I opted to take a flight to Bhubaneswar instead of a superfast train on the pretext that I had never before travelled in a flight in this life of mine. More to it, it is highly affordable when you could plan it well in advance. As a ritual at New Delhi every day my younger brother Karun started giving me tips on how to take a flight journey, as he himself is a frequent air-traveller. I started getting impatient as the days neared by for my return journey. The night before schedule departure I was in a state of euphoria. As a result of which I was sleepless till one past midnight, whereas I had to wake-up by 4.30 AM to get prepared for my Bahuda Jatra (return journey).

I had my return journey by Indigo in Flight # 6E-257 on 15th September 2010 early morning from Indira Gandhi International Airport (IGIA). It was scheduled to be departed at 7.30 AM. I was instructed to report at the check-in counter two hours before the schedule departure. I reached the airport lobby on the wee hours at around 5.30 AM. The whole area was glittering with neon-lights as if day time. So much illumination made me even more nervous. I was instructed by my brother to reach the counter of the Indigo Air and the rest they will manage. As I reached the counter of Indigo the lady officer greeted me with a smile. She asked for the ticket and the ID proof. After weighing the luggage she asked me politely to deposit Rs.500 for the overweight. She handed over the boarding pass. I learnt the valuable lesion to travel light whenever you take a journey by a flight. Thank God my mother was not accompanied with me. Had she been there my luggage charges would have been more than the ticket cost.

I was directed to reach Terminal # 20 for which I had to take an escalator. I went to the gate and waited. Soon after other co-passengers gathered one after another. There were two European tourists as well. All those people were aristocratic and wearing blazers and boots, where as I was wearing a cotton shirt, denim trousers but with sleepers on my feet as a “gaon ka Govinda”. I recalled, this could be the reason why my mother was particularly asked me to buy a new pair of boots on this trip of mine to New Delhi.

By 7.00 AM a transit bus picked us all to drop near the Indigo flight. In the bus I found a co-passenger in a low spirit and deeply engrossed in thoughts. In Oriya I greeted him “Namaskar Agyan” as it was a Bhubaneswar bound flight. He forcibly smiled, but kept quiet. I questioned if everything is fine. He said he is rushing to Bhubaneswar to stand by the side of his mother, as the previous day his father passed into comma. All I could do was to express my concern to him, just by placing my hand on his shoulder. In sharp contrast to the popular believe I realised that, these airline carriers are not just the luxury mode of transport, but they do deliver hope, aspirations, care and concern to the loved ones on time.

With the help of a ladder I stepped inside the flight. At the gate I was greeted by an air hostess. I was amazed to find her speaking in the regional Indian languages. It assured me, neither one need to know English nor need to wear a pair of boots to board a flight. She escorted me to the seat number 8D. I was disheartened to find it to be the centre chair far away from the window. I was dissatisfied with self for my maiden venture as I won’t be able to see the hemisphere and the earth below me when the flight takes off. I greeted my other two co-passengers with a smile to accommodate myself in the chair.

I just thought to be introduced to the Parthasarathi of my flight, as my safety is in his hands. I went to the cockpit. I expressed my good intension to the air-hostess. Without any suspicion she opened the doors of the cockpit. I greeted the pilots saying, you have to make me reach home safely as my mother would be waiting. The co-pilot said, just be assured all the life we are doing it un-failingly. I returned to my seat with a light-heart. Soon they announced the flight is about to take-off and to switch-off the cell phones, laptops and all other electronic equipments. They announced to fasten the seat belts. By observing my side-seater though I able to pullout the belts, but could not lock it. For a while I was hanged in the jumble game. My puzzled state of affair soon caught the attention of a tall air-hostess, and she came to my rescue.

They announced that the flight is about to takeoff. By keeping alive my orthodox personal beliefs, I prayed to my lord while shutting my eyes and folding both the hands. Engine started and the flight moved ahead. In seconds it accelerated to a greater speed and took off the ground. I sensed everything went smoothly. After takeoff it made a sharp L-turn. Then they announced to unlock the seat belts.

Now it was time for me to start lobbying. I expressed my desire to the neighbour about my eagerness to sit near the window as it’s my first journey by a flight. He wanted to laugh at this thought of mine, but vacated his seat quietly to keep alive his self-dignity. Now I occupied the window seat just a row ahead of the right-wing of the aeroplane. I could see the powerful engine on its wing which was pulling us ahead. By now flight elevated above the clouds. Entire life I had seen the clouds above me in the sky, but now for the first time in life I saw clouds below me.

“aaj mei uppar asman niche ……….”

To my disbelieve I heard that I am flying at a pace of 850 kmph and at a height of 35,000 feet above the ground level, which is much higher than the summit of Mt.Everest.

Than there came another airhostess with a cart load of breakfast. I got a pack of sandwich with fruit drink. It was wrapped in an eco-friendly paper. While eating my breakfast I read the beautiful love-story of Sahjade Salim and his lover Anarkali printed on this packet. It reminded me of my yester years of love life, even while at that moment I was moving ahead of time.

By 9.30 AM my flight landed safely at Biju Pattnaik Airport in Bhubaneswar. Every passenger got up to lift their hand bags from the cup-board and moved towards the gate. But I was sitting there still near the window while the seatbelt was tied onto my waist. That tall air hostess came back to ask if I need any help to unlock the belt.

But I said, no let me be tied to this seat ……..

My Son & Daughter (aged 13 & 9) (BOOKING REF NO: RCIQYT) recently took a flight from DXB to CCJ. While booking, I had checked the website for any possibility to make a booking as unaccompanied Minor, but as my son was above age limit, But no option as my son is with her.
They didn’t have any problem while traveling to Kozhikode. On their return trip to Dubai, I had called to enquire about the drop-in procedures about my children from Kozhikode and the call center informed me about the payment for unaccompanied minor service for my daughter even though my son will be accompanied with Indigo staff. I spend half an hour talking to him and finally he agreed to write a comment in the system regarding this matter without any payment for the service.We had re-confirmed the same from the airport regarding this (Me and Wife flew back a week before). But surprisingly when my father-in-law went to drop the children at the Indigo office, the staff insisted to pay Rs3000 for unaccompanied minor service for my daughter. I talked to the person from Dubai for at least 20 minutes to make him understand but was in vein. The superior, Lady who is in charge was very rude and even after paying the money they asked my Father-in-law to go and stand in the queue for the check-in procedures and when he strongly resisted, they took my children for check-in. My children from the age of 5 had started travelling as unaccompanied minor in Air-India and Emirates Airlines and we haven’t faced such a pathetic situation like this. If you have a policy about the services of unaccompanied minors, you should have informed and included the money while booking itself and moreover your staff should know how to behave towards an elderly man.
The net result is: - 
1)	I ended up paying extra for unaccompanied minor service. (which will not be paid to me by my company as it is was not included while purchasing the ticket).
2)	An elderly man had to face rude treatment from your staff.
3)	Wastage of time and money (STD & ISD calls) with a lot of stress.

title: 2 hours to collect baggage from Chennai airport
text:
Flew from Singapore to Chennai with family on 2nd July 2016. Everything was some sort good except the most horrible terrible experience ever of collecting our baggage in Chennai Airport!!! 
Till today we (passengers of Indigo flight 6E54) do not know what actually went wrong to release our baggage. It was just our flight (Indigo Airlines) baggage! Other flights which landed even more later then us collected their baggage and left. And we waited for almost 2 hours just for our luggage. 
There were NO announcement made for the delay, NO screen indication to which belt to collect our baggage from. Those Indigo staff on duty made us run from each belt to another belt with false information! Felt like an idiot running from one belt to another! 
Really felt pity for those who missed their connecting flights. Pity to see those with small kids and elderly people. And of course there are not chairs to be seated and wait for our luggage at the baggage collecting area. We felt totally helpless there!
The issue now is, it was NOT just a 10 mins or even 30 mins delay to just ignore it, the delay was almost 2 hours just for the baggage collection! And IF really there were any technical delay, why didn't the Indigo staff on duty made an proper announcement??? We are not expecting 1st class service here but just an proper on time announcement for the delay due to what reason, and not making an announcement 2 hours later after everyone have collected our baggage!!!

title: Always on time, smart, and 6E
text:
I have travelled with Indigo several times in the last 3-4 years. In fact, almost every time I have travelled, it has invariably been with Indigo. My travel has mostly been between Bangalore-Delhi, occasionally going to Raipur via Hyderabad.

The reason why I prefer Indigo are many.
1. The staff is always pleasant
2. Their planes are always clean
3. They are almost always on time
4. Their ticketing and boarding pass service is efficient (though this is pretty much the same with other airlines too)
4. Their use of language in advertising is quite interesting, with use of lots of puns (I love languages, so I have a natural inclination to such things). They even have smart one-liners written on the airstairs
5. Their in-flight meals come with attractive packaging, with smart catch lines, and there is a wide range of choice for both vegetarians and non-vegetarians. I jut wish they could substitute their standard Manchow soup with something tomato or corn based.
6. Their in-magazines make for interesting reads, always. The best part is, they always have a staff member featured on the magazine cover, and another staff member profiled inside. I haven't seen this with any other airline anywhere else.

In short, Indigo has kept things smart, simple and predictable.

text:

However, it just serves the minimum necessity for your travel. If you are someone who enjoys luxury travel, I fear you won't enjoy your travel with Indigo. For example, they have very few lounges in India (Bangalore, Delhi & Hyderabad), some basic (but necessary for some people) facilities like cotton buds, chair pillows aren't available in-flight.

Also, Indigo does not have a frequent flyer program. So if you are fly frequently especially along the same route and if you have options of flying with airlines offering this service, do weight your options before you opt in.

title: Too Many Stop Overs
text:
This must be one of the longest trips I have done in a while.
The direct flight from Singapore to New Delhi is normally just 5 and a half hours but I reached Delhi after 12 long hours of travel that took me to Chennai (first stop over) and Coimbatore india(2nd stop over) before reaching Delhi.
When I bought my cheap tickets from Air Indigo for only C$275 I thought I scored a bargain since most flights from Singapore to Delhi would cost no less than C$450.
I knew there was going to be a stop over in Chennai but I was not prepared for the long 2 hour layover that would prove to be cumbersome for me.

This is a rainy day stop over in Chennai where I alighted to take my connecting flight to Delhi.The flight from Singapore to Chennai took four hours but I had to wait another 2 hours for my connecting flight.

I had no idea  that my Delhi flight was going to have a stop over in Coimbatore .What? I had to ask my seatmate twice where we are headed to since I can't seem to pronounce the name right. Coimbatore is a city in India. It is the second largest metropolitan city after Chennai in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu.This I found out only after I reached Delhi and inquired about it from my Delhi hotel.

After a mere 36 minutes flight to Coimbatore I thought there were passengers that will get off and some waiting but I guess I was wrong since everyone alighted and I was the only one left inside the plane. We waited for another 45 minutes for the plane to be cleaned and vacuumed.

The stewardesses were at the galley taking their food when I asked them again where we are.I still can't get the name of this place right.

After an exhausting wait inside the plane, we finally took off after waiting for almost an hour. By this time I was in transit for almost 7 and a half hours.
I checked with the stewardesses again if there will be anymore stop overs and luckily she said we are flying direct to Delhi.

Arriving at Delhi after an exhausting 3 hours 30 minutes I was prepared for anything . It was therefore a relief to see a nicer looking airport compared to Chennai.

title: Pathetic Staff and Pathetic customer service
text: Apparently powerbanks are not allowed in checkin baggages. Indigo staff took out my powerbank at Delhi airport and gave me a number so that I can send someone to airport and collect it. Sent my colleague the very next day and when he called them, the staff said he is unable to find the powerbank. I gave him all the details even with the picture of the powerbank, he couldn't find it. I called him after one hour and asked how many powerbanks he has. He said around 50-60. I asked him, in an inquisitive tone, he is unable to find a powerbank with all the info in one hour in a bunch of 50-60. He said "Sir aap aakar dhund lo". Lodged a complaint with their appellate authority asking for delivering the powerbank now at home because I had already sent my colleague earlier at the airport to collect it. After some regular melodrama of their superficial regret and apology, when I asked do they even accept that they made a mistake. They said, sir we couldn't establish the fact that you sent someone to the airport to collect it. I offered them all the required evidence they need to establish the fact. To which their response was, "sir we are not saying you are lying but we can't take responsibility for this"? WOW. And to add to that, they now want me to send someone to delhi airport again because they can't deliver it as it was not their "fault". Why not change your motto to "with low fares comes no customer service".

title: Most harrowing experience at Delhi Check in and insensitive staff
text:
I was returning back from a trek and was not the most organised in packing my check in bags. After a long serpentine queue, as web check in doesn't give you seats, I am left with no option but to check in at the airport; when I got my turn, I was asked " Do you have a power bank in your check in bag?". I said, yes and I was asked to remove it and put it in my hand bag.

I tried to argue that I have just flown in from Dehradun to Delhi via Jet with same check in bags and I wasn't asked to remove the "power bank" so it is definitely not a rule. She didn't care. 

I tried to argue that i am returning back from a trek and don't remember where have I stowed my power bank, she didn't care.

I was instructed to stand/sit on one side, unpack all my bags and remove power bank  or miss my flight. Other IndiGo staff, unperturbed by my plight was happy to step on me, my luggage and didn't care a bit.

On my last attempt to argue, I told the girl that it is not announced or written anywhere that I can't carry power bank in check in bags, she looked at me with pity extended to a moron and said - YOU WANT US TO ANNOUNCE THAT? THOSE ARE OUR RULES.

I managed one small smile from her, when I said, "I know you are not responsible, atleast give your management feedback".

I vowed not to travel IndiGo in future unless it is most competitively priced.
