title: Ontime, Consistent, Efficient & Excellent Coverage
text:
Indigo airline has 3 major advantages for India. A country that is full of variables and last minute hiccups - 
1. Ontime - It is mostly on time. Airlines ofcourse cannot be Ontime 100% because of various uncontrollable factors such as weather, this airline keeps itself on its toes. So much so, that they are mostly the only ones operating during thick Winter fog months of the north. Only airline to trust during that period. Flipside for Travelers is that they are very stingy about not reporting on time for Checkin and do not overly callout for passengers if they re missing for boarding. Be unalert at your own Peril.
2. Efficient - Everything is excellently system driven, solutions are quick and therefore are able to remain consistently OnTime and excellent safety. However, this makes them cold and staff usually cannot take more human calls. So, do not over pack, keep fragile items or such, they are stingy on rules. And they do this everytime. 
3. Coverage - They fly everywhere to everywhere. if not direct, some hopping connection which does not require changing aircrafts. Good return connections for a day. 

Cons - 
1. Charge an arm and a leg for excess baggage, cancellations and any changes. Be very sure when you book what you'll do with them. Dont carry anything additional and dont change your mind. 
2. VERY SMALL LEGROOM. I am a 6 footer so very difficult for me. Seat checkin in advance for window and aisle is charged too which is quite ridiculous. 
3. Food is healthy and average. Nothing to brag about. Decent sandwiches but dont expect anything gourmet. 

All in all Everything feels so cold. from people to food to service. But its efficient ontime. I  think thats the price one has to pay for efficiency. But then theres no loyalty too.

title: On-time, good service - that's pocket friendly
text:
I have always been a fan of Indigo Airlines for their efficient  and pocket-friendly flight services right since the year 2007. Most of their flights are on time, they have a large-ly well-mannered and polite crew (ground as well as sky team), all their planes are Airbus A 320s or similar new ones with fuel efficient engines. They have 30 rows each bearing 6 seats - so that's a 3 x 3 format in a single economy class for all their planes. Makes it quicker to locate your seats :). The planes and toilets are clean. The seats are comfortable for small statured folks (5' 10") - cramped for others. Overhead cabin storage is quite limited. Being a budget airline complimentary meals are not served. They provide free water. Additional leg-room seats, pre-fixed meals (about 30 odd choices - hot and cold, veg and non-veg),cancellations and re-scheduling of seats are all possible at additional costs.
For domestic Indian flights they allow - 15 kg check-in and 7 kg hand baggage free. Anything more is charged. There is absolutely NO in-flight entertainment
In the past - 9 years - there were just a few incidents like assigned seats for my folks being given to some-one else with an argumentative check-in staff including their super (this was for a flight to Bangkok), . Other -wise most trips were hassle-free and pleasant.

title: Inconsistent baggage Rules
text: I flew Indigo for a to and fro trip from Bangalore to Pune in the same week in the month of Jun 16. I had a cabin size suit case and a laptop back pack with in the weighing limits. When I flew from Bangalore to Pune, I could carry both of them along with me in to the aircraft. Did not check in the suit case. After 3 days, I took the return flight from Pune to Bangalore. I approached the check in counter. I was told that I cannot carry 2 bags and I had to check in. I told them that I carried both on my onward journey from Blr to Pune. Why is there an inconsistency in the rules. They did not give me any satisfactory answer but insisted me to check-in the sui case which I did. Later, during boarding I observed that there were atleast 20 passengers who were carrying 2 bags in to the aircraft. I immediately questioned Indigo personnel (the lady who attended to me during check-in was part of the personnel at the gate) as to why they allowed 2 bags for some of the passengers. They could not give a satisfactory answer, saying that few are exception cases. Their body language and attitude also were rude. I am very disappointed with the inconsistent baggage rules and Indigo personnel

title: Value for money !
text:

The cabin space is okay, the attendants are well groomed, professional, helpful and pleasant. They serve with pleasure and are caring. The food served (I had to buy one  - veg), was hot, aromatic, of good quality and enough quantity. 

The check in process is easy and their guidance is appropriate. They even followup properly, if you get late in boarding after checking in, or if you are still in queue while the plane is ready to board. They try to expedite, and are quite effective and efficient. It's an excellent experience flying with them !
Overall : 

Timeline adherence - 10/10 (99.99% of times)
Checking counters - 9/10
Carrier quality and cleanliness - 9/10
Food quality and quantity - 9/10
Attendants - 9.5/10

Recommended for flying again !!

title: On time, but dubious & poor customer service
text: I have flown in Indigo quiet a number of times. But this flight to Kolkata was an harrowing experience. The flight was scheduled for 5:35AM and I was supposed to be at the gate 25 mins before. By 4:35 AM I was at the Security Check and my name was called by an Indigo staff. I told him will be there in the gate in a few minutes. He went off, as if, to inform the staff at the gate. When I finished the security check it was 4:50 AM. Considering that I still have 45 minutes, I went to the gate only to find that it is closed, though its 40 minutes before the departure time. Despite my plea and arguments, I was denied entry to the flight and have to get back to the ticket counter to get a new ticket issued for the next flight. I have been marked as "no-show" for the original flight and charged an additional 3K for the next flight. I saw two more guys in the counter with a similar issue. Considering they were there before me, I was wondering what time the gate closed. Further to my disappointment, I see that it does not come with breakfast, though my original ticket came with that. Someway reached Kolkata hungry, disgusted, angry, frustrated, annoyed etc. Will never use Indigo again.

title: Professional, Efficient, On Time - What every other airline needs to be
text:
Flying Indigo is a pleasure for the sheer experience of it. From the check-in, baggage handling, boarding to in-flight, arrival and baggage collection - the whole process is neat, hassle-free, works like a charm, and never fails.

The staff is really well groomed, understand their roles and behave at all times in a manner that is utmost professional. 

The processes and systems are well built and ensure that your baggage is handled well, the flight is ready and leaves on time (to arrive on time too). 

The in-flight performance is also great, with the staff handling the trip really well. 

It is also evident beyond a doubt, that this airline respects and values its employees. For instance where else would you find airline employees being published like celebrity STARS in an airline's inflight magazine. Indigo does it routinely, making its star performing employees popular amongst its fliers. And you have to take notice that its not just their pilots or host/hostesses that find a mention, this airline applauds its support staff like the cabin cleaners too. That is indeed commendable. Imagine the kind of pride and dignity each personnel would be carrying at work, and it sure would rub onto extremely pleasant experiences for the flyers.

Indigo also was the first to introduce a lot of things in its no-frills economy flights - be it the unique cookie-tins, the quirky stories printed on the sandwich covers, the unique food menu and much more. 

When flying within India, especially from North India, you must experience Indigo. It surely is what every other airline in India needs to be, but sadly isn't.

title: Nice enough, but.....
text:
It was an early morning flight on a Sunday, and it was fairly routine, until the third next to my husband was occupied by a man in his late thirties, or early forties. I was in 11A, my husband in 11B and this man was in 11C.

As the cabin crew were getting ready to takeoff, and they went through the usual spiel, we switched off our mobiles and tablet, as most sensible people would do.
Yet this guy had two smart phones, and kept on checking social sites and chatting, deaf to the crew's  request, even after my husband too started to advise him to turn it off.  When I drew the attention of one of the cabin crew, she just blithely dismissed it, signalling that it was okay, to my utter shock ! 

So then why ask everyone else to switch off mobiles if it was okay for one moron to not comply with it? Should we all just shrug off those warnings and requests to turn off our electronic devices, or was this crew member just too lazy? You be the judge.

A very interesting aspect of IndiGo's operation, especially given some of India's social problems, is that the inflight magazine featured a recruiting drive for cabin crew, with only ladies being eligible.  The ones who do get through are very sparky indeed, although interestingly two of the Delhi-based crew who took me to Dimapur admitted that their mothers were worried that they were spending even 30 minutes in Nagaland, one of the 'seven sisters' states tucked beyond Bangladesh.

It was on an earlier flight that one of the crew gave me her 'Girl Power' badge, which features in one of my photographs.

I am always happy to use IndiGo when I am in India.

title: Unethical practices
text: I was returning from my vacation in Guwahati to New Delhi to catch my flight back to US. While booking the ticket I had pre-booked a non-veg meal. It was a late afternoon flight, and these days with so much of security, etc. a passenger has to turn up quite early in the airport. So, I had thought that pre-booking a meal would at least allow me to have a late lunch during flight. When cabin crew started serving meals, I observed that they gave preference to customers who are buying meals by paying cash in-flight. This is because pre-booked meals are Twentyfive rupees cheaper than that sold in-flight. So, they changed their industry good practice of serving pre-booked meals first in the hope of making some petty gains. As a result, the cabin crew came to me at the last and told me that all meals are over. Since my meal is pre-booked, I can have some cookies and juice. I need not say how angry and cheated I felt at this. At that point I really felt ashamed about our Indian corporate culture. I leave it to the readers of this blog to comment on my indignation and feeling of humiliation. To end my post - I did NOT take any meals and just thanked the crew for at least remembering that I had paid in advance. After the flight landed in New Delhi, and I had stepped out on to the disembarkation ladder, one cabin crew ran after me mumbling some apologies - I told her that now it is too late to talk on the subject.

title: On time but impersonal and uncomfortable journies
text:
The USP of this airlines is the sheer no. of daily services offered and reach, mostly being on time it is a favorite of the business traveler. This is where the good part sadly ends. Issues with the services offered by the airlines far outweighs positives, some of them are:
1. Highly impersonal service, in the quest to maintain on time schedule passengers are harassed, there have been several instances where boarding starts even before the plane is serviced. Crew behavior at most best be termed as decent. In short this airlines has all but taken away the charm of air travel.
2. Low cost model has been taken too far, with the paid menu options being minimal, no in flight magazine on offer etc. This is irritating specially given all other low cot airlines in India are offering the same.
3. Customer comfort is lowest priority for this airlines, this fact is apparent given the seats on offer which can best be described as benches with minimal possible padding. It is impossible to survive a more than 2 hour flight on Indigo plane without a serious case of back ache
4. Low cost is just in name, in most sectors where there is competition you find cheaper options and on routes there the options are low prices offered by Indigo defy logic (the other day i was charged Rs. 15000/- for Patna Kolkata journey, this despite flight having less than 80% occupancy).

Fly Indigo only if you have to, it is a glorified on time bus service at best.

title: Completely avoid if with kids/infants
text:
There are various reasons you should not travel Indigo with infants/kids.
1. You cannot web check in since the infant is booked along with you on your ticket. Meaning you cannot select seats and would be forced to reach the airport early in order to get seats of your choice. Parents ideally would like to travel with children and sometimes select the last rows to avoid inconvenience to other fellow passengers. You cannot do anything about that.
2. The infant seat is placed in front, but even if you pay or get lucky in taking that seat, you cannot place your infant in the infant seat. Thats only for show. You will be taken to the rear.
3. If the infant/child is in the pram it can be taken on board with out any extra cost. If the pram can be folded its ok, otherwise it will be taken into the cargo and you will be charged for handling.
4. If the child is not in the pram you have to check it in. They charge Rs. 1000 per sector for infants and over and above that Rs. 1000 per sector for handling the pram. When I told them to treat it like other luggage and even though I was way below allowed weight, they wanted more money.
5. Milk only 100 ml can be taken. They do provide hot water, but the source and quality is something I need to look into. 100 ml is way to less for a longer flight and a hungry baby especially if you are going to reach the airport 1.5 hours before flight time, then spend 1 hour in the flight and an additional 1-1.5 hours from the airport to your home/hotel.
6. Carry all necessary documents to prove the age of the child. I had a birth certificate, but what I dont understand is - can't these guys make out the difference in a 5 yr old child and a 1 yr old baby. Why harass the passenger by asking him to bring all proof. 
Do yourselfa favour and your child, fly Jet Airways or Air India. Far better. Even many adults are complaining about the service of Indigo.
